7“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 8Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
9All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
11All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
12Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
13“I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
14Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
15Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
16 Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
17Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
18Micaiah replied:
I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 19The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 20then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
21“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
22Ahab, this is exactly what has happened. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
23Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
24Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
25Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 26Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
27Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(1 Kings 22.29-35)
28Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 29Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
30The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 31So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop. 32And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
33However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
34The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_text:
Mɩkaaya bʋl wɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa Ahab lɛ
1Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Jehosafat sɩ kʋ kɛŋ kɩaa woruŋ, nɩaa zizilu, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa mʋ mɛrɛ Iziral kuoro Ahab lɛ a leŋ ʋ nanʋala jaa Ahab tolo. 2Jɩsɩŋ baŋmɛnɛ harɩŋ, Jehosafat sii mʋ Samarɩa dɩ ʋ na Iziral kuoro Ahab. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ahab kpʋ piesee arɩ nɛsɩŋ yʋgɛ woruŋ a hʋɔrɛ ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩaa, aŋ yigu hɛ dɩ ʋ mʋ yuo taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ramɔf Gɩlɩad. 3Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral kuoro Ahab pɩɛsɛ Juda kuoro Jehosafat, “Ŋ jaŋ pɛ mɩ lɛ dɩ la mʋ yuo Ramɔf Gɩlɩad?” Jehosafat bʋla pɩ Iziral kuoro, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ, mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa ma kɛŋ la tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ. La jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ dɩ la mʋ yuo laal-la. 4Ama leŋ dɩ la laa sɩpaaŋ pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA na.”
5Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ahab yɩrɛ wʋnyɩɛrɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllaa zɔɔ-banɛsɛ a pɩɛsɛba, “Mɩ mʋ yuo Ramɔf Gɩlɩad koo mɩ sɩ́ mʋ?” Ba bʋl, “Mʋ yuou, Wɩa jaŋ joŋu hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.” 6Jehosafat bɩra pɩɛsɛ, “La TƖƖNA wʋlaabʋllʋ tuo daha dɩ la to ʋ lɛ a pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA naa?”
7Iziral kuoro Ahab bʋla pɩ Jehosafat, “Nʋʋ dɔŋ ha hɛ nɩmɛ la sɩ jaŋ wuo to ʋ lɛ a pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA na. Ʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Mɩkaaya, a ŋaa Imila nanʋala. Ama mɩ bɛrʋ nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ ha bɩ wʋzɔŋ kala bʋla pɩmɛ Wɩa doluŋ lɛ, see wʋbɔŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehosafat bʋl, “Kuoro, sɩ́ ŋɩɩ bʋl.”
8Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ahab yɩrɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ dɔŋɔ a bʋl, “Mʋ kɛŋ Imila nanʋala Mɩkaaya kɔ daha lɛɛlɛ.”
9Ka Iziral kuoro arɩ Juda kuoro Jehosafat kala laalɛ ba kuori gɛnnɩŋ a hɔŋ ba kuoru kpasɩnɩŋ lɛ taha-la sɩ kpagɛ Samarɩa taŋ-la boi-baalɩŋ niiŋ. Wʋnyɩɛrɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla-la chɩŋ ba sɩpaaŋ a bʋbʋl wɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa. 10Wʋnyɩɛrɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla-la dɔŋɔ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Zedikaaya, a ŋaa Kɛnaana nanʋala. Ʋ fa kɛŋ hɔɔŋ libi banyilliŋ nɛ, ʋ kaa heele bʋl, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Kɩaa deemba nɛ ŋ jaŋ kaa tɩɩgɛ Siiria tɩŋŋaa kala kpʋ.’ ” 11Wʋnyɩɛrɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla-la kʋkaanaa ma kala bʋl ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa. Ba sɩ, “Mʋ yuo Ramɔf Gɩlɩad, ŋ jaŋ yuo diiu, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA jaŋ joŋu hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”
12Nɩɩ-la ba sɩ tɩma dɩ ʋ yɩrɛ Mɩkaaya bʋla pʋ, “Na, Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla-la bʋl wʋbala nɛ. Ba sɩ, ‘Kuoro jaŋ yuo dii.’ Dɩ ŋ nɛ mʋa, ŋ ma chɩŋ ba kʋa lɛ a bʋl ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa.”
13Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mɩkaaya bʋl, “La TƖƖNA sɩ weye wɩaa, wɩɩ-la mɩ Wɩa sɩ bʋla, ʋ nɛ mɩ jaŋ bʋl.”
14Mɩkaaya sɩ kɔ, kuoro Ahab pɩɛsʋ, “La mʋ yuo taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ramɔf Gɩlɩad koo la sɩ́ mʋ?” Ʋ bʋl, “Má mʋ yuou. La TƖƖNA jaŋ joŋu hɛ ma nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”
15Kuoro Ahab bɩra pɩɛsʋ, “Naansɩɩŋ bʋŋmɛɛ nɛ maga dɩ mɩ leŋ dɩ ŋ ŋmɩɛsɛ aŋ bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ pɩmɛ La TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ?”
16Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mɩkaaya bʋl, “Mɩ na Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala dɩ ba pɩsa su dundolluŋ nyuŋ, a nagɛ piesee sɩ bɩ pie-daara kɛnɛ, ka La TƖƖNA bʋl, ‘Nɩaa deemba bɩ sɩpaalaarʋ kɛnɛ. Leŋ dɩ ba mɩɩra mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa.’ ”
17Kuoro Ahab bʋla pɩ Jehosafat, “Mɩ bɩ bʋla pɩŋ arɩ ʋ ha bɩ wʋzɔŋ kala sɩ jaŋ ŋaa bʋla pɩmɛ see wʋbɔŋ?”
18Mɩkaaya bɩra bʋl, “Má jegile nɩɩ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla: Mɩ na La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ hɔŋ ʋ kuoru kpasa nyuŋ, ka ʋ tɩndaaraa chɩŋ ʋ nadiiŋ arɩ ʋ nagʋa. 19Ka La TƖƖNA pɩɛsɛ, ‘Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ mʋ nyɩsɛ Iziral kuoro Ahab hɛ dɩ ʋ mʋ yuo Ramɔf Gɩlɩad tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba kpʋʋ nɩmɛ?’ Dɔnsʋŋ bʋl ŋ-la, dɔnsʋŋ ma bʋl wɩɩ dɔŋ. 20Ʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ, dɩma kʋbala kʋ lɩɩ chɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ a bʋl, ‘Mɩ jaŋ mʋ nyɩsʋ.’ La TƖƖNA pɩɛsʋ, ‘Ɛɛ nɛ ŋ jaŋ to?’ 21Dɩma-la bʋl, ‘Mɩ jaŋ joŋ wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ a hɛ ʋ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ bʋl wɩaa pʋpʋ niiŋ lɛ.’ La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋl, ‘Mʋ, ŋ jaŋ wuo nyɩsʋ.’ ”
22Mɩkaaya bʋl, “La TƖƖNA joŋ wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ dɩma hɛ nɩaa deemba sɩ bʋl wɩaa pɩpɩŋ niiŋ lɛ nɛ. La TƖƖNA tɩtɩa bʋla arɩ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ jaŋ jʋʋŋ.”
23Ŋɩɩ nɛ Zedikaaya sɩ ŋaa Kɛnaana nanʋala mʋ fallɛ Mɩkaaya, aŋ pɩɛsʋ, “Bʋa bɛɛ lɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA dɩma-la lɩɩ mɩ lɛ, a kɔ ŋ teeŋ a bʋl wɩaa pɩŋ?”
24Mɩkaaya bʋl, “Tapʋlɩɩ-la ŋ jaŋ kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa jʋʋ faa dɩa sɩpaaŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ.”
25Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Ahab bʋl, “Má kɛŋ Mɩkaaya mɩɩra mʋ taŋ nɩhɩaŋ Amɔŋ arɩ mɩ nanʋala Jʋas teeŋ. 26Má bʋla pɩba arɩ ba laaʋ tɔ bɩnɩŋ dɩa a pʋpʋ boroboro mʋa mʋa arɩ lɩɩŋ dʋndʋŋ a mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩ jaŋ mɩɩra kɔ arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa.”
Ba kpʋ Ahab Ramɔf Gɩlɩad lɛ
27Mɩkaaya bʋl, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ mɩɩra kɔ arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa, ŋɩɩ-na, La TƖƖNA dee bɩ mɩ lɛ to a bʋl wɩaa.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ bɩra bʋl, “Ma nɩaa deemba kala, má magɩlɛ wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ bʋla bil.” 28Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral kuoro arɩ Juda kuoro Jehosafat sii kɛŋ ba laalɩyuoroo mʋ dɩ ba yuo Ramɔf Gɩlɩad. 29Iziral kuoro bʋla pɩ Jehosafat, “Dɩ laalɩŋ nɛ suomo, mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa bɩrɩmɛ a jʋʋ laalɩŋ tʋɔŋ, ama ŋ-na laalɛ ŋ kuoru gɛnnɩŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral kuoro kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa bɩrɩmɛ a jʋʋ laal-la tʋɔŋ.
30Siiria kuoro fa bʋla pɩ ʋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba, “Má sɩ́ nʋʋkala yuo, see Iziral kuoro Ahab dʋndʋŋa.” 31Laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩ na Jehosafat, ba bɩɩnɛ a bʋl, “Iziral kuoro Ahab nɛ ŋ-la.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bɩrɩmɛ dɩ ba yuou. Ama Jehosafat ŋmoo niiŋ, La TƖƖNA Wɩa pɛ ʋ lɛ a kiriba ba mɩɩrɛ. 32Laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩ na dɩ Iziral kuoro dee, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba leŋu.
33Laal-la tʋɔŋ, laalɩyuoro-la dɔŋɔ yuo to-hɛmɩŋ bine, ʋ to Ahab laalɩyuori gɛrɩŋ pɛgɛ a jʋʋ kɛnʋ. Ʋ bʋla pɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ toruko vɩvɛŋ, “Mɩɩrɛ harɩŋ a kɛmmɛ lɩɩ laal-la tʋɔŋ, ba bolimimi nɛ.” 34Tapʋlɩɩ-la kala laalɩŋ hoso nɛ woruŋ, ka kuoro hɔnɔ tɩɛnɛ a yelli ʋ toruko-la a bibeŋ Siiria tɩmma-la a kaa mʋ yi dɩdaanɩŋ. Wɩɩ-muluŋ tuu jʋjʋʋ dɩ ʋ sʋba.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said:
By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you! 3But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord.
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
5He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah 6and told them:
Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide. 7So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
8Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem. 9He told them:
Faithfully serve the Lord! 10The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
11Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_text:
1Juda kuoro Jehosafat mɩɩra mʋ ʋ kuoru dɩa sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa. 2Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa sɩɩ-naara Jehu, Hanani nanʋala mʋ naʋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Ŋ bɩɩna ʋ maga dɩ ŋ pɛ nɩbɔmʋŋ lɛ, a kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɛrɛ La TƖƖNA bɩrɩmɛ ŋ sɩma nɛ koo? Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋ sɩ ŋaa leŋe La TƖƖNA na baanɩŋ nɛ ŋ nyuŋ. 3Ama arɩ ŋɩɩ kala, ŋ ha ŋaa wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ mʋa nɛ. Ŋ sɩ chei vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daasɩŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, aŋ kɛŋ ŋ tʋɔŋ a to Wɩa.”
Jehosafat lɩɩsɛ sarɩya diiree
4Jehosafat fa hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ nɛ, ama ʋ yie lɩɩ a gɔllɛ ʋ tinteeŋ kala, a chɩŋ Bɛɛsɩba lɛ a kaa mʋ yi Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ a bʋl wɩaa pɩ ʋ nɩaa dɩ ba bɩrɩmɛ a tuto La TƖƖNA, ba naabalɩmaba Wɩa. 5Ʋ fa lɩɩsɛ sarɩya diiree nɛ Juda tinteeŋ tabala-la kala lɛ ba sɩ saa kɛrɩsɩŋ golli. 6Ʋ bʋla pɩba, “Má fɩɛlɛ ma sɩaa a didii nɩaa sarɩya, bɛɛ wɩaa nuhuobiinee doluŋ dee ma kaa dii sarɩya-la, ama La TƖƖNA doluŋ nɛ. Ʋ jaŋ chɩŋ ma harɩŋ bʋa na-kala dɩ ma nɩɩ dii sarɩya. 7Má fá La TƖƖNA, a fɩɛlɛ ma sɩaa a didii sarɩya. La TƖƖNA Wɩa bɩ chɛ dɩ ma kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ bɩrɩmɛ, ʋ bɩ chɛ dɩ ma kɛŋ nɩaa kaa pɔrɛ koo a lɩlaa kpalaa nɩaa teeŋ.”
8Jerusalɛm ma lɛ, Jehosafat fa lɩɩsɛ Levi doho nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ nɛ dɩ ba dɩdagɛ La TƖƖNA wombiiŋ dɩ ba tuto, dɩ nɩaa nɛ kɛŋ kaalɛrɛ ma, dɩ ba bʋla wasɛ. 9Wɩaa deemba nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩba, “Ʋ maga dɩ ma fá La TƖƖNA a kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ arɩ tʋɔ-bala a tɩŋ ma tɩntɩŋŋaa. 10Dɩ ma taŋ nɩaa kʋŋ nɛ kɛŋ wɩɩkala kɔ ma teeŋ, dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ba kpʋ, koo wɩɩ-la tɩgɛ Wɩa wombiiŋ ʋ sɩ bile dɩ la tuto lɛ nɛ koo wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ daga lɛ nɛ koo Wɩa niiriŋ lɛ nɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ma bʋl wɩaa chagɩlɛba dɩ ba sɩ́ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaa La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Dɩ ŋɩɩ dee ʋ baanɩŋ jaŋ sii ma dɩ ma naambiiriŋ nyuŋ. Má ŋaa ŋɩɩ a sɩ́ wʋbɔŋ ŋaa. 11Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ Amarɩa nɛ jaŋ ŋaa ma nɩhɩaŋ wɩɩ na-kala sɩ mʋ tɩgɛ La TƖƖNA lɛ. Ka dɩ Ɩsɩmɛl nanʋala Zebadia sɩ ŋaa Juda doho nɩaa sɩpaalaara ma nɛ ŋaa ma nɩhɩaŋ wɩɩ na-kala sɩ mʋ tɩgɛ kuoro lɛ. Levi doho nɩaa ma nɛ jaŋ pɛ ma lɛ dɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ chɩŋ. Má kɛŋ bɔɩ-duoŋ a tɩŋ ma tɩntɩŋŋaa, La TƖƖNA jaŋ chɩŋ ma nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋaa woruŋ harɩŋ.”

english_text:
Moab and Ammon Are Defeated
1Some time later, the armies of Moab and Ammon, together with the Meunites, went to war against Jehoshaphat. 2Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
3Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow. 4They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
5After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard 6and prayed:
You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you. 7 Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever. 8Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you. 9They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
10 You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed. 11Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us. 12Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
13While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple, 14the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan. 15 Then Jahaziel said:
Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side! 16So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley. 17 You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
18Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord. 19Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
20Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.” 21Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing:
“Praise the Lord!
His love never ends.”
22As soon as they began singing, the Lord confused the enemy camp, 23so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
24When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground. 25So Jehoshaphat and his troops went into the camp to carry away everything of value. They found a large herd of livestock, a lot of equipment, clothes, and other valuable things. It took them three days to carry it all away, and there was still some left over.
26Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
27-28Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
29When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid 30to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace.
Jehoshaphat Dies
(1 Kings 22.41-50)
31Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, 33but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
34Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
35While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel. 36They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber. 37But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_text:
Jehosafat yuo dii Mʋab arɩ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa
1Bʋa kʋbala lɛ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa, Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa arɩ Mewuni tɩŋŋaa dɔnsʋŋ sii kɔ dɩ ba yuo Jehosafat. 2Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩaa kʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro Jehosafat, “Laalɩyuori-daŋ nɛ lɩɩ Ɛdɔm a to mʋgʋ-balɩŋ sɛmɛ kʋkɔ dɩ ba yuoŋ. Ba paala hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hazazɔŋ Tama lɛ.” (Ʋ nɛ ha Ɛŋ-Gedi.) 3Fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ Jehosafat, ʋ pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ na wɩɩ-la sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa, aŋ heele bʋla pɩ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa kala ba vɔɔ niiŋ. 4Juda nɩaa lɩɩ ba tasɩŋ kala a kʋ hilimi Jerusalɛm lɛ dɩ ba sʋl La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ pɛ ba lɛ.
5Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehosafat sii chɩŋ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ kʋ hilimi La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la kaalɩ-falɩɩ-la sɩpaaŋ, 6aŋ bʋl,
“La TƖƖNA, la naabalɩmaba Wɩa, ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ. Ŋ nɩɩ beŋ tinteyee kala sɩ hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ. Doluŋ kala hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ, nʋʋkala bɩ ŋ sɩpaaŋ wuo chɩŋ. 7La Wɩa, ŋ nɛ kiri tinteye-la nɩaa fa sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ ta ŋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ, aŋ joŋo pɩ ŋ nandɔŋɔ Abɩraham doho nɩaa dɩ ʋ ŋaa ba kʋŋ a kaa mʋ wuu. 8Ba hɔŋ tintee-la lɛ nɛ a saa ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ dɩ ba ziziliŋ nɩmɛ, aŋ bʋl, 9‘Dɩ wʋbɔŋ kala nɛ kʋ jʋʋla, dɩ laalɩŋ nɛ koo dɩ nyanyal-bɔŋ nɛ koo dɩ losuŋ nɛ, la jaŋ kɔ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ lɛ ba sɩɩ ziliŋ a chɩŋ ŋ sɩpaaŋ a yel la hɛɛŋ pɩŋ dɩ ŋ nɩɩ a laala ta.’
10Ama lɛɛlɛ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa, Mʋab tɩŋŋaa arɩ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa kʋʋ yuola nɛ. Ba tinteeŋ nɛ ŋ fa bʋla pɩ la naabalɩmaba dɩ ba sɩ́ jʋʋ ŋɩɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kieliba bal, ba bɩ ba cheye. 11Lɛɛlɛ, na ŋɩɩ ba sɩ joŋo ŋɩŋaa la lɛ, ba kɔ nɛ dɩ ba kirila ta tintee-la ŋ sɩ joŋo pɩla dɩ ʋ ŋaa la kʋŋ lɛ. 12Ŋ nɛ la Wɩa, dɔgɩsɛba, bɛɛ wɩaa la bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ dɩ la yuo laalɩyuori-daŋ deeŋ sɩ kʋʋ yuola. La-na bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la kala la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa, ama laa beŋ ŋ lɛ nɛ dɩ ŋ pɛ la lɛ.”
13Juda tɩŋŋaa baalaa arɩ ba haalaa arɩ ba biiriŋ kala fa chɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ nɛ.
14Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA Dɩma kʋ jʋʋ Jahazɩɛl sɩ ŋaa Zɛkarɩya nanʋala dɩ ʋ fa chɩŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hilime tʋɔŋ. Zɛkarɩya nyɩmma nɛ Bɛnaaya, Bɛnaaya ma nyɩmma nɛ Jɛyɛl, Jɛyɛl ma nyɩmma nɛ Matanɩa, a ŋaa Levi tɩɩna sɩ lɩɩ Asaf doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ. 15Ʋ bʋl, “Kuoro Jehosafat arɩ ma nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm lɛ, má jegili, wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pɩma nɛ ŋ-la, ‘Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ma bɔyɛ joŋ koo dɩ ma nandaasɩŋ yʋɔrɛ a tɩŋ laalɩyuori-daŋ-la wɩaa. Ma dee bɩ jaŋ yuo laal-la, ama Wɩa nɛ jaŋ yuo. 16Má chie lɩɩ tuu cheme yuoba. Ba jaŋ to Zɩs wombii-bie-la sɩ hɛ peelee tʋɔŋ a kʋʋ jɩl. Ma jaŋ naba fuonaa-la sɩ hɛ Jɛrʋɛl tintee-hɩlɩŋ dɩdɛrɩŋ. 17Ma dee bɩ jaŋ yuo laal-la, ma-na chɩŋ ma dɩchɩnaa, a gbɛrɛ na ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ jaŋ laama ta. Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm tɩmma, má sɩ́ fawʋllʋŋ fá, a sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ma nandaasɩŋ yʋɔrɛ. Má chie lɩɩ cheme yuoba, La TƖƖNA jaŋ chɩŋ ma harɩŋ.’ ”
18Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Jehosafat tuu kpirimi a kɛŋ ʋ sɩaa chu tinteeŋ, Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa ma kala tuu kpirimi a chʋɔlɛ La TƖƖNA. 19Levi doho nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ sɩ lɩɩ Kohaf arɩ Kora nyɩŋ-nɩaa tʋɔŋ sii chɩŋ a faasa ŋaa goŋ a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa. 20Taŋ sɩ pʋla chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla nɩalɩŋ sii mʋ Tɛkʋa tintee-hɩlɩŋ. Ba sɩ lɩa dɩ ba mʋ, Jehosafat sii chɩŋ aŋ bʋl, “Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm tɩmma, má jegili mɩ teeŋ, má laa ma TƖƖNA Wɩa dii, ʋ jaŋ chagɛma kɩɩ. Má laa wɩalɩŋ ʋ wʋlaabʋllaa sɩ bʋla dii dɩ ma wɩaa wasɛ.” 21Jehosafat sɩ bʋl wɩalɩŋ nɩalɩŋ teeŋ dɛrɛ, ʋ lɩɩsɛ nɩaa dɩ ba laa laalɩyuoro-la sɩpaaŋ a yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a pɩ La TƖƖNA, a dɛnnʋ a tɩŋ ʋ tʋla arɩ zɔmʋŋ wɩaa a bʋl,
“Má lɔllɛ La TƖƖNA,
ʋ chonuŋ bɩ dɛrɛ.”
22Ba sɩ suomo yɩɩ yɩɩla-la, La TƖƖNA kɛŋ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa, Mʋab tɩŋŋaa arɩ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoro-la sɩ kɔ dɩ ba yuo Juda wɩɩkala vʋgʋmɛ. 23Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa arɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa mɩɩra gʋra yuo Ɛdɔm laalɩyuoroo a kpʋ ba kala. Ba sɩ kpʋ Ɛdɔm nɩalɩŋ dɛrɛ, ba ma tɩtɩa gʋra kpʋ dɔŋɔ.
24Juda nɩaa sɩ kʋ yi lee-la ba sɩ jaŋ wuo chɩŋ aŋ bibeŋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la, ba na dɩ ba dʋndɔmɔ-la kala sʋba a pɩŋ, nɩbala ma bɩ foro fa. 25Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehosafat arɩ ʋ nɩaa sii mʋ dɩ ba paa nɩalɩŋ kɩaa. Ba sɩ mʋa, ba na laalɩyuori kʋ-daŋ nɛ a pɛ gɛnnɩŋ lɛ arɩ kɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ sɩ kɛŋ yuŋuŋ lɛ. Kɩalɩŋ fa yʋga kɩŋkɛŋ nɛ, ba joŋ tapʋlaa batori a paaba. 26Tapʋl nɛsɛ chɛɛŋ ba hilimi fuonaa kʋbala lɛ baa yɩrɛ Bɛraka a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA. Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ba kɛŋ fuonaa-la yɩyɩrɛ Bɛraka arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala. (Ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ ‘ŋ lɔlʋŋ’.) 27Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehosafat laa Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa kala sɩpaaŋ, ba jʋɔsɛ a mɩɩra kɔ Jerusalɛm, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA leŋe ba yuo dii ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ. 28Ba sɩ mʋ yi Jerusalɛm, ba du chenniŋ arɩ kɔnɛba a ŋmʋʋ banyilliŋ a mʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la. 29Tinteye-la kala sɩ golliba a nɩɩ ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA tɩtɩa sɩ yuo dii Iziral tɩŋŋaa dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ, fawʋllʋŋ kɛmba a tɩŋ Wɩa wɩaa. 30Jehosafat fa sɩɩ beŋ lee-la kala fɩɛla pɩŋ sɔm, bɛɛ wɩaa Wɩa pʋ wiese nɛ sɛmɛ kala.
Jehosafat kuoruŋ dɩdɛrɩŋ
31Jehosafat fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ banɔŋ nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ banɔŋ. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Azuba, a ŋaa Silihi tolo. 32Wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ nyɩmma Asa sɩ ŋaa, ba tɩtɩa nɛ ʋ ma ŋaa, ʋ bɩ kʋŋ kere ta. Ʋ fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ. 33Ama ʋ fa bɩ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa cheye, nɩalɩŋ fa ha bɩ ba tʋɔŋ kala joŋo hɛ ba naabalɩmaba Wɩa lɛ.
34Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Jehosafat sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, a chɩŋ dɩ-suomuŋ a kaa mʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Hanani nanʋala Jehu teniŋ tʋɔŋ a hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. 35Harɩŋ nɛ, Juda kuoro Jehosafat kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa mʋ mɛrɛ Iziral kuoro Ahazɩa lɛ. Ahazɩa fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ woruŋ. 36Ba pɛ niiŋ dɩ ba kpaasɛ lɩɩŋ daborusuŋ dɩ ba kaa mʋ bayalɩŋ Taasɩs lɛ. Ba sɩ kpaasa dɛrɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛzɩɔŋ Geba lɛ, 37Dodavahu nanʋala Elieza sɩ lɩɩ Marɛsa a ŋaa Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ bʋl wɩaa tɩgɛ Jehosafat lɛ a bʋl, “Ŋ sɩ kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa mʋ mɛrɛ Ahazɩa lɛ wɩaa, La TƖƖNA jaŋ chei kɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ lɩɩŋ daborusu-la yɛrɛ, ba bɩ wuo kaa mʋ bayalɩŋ Taasɩs lɛ.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Kings 8.16-24)
2King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. 3Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
4After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders. 5He was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled eight years from Jerusalem.
6Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong, 7 but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
8 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 9Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night, 10but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped. 11Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
12One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said:
I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather. 13Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
14Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own. 15You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
16The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram. 17They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
18After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease. 19About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
20Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_text:
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehosafat sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi Devit tabal-la lɛ ʋ naabalɩmaba tʋɔŋ. Ka ʋ nanʋala Jehoram dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ. 2Jehoram fa kɛŋ naambiiriŋ nɛ. Ba yɩraa nɛ: Azarɩa, Jɛhɩɛl, Zɛkarɩya, Azarɩahu, Maakɩl arɩ Sɛfatɩa. Ba kala fa ŋaa kuoro Jehosafat hambolibiisiŋ nɛ. 3Ba nyɩmma joŋ kʋ-daŋ nɛ pɩba, hɔpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ arɩ kɩaa dɔnsʋŋ sɩ kɛŋ yuŋuŋ, a pɛ Juda tinteeŋ tasɩ-la ba sɩ saa kɛrɛ golli lɛ. Ama ʋ fa lɩɩsɛ ʋ bii-hɩaŋ Jehoram nɛ ʋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.
Jehoram dii Juda tinteeŋ kuoruŋ
4Jehoram sɩ dii ʋ nyɩmma kuorii-la ʋ chɩŋ kpaŋkpaŋ a kɛŋ doluŋ, ʋ kpʋ ʋ naambiiri-la kala a pɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa dɔnsʋŋ lɛ. 5Jehoram fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ balɩa nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a beŋ Juda tinteeŋ jɩsɩŋ chori nɛ. 6Jehoram fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Ʋ ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la tɩtɩa Iziral kuoroo sɩ ŋaa nɛ a jaa Ahab tolo. Ŋɩɩ leŋ ʋ ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la tɩtɩa Ahab dɩa nɩaa fa sɩ ŋaa. 7Ama La TƖƖNA fa tɩŋ ʋ tɩntɩnna Devit wɩaa nɛ a bɩ Juda tinteeŋ cheye, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ fa hɛ niiŋ nɛ ʋ dɩ Devit pɛgɛ arɩ ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ʋ doho nɩaa nɛ didii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.
8Jehoram kuoruŋ bʋa lɛ, Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa fa vɩa dɩ ba to Juda tinteeŋ kuoro nɛ, aŋ ma bil ba kuoro. 9Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehoram sii kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba ba mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛdɔm. Nɩmɛ nɛ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa tɔ ʋ dɩ nɩhɩasɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba-la hɛ. Ama tɩtaŋɩŋ ʋ dɩ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba nɩhɩasɩ-la foro fá. 10Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa ha vɩa dɩ ba to Juda nɩaa nɛ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala. Bʋa-la tɩtɩa lɛ nɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lɩbɩna nɩaa ma vɩa dɩ ba to Juda kuoro Jehoram a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ vɩa La TƖƖNA, ba naabalɩmaba Wɩa.
11Ʋ fa saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa nɛ Juda dundolluŋ nyuŋ a leŋ Jerusalɛm arɩ Juda nɩaa kpaarɛ vʋɩyaa a yeŋŋi. 12Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla Ɩlaaja ŋmʋnsɛ teniŋ a pɩ Jehoram. Teŋ-la tʋɔŋ ʋ sɩ, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA, ŋ nyɩmma Devit Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la, ‘Ŋ bɩ ŋ nyɩmma Jehosafat koo ŋ naabalɩma Juda kuoro Asa naabʋɔsʋŋ to. 13Ama ŋ mɩɩra to Iziral kuoroo naabʋɔsʋŋ nɛ, a leŋ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa kpaarɛ vʋɩyaa a nagɛ Ahab arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Ŋ paala kpʋ ŋ naambiiriŋ nɛ, ŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ pɛ nyɩmma, nɩalɩŋ sɩ paala kpɩaŋ. 14A tɩŋ wɩaa deemba kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa, La TƖƖNA ka chɛ dɩ ʋ dɔgɩsɛ ŋ nɩaa, ŋ hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ŋ haalaa nɛ, a chei ŋ dʋa kala. 15Luoruŋ nyanyal-bɔŋ jaŋ kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa a dɔgʋsʋŋ ŋɩɩ deeŋ deeŋ dɩ ŋ luobiee lɩɩ.’ ” 16Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA yigi Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa arɩ Arab tɩmma-la sɩ hɔnɔ kpagɛ Kus tɩŋŋaa a hɛ Jehoram lɛ. 17Ba kʋ yuo Juda tinteeŋ a paa kʋzɔmɔ-la kala sɩ hɛ kuoru dɩa lɛ, aŋ kɛsɛ Jehoram hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ʋ haalaa kaa viiri. Ʋ nanʋa-bie Ahazɩa dʋndʋŋ nɛ fa ka. 18Wɩaa deemba harɩŋ, La TƖƖNA joŋ luoruŋ nyanyal-bɔŋ ba sɩ bɩ wuo tɩɩbɛ a hɛ Jehoram lɛ. 19Jɩ-lɩa tʋɔŋ bʋa kʋbala lɛ, ʋ luobiee kʋ lɩɩ. A tɩŋ nyanyalɩɩ-la wɩaa, ʋ na hɛɛŋ woruŋ a sʋʋ. Ʋ nɩaa fa bɩ yoho nyiŋ-balɩŋ hɛ zilu a yel ʋ yoho arɩ ba fa sɩ hɛ ŋɩɩ a pɩ ʋ naabalɩmaba. 20Jehoram fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ balɩa nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ chori nɛ. Ʋ sɩ sʋba nʋʋkala tʋɔŋ fa bɩ cheye, ba joŋu hugi Devit tabal-la lɛ, ama kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ lɛ dee.

english_text:
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 8.25-29; 9.21,27,28)
1Earlier, when the Arabs led a raid against Judah, they killed all of Jehoram's sons, except Ahaziah, the youngest one. So the people of Jerusalem crowned him their king. 2He was 22 years old at the time, and he ruled only one year from Jerusalem.
Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, 3and she encouraged her son to sin against the Lord. He followed the evil example of King Ahab and his descendants. 4In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors.
Their advice led to his downfall. 5He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 6and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him. 7It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death.
When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family, 8and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot, 9then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord.
There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah.
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Kings 11.1-3)
10As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that, 11but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 12Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_text:
Ahazɩa dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ
1Arab tɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ fa kʋ lʋara yuo kpʋ kuoro Jehoram hambolibii-hɩasɩŋ kala nɛ, aŋ ka ʋ nanʋa-bie Ahazɩa dʋndʋŋa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jerusalɛm nɩaa lɩɩsɛ Ahazɩa ʋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyɩmma nyuŋ lɛ. 2Ahazɩa fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ balɩa nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ, a hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩna. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Atalɩa, a ŋaa Iziral kuoro Omiri nihiŋ. 3Ŋɩɩ leŋ ʋ ma ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la tɩtɩa Ahab dɩa nɩaa fa sɩ ŋaa, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ naaŋ nɛ yigu hɛ.
4Ʋ fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ arɩ Ahab dɩa nɩaa fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ nyɩmma sʋʋŋ harɩŋ, ba nɛ nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ bʋl wɩaa chɩchagɩlʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ leŋe ʋ tel. 5Ahazɩa fa to nɩalɩŋ niiŋ nɛ a to Ahab nanʋala Joram harɩŋ a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ramɔf Gɩlɩad dɩ ba yuo Siiria tɩŋŋaa kuoro Hazɛɛl. Nɩmɛ nɛ Siiria tɩŋŋaa bolimi Joram. 6Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ mɩɩra mʋ ʋ jaŋ Jɛzɩrɛl dɩ ʋ vaarɛ ʋ tɩtɩa. Jehoram nanʋala Ahazɩa sɩ ŋaa Juda kuoro mʋ nɩmɛ dɩ ʋ na ʋ nyanyalaa.
7Ahazɩa sɩ mʋ na Joram nɛ tɩɩ Wɩa leŋ ʋ tel. Ahazɩa sɩ mʋa, ʋ dɩ Joram lɩɩ dɩ ba na Nimisi nanʋala Jehu, nɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ lɩɩsa dɩ ʋ chei Ahab dɩa. 8Jehu fa sɩɩ kpʋ Ahab dɩa nɩaa arɩ Wɩa sɩ sɩ ʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ na Juda nɩaa sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Ahazɩa malɩma biiriŋ sɩ to ʋ harɩŋ kɔ, Jehu kpʋ ba kala. 9Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ lɛɛlɛ gɔllɔ chɩchɛ Ahazɩa, Jehu nɩaa chɛ mʋ naʋ dɩ ʋ faa Samarɩa lɛ, ba kɛŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛnʋ kʋ pɩ Jehu ʋ kpʋʋ. Ba joŋu hugi aŋ bʋl, “Ʋ ŋaa Jehosafat, nɩɩ-la fa sɩ to La TƖƖNA arɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ kala nihii nɛ.” Nʋʋkala fa bɩra tuo Ahazɩa dɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ sɩ jaŋ wuo dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ a bemba.
Atalɩa dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ
10Ahazɩa naaŋ Atalɩa sɩ kʋ jɩŋ arɩ ʋ nanʋala Ahazɩa sɩ ŋaa Juda kuoro sʋba nɛ, ʋ wʋwalɩmɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋ nʋʋkala sɩ jaŋ wuo dii kuorii-la ba dɩa lɛ. 11Ama kuoro Jehoram tolo Jehoseba sɩ ŋaa Ahazɩa dɩhaala lʋara kɛŋ kuoro Ahazɩa hambolibiisi-la ba sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ba kpʋ tʋɔŋ dɔŋɔ a faa. Bile yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Jʋas. Ʋ fa kɛŋ ʋ dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ benu nɛ a kaa jʋʋ faa Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ dɩɩ-pɩnɩŋ dɔŋɔ lɛ. Jehoseba fa ŋaa Jehoram tolo nɛ, a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Jehoyada ma haala, aŋ ŋaa Ahazɩa dɩhaala, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ʋ kɛŋ bile faa, Atalɩa bɩ wuo kpʋʋ. 12Jʋas fa faa ba teeŋ nɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ ŋɩɩ jɩsɩŋ balɩdʋ, ka Ahazɩa naaŋ Atalɩa dii kuoruŋ a bibeŋ Juda tinteeŋ.

english_text:
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Kings 11.4-21)
1After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. 2These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem 3 and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash.
Jehoiada said to them:
Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king. 4Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple, 5one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards. 6Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded. 7You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
8The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty. 9Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders. 10They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
11Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
12As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple. 13There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
14At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!” 15She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
16Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed, 17then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
18Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing. 19Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
20Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah. 21Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_text:
1Ʋ jɩ-pɛɩ lɛ nɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Jehoyada bɩɩnɛ arɩ ʋ maga ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ leŋ ʋ dɩ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ deemba sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo zɔlɔba bil niiŋ pɩ dɔŋɔ: Jeroham nanʋala Azarɩa, Jehohanaŋ nanʋala Ɩsɩmɛl, Ɔbɛd nanʋala Azarɩa, Adaaya nanʋala Maasɛya arɩ Zikiri nanʋala Ɛlɩsafat. 2Ba gɔllɛ Juda tinteeŋ tasɩŋ kala a yɩrɛ Levi doho nɩaa arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ. Ba kala kɔ Jerusalɛm, 3a hilimi Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ. Nɩmɛ nɛ ba dɩ kuoro nanʋala Jʋas bil niiŋ pɩ dɔŋɔ. Jehoyada bʋla pɩba, “Kuoro nanʋala Jʋas nɛ maga dɩ ʋ dii kuoruŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ hɛ niiŋ ŋɩɩ arɩ Devit doho nɩaa nɛ jaŋ didii kuoruŋ. 4Wɩɩ-la sɩ maga dɩ ma ŋaa nɛ ŋ-la: Chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa bugoo batori jaŋ tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa. Buguŋ dɔŋɔ jaŋ pɔ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la boiŋ-niiree, 5dɩ dɔŋɔ ma pɔ kuoro dɩa, dɩ dɔŋɔ ma pɔ boi-baal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gentine Boi-baalɩŋ, ka dɩ nɩkaanaa ma hɛ La Tɩɩna dɩɩ-bal-la kaalɩsɩŋ tʋɔŋ. 6Nʋʋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ jʋʋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ, see Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa sɩ hɛ tɩntɩŋŋaa lɛ. Ba-na jaŋ wuo jʋʋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba pɩɩsɛ ba disiniŋ ta nɛ. Ama nɩkaana-la maga dɩ ba sɛɩ ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ daga nɛ a hɛ kaala tʋɔŋ.
7Levi doho nɩaa maga dɩ ba chɩna golli kuoro nɛ a pɔʋ, a kori ba laalɩyuori kɩaa. Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ kʋ jʋʋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ, ʋ maga dɩ ba kpʋʋ nɛ. Má kpagɛ kuoro lee na-kala ʋ sɩɩ mʋ.” 8Ŋɩɩ nɛ Levi doho nɩaa arɩ Juda nɩaa ŋaa ŋɩɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Jehoyada sɩ dagɛba. Laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la leŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba mʋ tɩntɩŋŋaa chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ maga dɩ ba wiesi, ba kala mʋ hɛ nɩmɛ. Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Jehoyada bɩ leŋe ba kʋŋkala viiri. 9Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ paa kuoro Devit tiŋŋee arɩ hɔɔtaalɩ-la laalɩyuoro sɩ kaa kɛrɛɛ laa bayuori-hɛŋŋɛɛ kʋbalaa arɩ kʋbiisiŋ sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ lɛ a pɩ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo zɔlɔba. 10Ʋ leŋ baala-la kala sɩɩ pɔ lee-la kori ba laalɩyuori kɩaa a chɩna golli kuoro a kpagɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ koru-la arɩ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la a pɔ kuoro Jʋas, a chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a kaa mʋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ.
11Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehoyada arɩ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ kɛŋ Ahazɩa nanʋala Jʋas kʋ lɩɩ a joŋ kuoru nyunchuulo chuu, aŋ joŋ teniŋ pʋ. Teŋ-la lɛ nɛ ba ŋmʋnsɛ wombie-la kuoroo sɩ maga dɩ ba to a bibeŋ tintee-la hɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba joŋ nʋʋŋ tɩsʋ a dagɛ arɩ ʋ nɛ lɛɛlɛ ŋaa kuoro. Nɩalɩŋ kala ŋaa goŋ a bʋl, “A leŋ dɩ kuoro mɩɩsɩŋ duomi.”
12Atalɩa sɩ nɩa dɩ nɩalɩŋ gɔllɔ fá a ŋaa goŋ a nyɩnyaasɛ kuoro nyuŋ, ʋ sii mʋ ba teeŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ. 13Ʋ sɩ bene, ʋ na kuoro Jʋas dɩ ʋ chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la boiŋ niiŋ a kpagɛ jebiiŋ, ka laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋmʋʋ nyilliŋ chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ. Tintee-la nɩaa kala jʋjʋɔsɛ aŋ ŋmʋŋmʋʋ nyilliŋ. Nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ du kɩaa nɛ fa kɛŋ yɩɩlɩ yɩɩraa ba gbigbieli. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Atalɩa tʋɔŋ chei, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ aŋ ŋaa goŋ a bʋl, “Ma ŋaamɛ zɛmbɛ, ma ŋaamɛ zɛmbɛ.”
14Jehoyada bɩra bʋla pɩ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo zɔlɔba, “Má kɛŋ Atalɩa pɩɛga to nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ leriŋ tʋɔŋ kʋ lɩɩ, má kpʋ nʋʋkala sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ laaʋ ta, ama má sɩ́ Atalɩa kpʋ a kpagɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lee-kala.” 15Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛnʋ, dɩ ʋ yi boi-baal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Janɩŋ Boi-baalɩŋ a kpagɛ kuoru dɩa, a kpʋʋ nɩmɛ.
16Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Jehoyada, kuoro Jʋas arɩ nɩalɩŋ hɛ niiŋ pɩ dɔŋɔ arɩ ba jaŋ ŋaa La TƖƖNA nɩaa. 17Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ kala mʋ ŋmoo Baal vene-la dɩa-la lo a yɛrɛ ʋ korunuŋ kala, a ŋmoo tɔmɔ-la kala yɛrɛ muno muno, aŋ kpʋ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ kpaarɛ Baal baa yɩrɛ Mataŋ korunu-la sɩpaaŋ.
18Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehoyada joŋ Levi doho nɩaa arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa hɛ dɩ ba nɛ tɩtɩŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ. Ba nɛ nɩalɩŋ kuoro Devit fa sɩ joŋ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la pa Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ. Ba nɛ ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩpɩ La TƖƖNA arɩ wɩalɩŋ Mosis sɩ ŋmʋnsa bil dɩ ba tuto sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ, a yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a jʋjʋɔsɛ arɩ Devit fa sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ. 19Jehoyada fa bɩra leŋe nɩaa pɔ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la boiŋ niiree nɛ, dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ sɩ wuo jʋʋ. 20Ka ʋ kɛŋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo zɔlɔba arɩ nɩbalaa, sɩpaalaaraa arɩ tintee-la nɩaa kala, ba kɛŋ kuoro Jʋas a lɩɩ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ, a to boi-baal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nyuŋ Boi-baalɩŋ a jʋʋ kuoru dɩa, a hollu ʋ kuoru kpasa nyuŋ. 21Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ tintee-la lɛ jʋjʋɔsɛ. Jerusalɛm kala lɛɛlɛ fɩɛla pɩŋ sɔm, a tɩŋ ba sɩ kpʋ Atalɩa wɩaa.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Kings 12.1-16)
1Joash was only 7 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right. 3Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
4Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple. 5He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.”
But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders. 6 So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent. 7And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
8Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple. 9He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
10The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box. 11Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside.
This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected. 12Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
13These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new. 14They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple.
Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived. 15He died at the ripe old age of 130 years, 16and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple.
Joash Turns Away from the Lord
17After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted. 18The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 19but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
20 God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
21-22King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.”
Joash Is Killed
23In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus. 24The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
25-26Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah. They plotted and killed Joash while he was in bed, recovering from his wounds. Joash was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. 27The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_text:
Jʋas wasɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ
1Jʋas fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ balɩpɛ nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa nɛ. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Zɩbɩa, a lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛɛsɩba. 2Jʋas fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ, Jehoyada sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa kala lɛ. 3Jehoyada fa jaa haalaa balɩa nɛ pʋ, ʋ kaa lʋl hambolibiisiŋ arɩ hantolibiisiŋ.
4Harɩŋ bʋa-kʋbala lɛ Jʋas kɛŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ dɩ ʋ wasɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la. 5Ʋ yɩrɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa a bʋla pɩba, “Má mʋ Juda tasɩŋ kala a laa moribie-la ba sɩ vɛnɛ titiŋ jɩna kala ba kaa wasɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la. Má ŋaa ŋɩɩ lɩma.” Ama Levi doho nɩalɩŋ bɩ moribie-la lɩma laa.
6Ŋɩɩ wɩaa Jʋas yɩrɛ Jehoyada, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ha bɩ leŋe Levi doho nɩaa laa moribie-la Juda nɩaa arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa sɩ yie vɛnɛɛ tiŋ? Moribie-la La TƖƖNA tɩntɩnna Mosis arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ sɛyɛ arɩ ba jaŋ titiŋ dɩ ba kaa wʋwasɛ lɛbɩ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ.”
7Atalɩa, ha-bɔŋ-la hambolibiisiŋ fa boro jʋʋ paa kʋzɔmɔ-la ba sɩ joŋo hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ dɔnsʋŋ nɛ a kaa kpaarɛ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal.
8Kuoro leŋ ba ŋaa dagɩ-bie a joŋo bil La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la boiŋ niiŋ jeeŋ harɩŋ. 9Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba heele bʋla pɩ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa dɩ nʋʋkala kʋ tiŋ lampoo-la a pɩ La TƖƖNA, kʋ-la Wɩa tɩntɩnna Mosis fa sɩ leŋe Iziral tɩŋŋaa tiŋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ. 10Nɩalɩŋ arɩ ba sɩpaalaaraa kala tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ, ba kɛŋ moribie-la kaa kʋ hɛ dagɩ-bie-la tʋɔŋ ʋ su. 11Bʋa na-kala lɛ dɩ Levi doho nɩaa nɛ joŋ daga-la a kaa mʋ kuoro tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ teeŋ, dɩ ba na dɩ moribiee suo, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ kuoro teniŋ arɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ tɩma pɩpɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ yie chaarɛ nɛ, aŋ leŋ ba kaa mɩɩra mʋ bil ʋ dɩ-biliŋ. Ba ŋaa ŋɩɩ nɛ bʋa na-kala a laa moribiee yʋgɛ woruŋ. 12Kuoro arɩ Jehoyada joŋ moribie-la pɩ nɩalɩŋ ba sɩ lɩɩsa ba bibeŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ wasɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la. Ba laa, a chɛ dɩɩ-saaraa, kapɩntaba, arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ hɔɔŋ arɩ kɔlɩɩŋ tɩtɩŋ dɩ ba wasɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la.
13Nɩalɩŋ fa sɩɩ beŋ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la fɩɛsɛ sɩɩŋ tɩŋ woruŋ, ba wasɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la ʋ bɩra nagɛ ŋɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ naga nɛ, a kɛŋ doluŋ woruŋ. 14Ba sɩ wasɛ dɩa-la dɛrɛ, ba kɛŋ moribii kaanaa kʋ pɩ kuoro arɩ Jehoyada. Ba kaa ŋaa Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tɩntɩnnɩ kɩaa, tɩntɩnnɩ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kaa ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, hɛntɛrɛɛ arɩ kɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla ŋaa. Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ Jehoyada mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ, baa ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ nɛ bʋa na-kala La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ.
15Jehoyada fa hɩɛsa nɛ woruŋ, ʋʋ sʋʋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa jɩsɩŋ zɔlɔ arɩ mara arɩ fɩɩ nɛ. 16Ba joŋu hugi kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ Devit tabal-la lɛ, a tɩŋ tɩntɩŋ-zɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ tɩma pɩ Wɩa, Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la.
Wʋbɔmɔ-la Jʋas sɩ ŋaa
17Jehoyada sʋʋŋ harɩŋ, Juda nɩaa sɩpaalaaraa sii kɔ kuoro Jʋas teeŋ a zilu, ʋ leŋ ba ŋaa wɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ chɛ. 18Ba vɩa La TƖƖNA, ba naabalɩmaba Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la ta nɛ, aŋ mɩɩra kpʋkpaarɛ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daasɩŋ arɩ tɔŋŋɔɔ. Ba wʋbɔmɔ-la leŋ Wɩa na baanɩŋ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa nyuŋ. 19La TƖƖNA tɩŋ ʋ wʋlaabʋllaa dɩ ba kpʋrɩsɛ nɩalɩŋ dɩgɩlaa dɩ ba mɩɩra kɔ ʋ teeŋ, ama ba vɩa dɩ ba nɩɩ.
20Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa Dɩma kʋ jʋʋ Zɛkarɩya sɩ ŋaa Jehoyada, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara nanʋala. Ʋ chɩŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩpaaŋ a bʋla pɩba, “Wɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma vɩa wɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩ daga? Wɩɩkala bɩ jaŋ vɛŋ woruŋ a pɩma. Ma sɩ vɩa La TƖƖNA ŋɩɩ, ʋ ma vɩama nɛ.’ ”
21Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba vʋʋra sii chɩŋ ʋ lɛ, kuoro pa wombiiŋ ba yagʋ arɩ tabɩaa a kpʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la kaala lɛ. 22Kuoro Jʋas fa bɩ wʋzɔmɔ-la Zɛkarɩya nyɩmma Jehoyada fa sɩ ŋaa ʋ lɛ liise aŋ kpʋ ʋ nanʋala. Zɛkarɩya fa sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ, ŋ-la nɛ ʋ bʋl, “A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA na wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa a dɔgʋsʋŋ.”
23Jɩna dɩ-suomuŋ, Siiria tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo sii kʋ yuo dii kuoro Jʋas, a tɔ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa hɛ a kpʋ ba sɩpaalaaraa kala, aŋ paa ba dʋa kala kaa mʋ pɩ ba kuoro sɩ hɛ Damasɩkʋs lɛ. 24Siiria tɩmma-la laalɩyuoroo fa bɩ yʋgɛ, ka La TƖƖNA joŋ Juda tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuori daŋ-la a hɛ ba nɩsɩŋ lɛ, a tɩŋ Juda nɩaa sɩ vɩa La TƖƖNA ba naabalɩmaba Wɩa. Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA to a dɔgɩsɛ Jʋas. 25Siiria tɩmma-la kʋʋ leŋ laal-la dɩ ba chaasa bolimi Jʋas nɛ woruŋ. Ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ balɩa ma vʋʋrɛ a kpʋʋ ʋ kʋpɩnɩŋ nyuŋ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ kpʋ Zɛkarɩya, Jehoyada sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara nanʋala wɩaa. Ba joŋu hugi Devit tabal-la lɛ. Ama kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ dee.
26Nɩalɩŋ sɩ vʋʋra kpʋʋ nɛ ŋaa: Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa tolo Sɩmɛɛf nanʋala Zabad arɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa tolo Sɔmɔ nanʋala Jehozabad. 27Wɩalɩŋ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ sɩ ŋaa arɩ wʋdaŋ-la kala Wɩa wʋlaabʋllaa sɩ bʋla a tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ wasɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ lɛ. Ʋ nanʋala Amazɩa nɛ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_text:
King Amaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.1-6)
1Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jehoaddin.
2Even though Amaziah obeyed the Lord by doing right, he refused to be completely faithful. 3For example, as soon as he had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father. 4 But the children of those officers were not killed; the Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished.
Edom Is Defeated
(2 Kings 14.7)
5Amaziah sent a message to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin and called together all the men who were 20 years old and older. Three hundred thousand men went to Jerusalem, all of them ready for battle and able to fight with spears and shields. Amaziah grouped these soldiers according to their clans and put them under the command of his army officers. 6Amaziah also paid about 3.4 tons of silver to hire 100,000 soldiers from Israel.
7One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel, 8and so he will let your enemies defeat you, even if you fight hard. He is the one who brings both victory and defeat.”
9Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?”
“The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
10Amaziah ordered the troops from Israel to go home, but when they left, they were furious with the people of Judah.
11After Amaziah got his courage back, he led his troops to Salt Valley, where he killed 10,000 Edomite soldiers in battle. 12He captured 10,000 more soldiers and dragged them to the top of a high cliff. Then he pushed them over the side, and they all were killed on the rocks below.
13Meanwhile, the Israelite troops that Amaziah had sent home, raided the towns in Judah between Samaria and Beth-Horon. They killed 3,000 people and carried off their possessions.
14After Amaziah had defeated the Edomite army, he returned to Jerusalem. He took with him the idols of the Edomite gods and set them up. Then he bowed down and offered them sacrifices. 15This made the Lord very angry, and he sent a prophet to ask Amaziah, “Why would you worship these foreign gods that couldn't even save their own people from your attack?”
16But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.”
The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!”
Israel Defeats Judah
(2 Kings 14.8-14)
17King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
18Jehoash sent back a reply that said:
Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
19Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
20God made Amaziah stubborn because he was planning to punish him for worshiping the Edomite gods. Amaziah refused to listen to Jehoash's warning, 21so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops. 22During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home, 23and Jehoash captured Amaziah.
Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly 200 meters long. 24He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
Amaziah Is Killed
(2 Kings 14.15-20)
25Amaziah lived 15 years after Jehoash died. 26Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
27As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there. 28His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_text:
Amazɩa dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ
1Amazɩa fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ banɔŋ nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ nibi. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Jehuadiŋ, a lɩɩ Jerusalɛm. 2Amazɩa fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ, ama ʋ fa bɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ kala kaa to La TƖƖNA. 3Amazɩa kuoruŋ fa sɩ chɩna dɛrɛ, ʋ kɛsɛ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la fa sɩ kpʋ ʋ nyɩmma fa sɩ ŋaa kuoro a kpʋba. 4Ama ʋ fa bɩ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la sɩ kpʋ ʋ nyɩmma hambolibiisiŋ-na kpʋa, bɛɛ wɩaa wɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩ joŋo dagɛ Mosis ʋ ŋmʋnsa bil dɩ nɩaa tuto bʋl ŋ-la nɛ: “Dɩ nʋʋ bii nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba kpʋ ʋ nyɩmma a tɩŋ wɩɩ-la wɩaa. Dɩ nyɩmma ma nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba kpʋ ʋ bie a tɩŋ wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa. Nʋʋkala maga dɩ ba kpʋʋ a tɩŋ ʋ tɩtɩa wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa nɛ.”
5Kuoro Amazɩa yɩrɛ Juda nɩaa hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a leŋ ba chɩŋ dɩa dɩa, ʋ jomba hɛ Juda arɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo bʋɩba arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo zɔlɔba nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tʋɔsɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ yi jɩsɩŋ mara koo a kieli, a na dɩ ba fa ŋaa nɩaa bʋɩ zɔɔ-batori sɩ jaŋ wuo yuo laalɩŋ, a jaŋ wuo kori timiŋ arɩ hɔɔtaalɩ-la laalɩyuoroo sɩ kaa kɛrɛɛ laa bayuori hɛŋŋɛɛ. 6Ʋ fa bɩra joŋ warɩpʋla bʋɩ batori arɩ zɔɔ-banɛsɛ nɛ, a pɩ Iziral laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ zɔlɔ ka dɩ ba pɛ ʋ nɩaa lɛ.
7Ama Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ kʋbala kʋ bʋla pʋ, “Kuoro, sɩ́ Iziral laalɩyuoroo deemba kaa to ŋ harɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA bɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa harɩŋ chɩna, ʋ bɩ jaŋ pɛ Efirem tɩmma-la kʋŋkala lɛ. 8Ŋ jaŋ bɩɩnɛ dɩ ba nɛ to ŋ laalɩyuoroo harɩŋ mʋ, ŋɩɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ kɛŋ doluŋ a yuo laalɩŋ dii, ama Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ a jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ ŋ yuo dii koo ŋ sɩ́ yuo dii. Ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ yuo diiŋ.”
9Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amazɩa pɩɛsɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la, “Aŋ ka warɩpʋla-la mɩ sɩ joŋo tiŋ Iziral laalɩyuoro-la?” Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la bʋl, “La TƖƖNA jaŋ wuo pɩŋ a kɩɩ ŋɩɩ.”
10Amazɩa leŋ Efirem laalɩyuoro-la ʋ sɩ time viiri. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba na baanɩŋ woruŋ Juda nɩaa nyuŋ.
11Amazɩa nyɩrɛ bɔyɛ a kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo mʋ fuonaa-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Yɩsɩŋ Fuonaaŋ. Nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ kpʋ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa bʋɩ fii. 12Juda laalɩyuoro-la fa bɩra yuo kɛsɛ nɩaa bʋɩ fii ma nɛ, a kɛmba kaa jɩl bʋŋ kʋbala nyu-gbaŋa, aŋ jomba yuo ta ba kʋ tuu tel a kala yɛrɛ muno muno.
13Ama Iziral laalɩyuoro-la Amazɩa fa sɩ leŋe ba mɩɩrɛ a bɩ ʋ harɩŋ to mʋ laalɩŋ, ma mʋ yuo Juda tasɩŋ, a chɩŋ Samarɩa tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa mʋ yi Bɛf Hɔrɔŋ. Ba fa kpʋ nɩaa bʋɩ batori nɛ, aŋ paa ba kɩaa yʋgɛ woruŋ a kaa viiri.
14Amazɩa sɩ mʋ yuo dii Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa aŋ mɩɩra kʋkɔ Jerusalɛm, ʋ pɛ paa ba vesiŋ ma nɛ a kaa kʋ bil a nagɛ ʋ tɩtɩa vesiŋ, a kpirime zizilba aŋ pɛ kpʋkpaarɛba. 15Ŋɩɩ leŋ La TƖƖNA faasa na baanɩŋ Amazɩa nyuŋ, a tɩŋ ʋ wʋlaabʋllʋ kʋbala ʋ kʋ pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kpʋkpaarɛ vesi-la sɩ bɩ wuo laa ba tɩŋŋaa ta ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ?”
16Ʋ fa ha sɩɩ bʋl wɩaa ŋɩɩ, kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “La lɩɩsɩŋ nɛɛ dɩ ŋ chagɩlɛ kuoroo? Bɩra sɩ́ wɩɩ bʋl, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba kpʋŋ.”
Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la leŋ, aŋ bʋl, “Mɩ jɩma arɩ Wɩa ŋaa siri nɛ dɩ ʋ cheyiŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ deemba kala nɛ aŋ bɩra vɩa dɩ ŋ jegile nɩɩ mɩ sɩɩ chagɩlɩŋ.”
17Juda kuoro Amazɩa sɩ mʋ pɩɛsɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ chagɩlʋ wɩaa, ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Jehuas sɩ ŋaa Jehuahas nanʋala aŋ ŋaa Jehu ma nihiŋ, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa baal, kʋ lɩɩ chemmi dɩ la yuo laalɩŋ.”
18Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Jehuas mɩɩra tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋl ŋ-la pɩ Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Amazɩa: “Sɔ-pugu-bie nɛ fa hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ tinteeŋ lɛ, a tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ kuolu tɩa ma sɩ hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ lɛ, ‘Joŋ ŋ tolo pɩ mɩ nanʋala dɩ ʋ jaa.’ Ŋɩɩ nɛ baga kʋŋ ma fa sɩ hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ lɛ kʋ nʋɔsɛ sɔ-pugu-bie-la a bʋrɩgɛ. 19Amazɩa, ŋ bɩɩna ŋ dolie nɛ ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ yuo dii Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa a bibigisi ŋ tɩtɩa lɛ. Hɔŋ ŋ dɩa lɛ sɔm, sɩ́ wɩaa lɔgɔ hɛ ŋ tɩtɩa arɩ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa kala lɛ.”
20Ama Amazɩa bɩ jegile nɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa Wɩa chɛ dɩ ʋ leŋ Jehuas yuo diiba nɛ, a tɩŋ ba sɩɩ kpaarɛ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa vesi-la wɩaa. 21Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral kuoro Jehuas arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kʋ yuo Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Amazɩa arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Sɛmɛs sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. 22Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo dii Juda tɩŋŋaa, ba kala fá mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ, 23ka Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Jehuas sɩ ŋaa Jʋas nanʋala, a ŋaa Ahazɩa ma nihiŋ yuo kɛŋ Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Amazɩa Bɛf Sɛmɛs lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jehuas kɛnʋ kɔ Jerusalɛm a ŋmoo jebii-la ba sɩ saa golli Jerusalɛm lo, a chɩŋ Efirem Boi-baalɩŋ a kaa mʋ yi Je-gʋnʋŋ Boi-baalɩŋ lɛ. Ʋ duomuŋ ŋaa arɩ naakieliŋ zɔɔ-balɩa. 24Jehuas paa sɛlɩmɛ, hɔpʋla arɩ kɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ kaa tɩtɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ, kɩalɩŋ Ɔbɛd-Ɛdɔm doho nɩaa fa sɩɩ beŋ, a paa kɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ kuoru dɩa ma lɛ, a pɛ nɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ yuo kɛsɛ lɛ, a kaa mɩɩra mʋ Samarɩa.
25Jehuahas nanʋala Jehuas sɩ ŋaa Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro sʋʋŋ harɩŋ lɛ, Jʋas nanʋala Amazɩa sɩ ŋaa Juda tinteeŋ kuoro ha hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ banɔŋ nɛ. 26Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Amazɩa sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, a chɩŋ dɩ-suomuŋ a kaa mʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ arɩ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. 27A chɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ Amazɩa sɩ vɩa La TƖƖNA tonuŋ, nɩaa vʋʋrɛ a sii chɩŋ ʋ lɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ lɩɩ fá a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lakɩs. Ama ba hɛ nɩaa ba kiri ʋ libe, a mʋ kpʋʋ nɩmɛ. 28Ba kɛŋ jaaba joŋ ʋ kʋsʋʋŋ a kaa mɩɩra kɔ, a hugu ʋ nyɩmmaba dɩ-huguŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ.

english_text:
King Uzziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.21,22; 15.1-7)
1-3After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only 16 at the time. Uzziah ruled 52 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jecoliah. During his rule, he recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath.
4He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done. 5Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
6While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia. 7God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites. 8Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
9In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward. 10He also built defense towers out in the desert.
He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
11Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials. 12-13There were 307,500 trained soldiers, all under the command of 2,600 clan leaders. These powerful troops protected the king against any enemy. 14Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging. 15Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall.
God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world.
Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
16Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall.
One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him. 17Azariah the priest and 80 other brave priests followed Uzziah into the temple 18 and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
19Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead! 20Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
21Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
22Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. 23 Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_text:
Uzia dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa kala lɩɩsɛ ʋ nanʋala Uzia sɩ ŋaa jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩdʋ, ʋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyɩmma nyuŋ lɛ. 2Ʋ nyɩmma sʋʋŋ harɩŋ lɛ nɛ ʋ bɩra yuo laa taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛlaf a wasa paa saa pɩ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa.
3Uzia (ʋ nɛ ha Azarɩa) fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩdʋ nɛ aŋ dii Juda tinteeŋ kuoruŋ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ fii arɩ balɩa. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Jekolia, a lɩɩ Jerusalɛm. 4Ʋ fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ, arɩ ʋ nyɩmma Amazɩa fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. 5Zɛkarɩya mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ, Uzia fa to Wɩa nɛ woruŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ nɛ faa dagʋ. Ʋ sɩ to La TƖƖNA ŋɩɩ, Wɩa leŋ ʋ wɩɩkala vɛŋ woruŋ.
6Uzia sii mʋ kɛŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa yuo laalɩŋ a ŋmoo tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gaf, Jabɩnɛ arɩ Asido jebiee kala lo. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ wasa saa tasɩ-la sɩ kpagɛ Asido arɩ tasɩ-la sɩ hɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tinteeŋ sɛsɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ. 7Wɩa pɛ ʋ lɛ ʋ yuo dii Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa arɩ Arab tɩmma-la fa sɩ hɔŋ Guu Baal lɛ, a kɛŋ Mewuni tɩŋŋaa pɛ. 8Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa fa paala tiŋ lampoo a pɩpɩ Uzia nɛ, ŋɩɩ leŋ ʋ kɛŋ doluŋ woruŋ, ʋ yɩrɩŋ sii leriŋ kala, a mʋ yi Ijipiti tinteeŋ.
9Uzia fa saa jebii-duduosuŋ hɛ Jerusalɛm boi-baalaa deemba lɛ nɛ: Je-gʋnʋŋ Boi-baalɩŋ, Fuonaaŋ Boi-baalɩŋ arɩ jebii-la loŋgoruŋ lɛ, a leŋ ba dol woruŋ. 10Ʋ fa bɩra saa jebii-duduosuŋ nɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ a lu pɩlaa yʋgɛ nɩmɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ fa kɛŋ pʋsʋŋ yʋgɛ nɛ dundolluŋ arɩ tintee-taalaa lɛ. Ʋ fa kɛŋ nɩaa ma nɛ ba tɩtɩŋ ʋ bagɩsɩŋ arɩ ʋ girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ lɛ dundollu-la sɩ hɛ peelee bʋbʋɔŋ nyuŋ arɩ tintee-taala sɩ zɔmɔ lɛ. Ʋ fa cho pɛrɩŋ.
11Uzia fa kɛŋ laalɩyuoro-la sɩ chaasa gʋnnɛ laalɩŋ yuonuŋ nɛ woruŋ, a kɛŋ ba hɛ dɔŋɔ dɩ ba mʋ laalɩŋ, arɩ Jɛyɛl nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ ba tenniŋ arɩ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Maasɛya sɩ kɛmba kpaa bugoo. Kuoro dɩa tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ dɔŋɔ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hananaaya nɛ fa ŋaa Jɛyɛl arɩ Maasɛya kala nɩhɩaŋ, ʋ nɛ dagɛba ŋɩɩ. 12Dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ bʋɩ balɩa arɩ zɔɔ-balɩdʋ nɛ faa beŋ laalɩyuoro-la. 13Dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ deemba fa beŋ laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ zɔɔ-batori arɩ balɩpɛ arɩ zɔɔ-banɔŋ nɛ sɩ chaasa gʋnnɛ laalɩŋ yuonuŋ. Ba fa ŋaa laalɩyuori-duoru nɛ a pɛ kuoro lɛ a yuyuo ʋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ. 14Ŋɩɩ nɛ Uzia chɛ laalɩyuori kɩaa deemba a pɩ laalɩyuoro-la kala: Hɔɔtaalɩ-la ba sɩ kaa kɛrɛɛ laa bayuori-hɛŋŋɛɛ, tiŋŋee, nyuŋ-chugbaŋkogunuŋ, laalɩyuori-gɛnnɩŋ, tosuŋ arɩ kpalɩŋ tabɩaa. 15Jerusalɛm lɛ ʋ leŋ gɔgɔɔ ŋaa kɩaa ba sɩ jaŋ kaa yuyuo to-hɛŋŋɛɛ arɩ tabɩɩ-balaa, ba chɩŋ jebii-duduosuŋ arɩ je-gʋnaa lɛ. Ʋ yɩrɩŋ sii leriŋ kala, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA pɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ ʋ kɛŋ doluŋ woruŋ.
16Uzia sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ ŋɩɩ, ʋ joŋ ŋɩɩ ŋaa babiibal wɩɩ, ŋɩɩ leŋ ʋ tel. Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala ʋ vɩa ʋ TƖƖNA Wɩa niiŋ aŋ sii jʋʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-balɩŋ dɩ ʋ nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ koru-la lɛ ba sɩɩ nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ. 17Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Azarɩa arɩ nɩaa mahɩŋ banɛsɛ ma sɩ ŋaa La TƖƖNA Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa sɩ kɛŋ nyuŋ-duoŋ woruŋ to ʋ harɩŋ a jʋʋ, 18a mʋ ʋ teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ-na Uzia, ŋ bɩ wombii kɛnɛ dɩ ŋ nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA. Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa sɩ ŋaa Arɔŋ doho nɩaa, ba sɩ joŋo hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ tɩntɩmɩɩ nɛ. Lɩɩ Wɩa dɩa deeŋ tʋɔŋ. Ŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ, La TƖƖNA Wɩa bɩra bɩ jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ.”
19Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Uzia fa kori kʋ-la lɛ ba sɩ yie hɛ nyiniŋ a nyɩnyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ a chɩŋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ koru-la sɛmɛ a kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ dɩ ʋ nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA. Ʋ sɩ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ Azarɩa sɩ bʋla, ʋ na baanɩŋ a tʋtʋʋsɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa koru-la sɩpaaŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ. Ʋ sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, dayalɩmɩŋ guu yagɛ ʋ tile lɛ. 20Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ Azarɩa arɩ nɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa sɩ na dɩ dayalɩmɩŋ yagɛ ʋ tile lɛ ŋɩɩ, ba kiru ta ʋ lɩɩ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ. Uzia ma tɩtɩa fa cho dɩ ʋ lɩɩ lɩma nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA dɔgʋsʋ nɛ. 21Dayalɩbɩɩ-la fa hɛ Kuoro Uzia lɛ nɛ ʋ mɩɩ-kaanɩŋ kala lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba lɩɩsʋ kuoru dɩa lɛ, ʋ jʋjʋʋ ʋ dʋndʋŋ dɩa, ʋ bɩra bɩ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la jʋa aŋ mʋ sʋʋ. Ka ʋ nanʋala Jotam laa ʋ nyuŋ a bibeŋ tintee-la. 22Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Uzia sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, a chɩŋ dɩ-suomuŋ a kaa mʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ, ba kala nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla Azaaya sɩ ŋaa Amos nanʋala ŋmʋnsa bil. 23Ŋɩɩ nɛ Uzia sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi kuoroo ŋmaŋkaaŋ lɛ a kpagɛ kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ, a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ kɛŋ dayalɩmɩŋ wɩaa. Ka ʋ nanʋala Jotam dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_text:
King Jotham of Judah
(2 Kings 15.32-38)
1Jotham was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years. Jerushah his mother was the daughter of Zadok.
2Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
3Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the temple and did a lot of work to repair the wall near Mount Ophel. 4He built towns in the mountains of Judah and built fortresses and defense towers in the forests.
5During his rule he attacked and defeated the Ammonites. Then every year for the next three years, he forced them to pay 3.4 tons of silver, 1,000 tons of wheat, and 1,000 tons of barley.
6Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
7Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah. 8After he had ruled Judah 16 years, he died at the age of 41. 9He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_text:
Jotam dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ
1Jotam fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ banɔŋ nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩdʋ. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Jerusa, a ŋaa Zadɔk tolo. 2Jotam fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ a nagɛ ʋ nyɩmma Uzia fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Ʋ-na fa bɩ ʋ nyɩmma wʋbɔŋ-la ŋaa ʋ sɩ jʋʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la dɩ ʋ nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ. Ama nɩaa fa haa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ. 3Jotam nɛ fa wasa saa La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la boi-baal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nyuŋ Boi-baalɩŋ, a tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa yʋgɛ jee-la ma sɩ hɛ Ɔfɛl dundolo nyuŋ lɛ. 4Ʋ nɛ saa tasɩŋ Juda tinteeŋ dundolluŋ nyuŋ, a saa dɩɩ-duoruŋ arɩ jebii-duduosuŋ ma ba duunuŋ tʋɔŋ.
5Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jotam sii mʋ yuo dii Amɔŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo. Jɩna-la ʋ fʋgɛ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa ba tiŋ hɔpʋla yuŋuŋ sɩ ŋaa kilo bʋɩ batori arɩ zɔɔ-banɛsɛ, mɛmpɛ bɔtɔba bʋɩ, mɩaa ma bɔtɔba bʋɩ a pʋ. Amɔŋ tɩmma-la tiŋ kɩalɩŋ magɛ ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ a pʋ jɩ-lɩa arɩ jɩ-tori kala lɛ.
6Jotam fa to ʋ TƖƖNA Wɩa nɛ woruŋ, ŋɩɩ leŋ ʋ kɛŋ doluŋ yʋgɛ.
7Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Jotam sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ: laal-la kala ʋ sɩ yuo arɩ ʋ wɩaa dɔnsʋŋ. 8Jotam fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ banɔŋ nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩdʋ. 9Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jotam sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ Devit tabal-la lɛ. Ka ʋ nanʋala Ahas dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_text:
King Ahaz of Judah
(2 Kings 16.1-4)
1Ahaz was 20 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Ahaz was nothing like his ancestor David. Ahaz disobeyed the Lord 2and was as sinful as the kings of Israel. He made idols of the god Baal, 3and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 4Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
Syria and Israel Attack Judah
(2 Kings 16.5,6)
5-6 Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them.
The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed 120,000 of its bravest soldiers in one day. 7During that battle, an Israelite soldier named Zichri killed three men from Judah: Maaseiah the king's son; Azrikam, the official in charge of the palace; and Elkanah, the king's second in command. 8The Israelite troops captured 200,000 women and children and took them back to their capital city of Samaria, along with a large amount of their possessions. They did these things even though the people of Judah were their own relatives.
Oded the Prophet Condemns Israel
9Oded lived in Samaria and was one of the Lord's prophets. He met Israel's army on their way back from Judah and said to them:
The Lord God of your ancestors let you defeat Judah's army only because he was angry with them. But you should not have been so cruel! 10If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
11Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
12About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong, 13and they said:
If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
14So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah. 15The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria.
Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help
(2 Kings 16.7-9)
16-18Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places.
Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help. 19But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning. 20So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse. 21Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz.
The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
22Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before. 23He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
24Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem. 25In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
26Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 27 Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_text:
Ahas dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ
1Ahas fa ŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara nɛ aŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩdʋ nɛ. Ʋ fa bɩ ʋ naabalɩma Devit naabʋɔsʋŋ to. Ʋ-na fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ ka tɔrɛ nɛ. 2Ʋ fa to Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo naabʋɔsʋŋ nɛ a libi Baal tɔŋŋɔɔ a kpʋkpaarɛ. 3Ʋ fa kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a nyɩgɛ nɛ Bɛŋ Hɩnɔm fuonaaŋ lɛ, a paala kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa hambolibiisiŋ kpʋ a nyɩga pɩ vesiŋ a ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ kɩsʋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Wɩalɩŋ tɩtɩa nɛ tinteye-la nɩaa fa ŋɩŋaa tintee-la lɛ, La TƖƖNA kiriba ta ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ hɔŋ.
4Ʋ faa kpaarɛ vʋɩyaa nɛ aŋ nyɩnyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa, dundolluŋ nyuŋ arɩ tɩɩ-lugunuŋ bʋbʋɔsʋŋ kala.
5Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ Tɩɩna Wɩa joŋu hɛ Siiria kuoro nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ba yuo diiu a kɛsɛ ʋ nɩaa yʋgɛ woruŋ a kaa mʋ Damasɩkʋs ba ŋaa dansarɩkaba. La TƖƖNA bɩra joŋu hɛ Iziral kuoro nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ ʋ chaasa kpʋ ʋ nɩaa woruŋ. 6Juda nɩaa sɩ vɩa dɩ ba to La TƖƖNA, ba naabalɩmaba Wɩa, ʋ leŋ Remalia nanʋala Pɛka sɩ ŋaa Iziral kuoro joŋ tapʋl bala a kpʋ ba laalɩyuori-duoruŋ bʋɩ zɔlɔ arɩ mara. 7Laal-la lɛ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuori-babiibal ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zikiri a lɩɩ Efirem kpʋ Juda nɩaa deemba: kuoro nanʋala Maasɛya, Azirikam, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ kuoro dɩa arɩ Ɛlɩkaana, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ tɩgɛ kuoro lɛ. 8Iziral tɩmma-la fa yuo kɛsɛ ba naambiiriŋ Juda nɩaa haalaa arɩ hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ba hantolibiisiŋ bʋɩ zɔɔ-balɩa nɛ. Ba fa pɛ paa ba kɩaa a yʋgɛ nɛ woruŋ a kaa mʋ Samarɩa.
9Ama Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ baa yɩrɛ Ɔdɛd, ʋ lɩɩ cheŋ Iziral laalɩyuoro-la dɩ ba mɩɩraa kɔ Samarɩa. Ʋ bʋla pɩba, “La TƖƖNA, ma naabalɩmaba Wɩa fa sɩ na baanɩŋ Juda nɩaa nyuŋ nɛ tɩɩ ʋ leŋ ma yuo diiba. Ama ma faasa kpʋba kɩŋkɛŋ nɛ arɩ tʋɔhɛɛŋ, Wɩa tʋɔŋ chei. 10Lɛɛlɛ maa chɛ dɩ ma kɛŋ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm baalaa arɩ haalaa bɩrɩmɛ ma yosi nɛ. Ama ma ma ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa teeŋ. 11Má nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ, má joŋ ma naambiiri-la ma sɩ kɛsɛ arɩ yosuŋ ta dɩ ba mɩɩra viiri, ŋɩɩ dee La TƖƖNA jaŋ faasa na baanɩŋ ma nyuŋ a dɔgɩsɛma.”
12Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa dɔnsʋŋ sɩ hɛ Efirem lɛ: Jehohanaŋ nanʋala Azarɩa, Mɛsɩlɩmɔf nanʋala Bɛrɛkɩa, Salum nanʋala Jɛhɩzɩkɩa arɩ Hadɩlaɩ nanʋala Amasa mʋ cheŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ lɩɩ laal-la kʋkɔ, a bʋla pɩba, 13“Má sɩ́ nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ yuo kɛsɛ kaa kɔ daha. Ŋɩɩ dee la jaŋ laa cheeriŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Maa chɛ dɩ la laa cheeriŋ dɩ la wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ wasa yʋgɛ nɛɛ? La cheeriŋ paala yʋgɛ nɛ, La TƖƖNA faasa na baanɩŋ la Iziral nɩaa nyuŋ.”
14Ŋɩɩ nɛ laalɩyuoro-la joŋ Juda nɩalɩŋ ba fa sɩ yuo kɛsɛ arɩ ba kɩaa kala ta, ba sɩpaalaara-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hilime sɩɩŋ lɛ. 15Sɩpaalaara-la banɛsɛ beŋ nɩalɩŋ ba fa sɩ yuo kɛsɛ kɩaa tʋɔŋ a chaarɛ gɛnnɩŋ pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ yarɩ-biree ba laalɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba pɩba gɛnnɩŋ, nɛntɛŋŋɛɛ, kʋdiilee arɩ lɩɩŋ, aŋ ŋaa nʋʋŋ ma a hɛ ba naawɩɩlaa. Ba nɩalɩŋ kala fa sɩ lɔlɔ a bɩra bɩ wuo vɛŋ, ba paaba sagɛ kakusuŋ nyuŋ, a kɛmba kaa mɩɩra mʋ ba nɩaa teeŋ Jeriko lɛ, tabal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Abɛ Tɩɩsɩŋ taŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ mɩɩra mʋ Samarɩa.
16Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Ahas tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa dɩ ʋ kʋ pɛ ʋ lɛ yuo ʋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ. 17Dɩ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa ma fa bɩra kʋ yuo dii Juda nɩaa a kɛsɛ ba dɔnsʋŋ. 18Bʋa-la tɩtɩa lɛ nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa ma kʋ yuo dii Juda tasɩ-la sɩ hɛ dundollu-la sɩ hɛ peelee bʋbʋɔŋ nyuŋ arɩ Juda wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ. Tasɩ-la ba fa sɩ yuo laa a hɔŋ ba lɛ nɛ: Bɛf Sɛmɛs, Aɩjalɔŋ, Gɛdɛrɔf, a pɛ Soko, Tɩmɩna, Gimizo arɩ tabiisi-la sɩ golliba. 19La TƖƖNA fa leŋe wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ deemba kala ŋaa Juda nɩaa lɛ a dɔgɩsɛba a tɩŋ kuoro Ahas wɩaa nɛ. Ʋ fa chaasa vɩa La TƖƖNA niiŋ nɛ, a leŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ pʋrɩgɛ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. 20Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria kuoro Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa kɔ Ahas teeŋ, ama ʋ mɩɩra kʋ hɛʋ wɩaa lɛ nɛ, ʋ bɩ ʋ lɛ pɛ. 21Ahas paa kɩaa dɔnsʋŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ, ʋ kuoru dɩa lɛ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩpaalaaraa dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, a ŋaa zile pɩ Asiiria kuoro, ama ŋɩɩ ha bɩ ʋ lɛ pɛ.
22Bʋa deeŋ lɛ wɩaa sɩ jʋʋ Ahas nɛ ʋ wasa vɩa La TƖƖNA niiŋ, a kɩɩ faafaa-la. 23Ʋ faa kpaarɛ Damasɩkʋs tɩmma-la sɩ yuo diiu vesiŋ nɛ, aŋ bɩɩnɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ lɛ a bʋl, “Asiiria tɩŋŋaa vesi-la nɛ pɛ ba kuoroo lɛ a yuo diimi. Mɩ jaŋ kpaarɛba, ŋ bɩ pɔ ba jaŋ pɛ mɩ ma lɛ.” Ama wɩɩŋ deeŋ nɛ wasa lɛrɛ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ kʋ hɛ Ahas arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala lɛ.
24Ahas paa Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ tɩntɩnnɩ kɩaa kala hɛ dɔŋɔ a ŋmoo yɛrɛ muno muno. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɔ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la, aŋ saa vʋɩ-kpaarɛ korunuŋ Jerusalɛm wombiee loŋgoru kala lɛ. 25Juda taŋ kala lɛ ʋ saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa ba kpʋkpaarɛ vesiŋ, a nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ a pɩpɩ vesi-la. Ʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA, ʋ naabalɩmaba Wɩa baanɩŋ chaasa sii ʋ nyuŋ woruŋ.
