nʋʋkala bɩ ʋ wuo kaa bɩrɩmɛ.
Ʋ yie ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩɩ chɛ nɛ.
14Ʋ jaŋ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ʋ ŋaa mɩ lɛ.
Wʋdosunuŋ yʋga ʋ kɛŋ.
15Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ fawʋllʋŋ faasa kɛmmɛ ʋ sɩpaaŋ.
Dɩ mɩ nɛ bɩɩnɛ wɩaa deemba kala, mɩ yie fɩfáʋ nɛ.
16Wɩa leŋe mɩ tʋɔbɩɩnaa lɛl nɛ.
La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna leŋe fawʋllʋŋ kɛmmɛ nɛ.
17Ama mɩ bɩ mɩ niiŋ tɔrɔ biriŋ-la kala sɩ tɔmɛ lɛ,
biriŋ-lim-la sɩ tɔ mɩ sɩaa.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna bɩ bʋa-la lɛ,
ʋ sɩ jaŋ dii nɩaa sarɩya lɩɩsa bil?
Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ jɩmʋ bee chɩchɛ ŋɩɩ tapʋlʋŋ, a bɩ ʋ ka na?
2Nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ kɛŋ tabɩa-la ba sɩ joŋo magɩlɛ tinteeŋ bʋa sʋrɩsɛ nɛ,
a gaa piesee pɛ ba kɩaa lɛ a dɩdaa.
3Ba kɛŋ biisime kakusuŋ laa nɛ.
Dɩ yo-haala nɩɩ chɛ chɩnnɩŋ,
ba laa ʋ nɛ-pɛrɩŋ, a bil ŋɩɩ bʋbʋɔŋ lɛ.
4Ba kiri nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ, dɩ ba sɩ́ wombiiŋ lɛ vɛŋ nɛ,
a fʋgɛ summoo kala sɩ hɛ tintee-la lɛ ba faa.
5Summoo deemba mɩɩra nagɛ bʋrʋmba nɛ,
a baaraa chɛ kʋdiilee tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ.
Tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ nɛ ba kuuni kʋdiilee a pɩpɩ ba biiriŋ.
6Ba yie ŋɩŋaa kɩaa bagɩsɩ-la sɩ tuo ba kɩaa lɛ nɛ,
a kukuuni kɩaa nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ lɛ.
7Dɩ taŋ nɛ bire, ba kɛŋ yarɩ-biree pɩŋ
a tɩŋ ba sɩ bɩ kʋŋ kɛnɛ dɩ ba kaa tɔ ba tɩtɩa.
Ba bɩ kʋŋkala kɛnɛ dɩ ba kaa tɔ waarɩŋ
dɩ ʋ sɩ́ ba kpʋ.
8Duonuŋ nɩɩ peelee nyuŋ lɩɩŋ leŋ ba kala chuoli.
Ba chɛ dɩjʋʋlaa ka, aŋ pɛllɛ bʋsʋŋ.
9Nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ kɛŋ biisiŋ bii-mulluŋ lɛrɛ kɛrɛ ba naamba yɩlɩŋ lɛ nɛ.
Ba kɛŋ summoo bii-mulluŋ laa nɛ chɩmɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ lɛ.
10Summoo sɩ bɩ gɛnnɩŋ kɛnɛ, kɛŋ yarɩ-biree vɩvɛŋ,
ba yie chʋŋ mɩaa vɩvɛŋ, aŋ kɛŋ losuŋ.
11Ba yie tugi olif nɛnɛɛ a lɩɩsɛ nʋʋŋ aŋ bɩ dii,
a chagɛ girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ ma, aŋ kɛŋ lɩɩnyʋasʋŋ.
12Nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ sʋʋ ka huuni nɛ tabal-la tʋɔŋ.
Nɩalɩŋ ma ba sɩ bolimo ŋmoo niiŋ a chɩchɛ nɩaa dɩ ba pɛ ba lɛ.
Ama Wɩa bɩ cheeriŋ joŋo pɩ nʋʋkala.
13Nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ hɛ nɩmɛ a bɩ pʋlʋmʋŋ ka chɛ.
Ba paala bɩ ʋ wɩaa jɩŋ, koo a tuto ʋ wombiiŋ.
14Dɩ leriŋ ha bire, nɩkpʋʋraa yie sii nɛ,
a kpʋ summoo arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ.
Tɩtaŋɩŋ ma, ba gɩgaa nɩaa kɩaa.
15Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ koo bachɔrʋŋ yie gbɩgbɛrɛ nɛ dɩ sɩaa dɩsɛ.
Ʋ yie bɩɩnɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ lɛ a bʋl, ‘Nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ namɛ,’
aŋ joŋ kʋa tɔ ʋ sɩaa.
16Tɩtaŋɩŋ gaaraa yie bori nɩaa dɩɩsɩŋ a jʋʋ gaa kɩaa,
ama dɩ taŋ nɛ pʋla, ba jʋʋ faa dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ.
Ba bɩ chɛ ba dɩ pʋlʋmʋŋ pɛ wɩɩkala.
17Birimiŋ lim nɛ ŋaa ba kala chʋchʋɔŋ.
Birimiŋ bɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛnɛ ba teeŋ.
18Ama nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ nagɛ fʋnfʋga nɛ aa delli lɩɩŋ nyuŋ.
Wɩa ŋmɩɛsɛ hɛ ba tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ,
ŋɩɩ leŋ ba bɩ ba girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ wuo mʋ.
19A nagɛ lɩmɩŋ arɩ hɩlɩŋ sɩ yie leŋ bʋrʋŋ sɩ tɔ lɛl ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ wʋbɔŋ ŋaaraa ma jaŋ lɛl sʋʋŋ bʋa lɛ.
20Lʋla-la lɛ ba sɩ to lɩɩ jaŋ yʋ ba wɩaa,
nanchʋɔlaa jaŋ diiba a nɩɩ sɩma.
Ba bɩra bɩ jaŋ liisi nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ deemba wɩaa,
ba boro tel nɛ a nagɛ tɩa.
21Ba kɛŋ hapɩraa arɩ haala-la sɩ bɩ biiriŋ kɛnɛ jɩlaa tuu nɛ,
a bɩ zile kɛnɛ mʋa ma yo-haalaa lɛ.
22Ama Wɩa jaŋ chei nɩduoruŋ deemba arɩ ʋ doluŋ.
Ba naga ba chɩna nɛ kpaŋkpaŋ,
ama ba bɩ yɩɛlaa kala kɛnɛ ba mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ.
23Wɩa jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ ba hɔŋ, wɩɩkala bɩ baa walɩmɛ.
Ama ʋʋ beŋ wɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩɩ ŋaa nɛ.
24Ba yɩrɩŋ yie sii mʋa nɛ, ʋ bɩ dieni, ka ba lɛl.
Ba yie sʋʋ nɛ ba hugiba a nagɛ ŋɩɩ ba sɩɩ ŋaa nʋʋkala lɛ.
Ba yie lɛl nɛ a nagɛ mɩɩ-nyusuŋ ba sɩ boro.
25Dɩ wɩaa deemba nɛ bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ ŋaa, kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo bʋl mɩɩ nyɩɛ nɛ,
a bʋl mɩ wʋbʋlaa ŋaa wʋpɛɩba nɛ?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Wɩalɩŋ Bɩlɩdad sɩ bʋla
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bɩlɩdad, Sʋa tɩɩna-la bʋl:
2“Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ a magɛ dɩ nʋʋkala fɩfáʋ.
Ʋ nɛ leŋe fɩɛlɩŋ hɛ ʋ jaŋ lɛ.
3Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo dɩɩsɛ ʋ laalɩyuoroo?
Kʋbɛɛ lɛ nɛ ʋ pʋlʋmʋŋ bɩ chaana hɩhɛ?
4Ɛɛ nɛ saa nuhuobiine jaŋ wuo ŋaa tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna Wɩa sɩpaaŋ?
Nʋʋ sɩ pɩŋ haala tʋɔŋ lɩɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa nɩpʋlaa?
5Dɩ chɛnɛ nɛ paala bɩ pʋlla,
dɩ chɛnwʋlaa ma bɩ pʋlla ʋ sɩaa lɛ,
6ɛɛ nɛ saa nuhuobiine sɩ nagɛ nanchʋɔlʋŋ jaŋ wuo ŋaa nɩpʋla ʋ teeŋ?
Nuhuobiine kala paala nagɛ vɛrɩŋ nɛ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Wɩalɩŋ Job ma bɩra sɩ bʋla a mʋ tɩgɛ Bɩlɩdad wʋbʋlaa lɛ
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Job ma bɩra bʋl:
2“Ŋ pɛ nʋʋ sɩ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ lɛ nɛ.
Ŋ laa nʋʋ sɩ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ ta nɛ.
3Ŋ bʋl wɩaa chagɩlɛ nʋʋ sɩ bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ kɛnɛ nɛ.
Ŋ dagɛ ŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ mɩ teeŋ.
4Kʋbɛɛ nɛ pɛ ŋ lɛ ŋ wuo bʋl wɩaa deemba?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ to ŋ lɛ a bʋl wɩaa deemba?
5Fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ sʋba ba chichel nɛ,
nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ lɩɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ bʋbʋɔŋ kala.
6Sʋʋŋ wɩɩkala bɩ faa Wɩa teeŋ,
Lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ pɩŋ kpɩlɩɩ nɛ ʋ teeŋ.
7Wɩa kɛŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ wɩa-nyuŋ a kaa jɛrɛ tɔ lee-la sɩ wuolo nɛ.
Ʋ leŋe tinteeŋ chɩŋ nɛ, ʋ bɩ kʋŋkala nyuŋ saga.
8Ʋ leŋe lɩɩŋ hɛ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa tʋɔŋ nɛ.
Ama lɩɩ-la yuŋuŋ bɩ leŋe duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaana-la yɛrɛ.
9Wɩa pilime tɔ chɛnɛ kala nɛ.
Ʋ leŋe ʋ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa jɛrɛ tɔ ʋ kala nɛ.
10Ʋ tuuri kʋŋ nɛ lɩɩŋ nyuŋ,
a magɩlɛ pʋlʋmʋŋ arɩ birimiŋ bʋa.
11Jebie-la sɩ chagɛ wɩa-nyuŋ kɩɩ jigise nɛ,
Wɩa sɩ kpɩa ba lɛ.
12Ʋ doluŋ lɛ, ʋ bugumi mʋgʋ-balɩŋ nɛ.
Ʋ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ, ʋ kaa keri mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tʋɔŋ kʋbɔŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Rahab muno muno.
13Ʋ wiese peliŋ nɛ leŋe wɩa-nyuŋ pʋllɛ.
Ʋ nɩsɩŋ ma nɛ ʋ kaa kpʋ dɩ-bɔŋ-la sɩ hɛ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tʋɔŋ.
14Wɩaa deemba kala mɩ sɩ bʋla, ŋaa ʋ doluŋ mʋa nɛ ʋ dagɛ ŋɩɩ.
Ʋ wɩaa mʋa kʋrʋ nɛ la nɩɩ ŋɩɩ.
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo jɩŋ Wɩa doluŋ maŋŋaa?”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Job ha bʋbʋl wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ kɛnɛ:
2“Mɩ ŋmɩɛsɛ Wɩa sɩ weye, nɩɩ-la sɩ vɩa dɩ ʋ bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ a pɛ mɩ lɛ,
La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna chaasa leŋ mɩ tʋɔŋ chei nɛ.
3Mɩ ha sɩ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ,
a kɛŋ wiese-la Wɩa sɩ joŋo hɛ mɩ lɛ,
4mɩ bɩ jaŋ suri mɩ niiŋ a bʋl wʋbɔŋ,
mɩ bɩ jaŋ nyɩsɛ nʋʋ ma.
5Mɩ bɩ jaŋ sɛɩ arɩ ma kɩaa sɩma nɛ,
mɩ jaŋ chɩŋ mɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ naaŋ lɛ
a kaa mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.
6Mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩ tʋɔpʋla,
mɩ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ʋ fori mɩ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.
Mɩ tʋɔbɩɩnaa bɩ jaŋ joŋ cheeriŋ pɩmɛ mɩ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ.
7A leŋ dɩ mɩ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nagɛ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ.
A leŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ chɩŋ mɩ lɛ
na hɛɛŋ a nagɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ.
8Dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ Wɩa ka to nɛ sʋba,
dɩ Wɩa nɛ laa ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ, bɛɛ kʋŋ yɩɛlaa nɛ ʋ kɛŋ?
9Dɩ wɩaa nɛ jʋʋ-ʋ dɩ ʋ yele pɩ Wɩa,
ma bɩɩna ʋ jaŋ jegile nɩɩ ʋ teeŋ?
10Ma bɩɩna ʋ jaŋ na tʋɔtɔrʋŋ La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna teeŋ?
Ʋ jaŋ wuo sʋsʋlʋ bʋa na-kala lɛɛ?
11Mɩ jaŋ dagɛma wɩaa a tɩgɛ Wɩa doluŋ lɛ.
Mɩ bɩ jaŋ kɛŋ La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna wombiiŋ wɩaa faama.
12Ma tɩtɩa kala na wɩɩŋ deeŋ nɛ.
Bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ ma bʋbʋl wʋpɛɩ deemba kala?
13Wɩalɩŋ Wɩa sɩ kpaa bil nɩbɔmʋŋ lɛ nɛ ŋ-la,
wɩalɩŋ yuo-hɛɛrɛ sɩ jaŋ laa La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna teeŋ nɛ ŋ-la:
14Ʋ biiriŋ cho dɩ ba yʋga magɛ ɛɛ ma kala, laalɩŋ nɛ jaŋ dɛrɛ ba kala.
Ʋ doho nɩaa jaŋ sʋʋ losuŋ.
15Nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ paala fori laalɩŋ lɛ, nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ jaŋ kpʋba.
Ba yo-haalaa bɩ jaŋ yel ba lɛ.
16Dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ paala kɛŋ dʋnɩa moribiee kala,
dɩ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ ma chʋɔrɛ a nagɛ chʋrʋŋ,
17tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa nɛ jaŋ laalɛ ʋ gɛnnɩ-la kala.
Nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye nɛ jaŋ kɛŋ ʋ moribie-la kala kpaa dɔŋɔ.
18Dɩɩsɩ-la kala nɩbɔmʋŋ sɩ saa nagɛ badɛrɛ ŋmɛsɩŋ nɛ,
ba nagɛ palɩŋ nɩa sɩ hɛ a hɔnɔ pʋpɔ kɩaa nɛ.
19Ʋ pɩŋ dʋa tʋɔŋ nɛ, ama ʋ bɩra bɩ jaŋ na ŋɩɩ.
Ʋ jaŋ susuri ʋ sɩaa dɩ dʋa-la kala lɛlɛ.
20Fawʋllʋŋ jaŋ jʋʋ-ʋ a nagɛ lɩɩŋ sɩ tɔ leriŋ.
Pel-duoŋ jaŋ joŋu a kaa viiri tɩtaŋɩŋ.
21Peliŋ jaŋ lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a kʋ joŋu viiri.
Ʋ jaŋ joŋu ʋ dɩa-la lɛ a kaa viiri.
22Pel-la jaŋ tuu ʋ lɛ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ fá ʋ nenige,
ka dɩ ʋ nɩnɛrɩgɛ dɩ ʋ fori pel-la doluŋ lɛ a fá.
23Nɩbɔmʋŋ jaŋ fɩfá, ka dɩ pel-la tuu ʋ lɛ,
a ŋaa goŋ kiru ta dɩ ʋ lɩɩ ʋ dɩjʋʋlʋŋ.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
1Leriŋ hɛ nɩmɛ ba sɩɩ huri hɔpʋla,
leriŋ ma hɛ nɩmɛ ba sɩ yie joŋ sɛlɩmɛ chɔ a lɩɩsɛ sɛlɩŋ-bɩnɩŋ.
2Tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ ba yie huro lɩɩsɛ hɔɔŋ,
ba yie du jigiŋ nɛ a lɩɩsɛ hɔɔ-fɩaŋ.
3Nuhuobiine yie kɛŋ chaanɩŋ nɛ a tuu biriŋ-lim tʋɔŋ,
a chɛ tuu tinteeŋ bʋbʋɔŋ,
a huroo chɛ jigiŋ birimiŋ tʋɔŋ.
4Ba yie huro tuu dɩ-bolie nɛ a hɛ bʋa-naaŋ,
lere-la nɩaa sɩ bɩ vɛnɛɛ mʋ.
Ba yie to ŋmɛsɩŋ nyuŋ nɛ a lieŋe tuu bʋa-la.
5Tinteeŋ nyuŋ nɛ kʋdiilee wʋwaa,
ama ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ ba yie hɛ nyiniŋ dɩ tabɩa-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ sʋʋ dɩ ba yɛrɛ.
6Bʋŋ lɛ nɛ ba yie lɩɩsɛ tabɩɩ-tʋlɩa-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ safɩya,
hagɩlɩ-biee ma kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ.
7Kachuu kala bɩ wombii-la sɩ faa bʋa-la lɛ jɩŋ.
Duu kala sɩɩŋ ha bɩ lee-la na.
8Baga kʋŋkala naaŋ ha bɩ lee-la nʋɔsa.
Naachigi kala ha bɩ lee-la gɔllɔ.
9Nuhuobiine nɛ giri tabɩɩ-duoru-la kala,
a huri peelee a tuu nyɩɩsɛ ba gentisiŋ lɛ.
10Ba yie lɔsɛ bʋa-naasɩŋ bʋŋ lɛ,
a na kʋzɔmɔ-la kala sɩ hɛ ʋ lɛ.
11Nuhuobiine yie chɛ tuu yi fuonuŋ lɩɩŋ dɩ-lɩɩlɩŋ kala,
a kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ sɩ faa kaa kʋ lɩɩ pʋlʋmʋŋ.
12Ama nɩɩ nɛ nʋʋ jaŋ wuo na wʋjɩmɩŋ?
Nɩɩ nɛ wɩaa sɩaa jɩmɩŋ hɛ?
13Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo naʋ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ.
Nuhuobiinee bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ yuŋuŋ maŋŋaa wuo jɩŋ.
14Fuoŋ sɩ, ‘Wʋjɩmɩŋ tuo mɩ lɛ.’
Mʋgʋ-balɩŋ ma sɩ, ‘Ʋ tuo mɩ teeŋ.’
15Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ yɔbʋ,
koo a kɛŋ hɔpʋla magɩsɛ ʋ yalɩŋ.
16Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ a yɔbʋ.
Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ tabɩɩ-tʋlɩa-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ ɔnɩs koo safɩya a yɔbʋ.
17Wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ kɛŋ yuŋuŋ a kɩɩ sɛlɩmɛ koo bʋ-sɩaa.
Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo joŋ kpɩɛra-la ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ ŋaa a yɔbʋ.
18Sɛlɩmɛ kɛŋ yuŋuŋ a kɩɩ tabɩɩ-tʋlɩa-la
ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ kora koo jasɩpa koo rubi.
19Tabɩɩ-tʋlɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ topas sɩ hɛ Kus tinteeŋ lɛ bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ wuo magɛ,
ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ yɔbʋ.
20Nɩɩ nɛ saa wʋjɩmɩŋ lɩɩ?
Nɩɩ nɛ wɩaa sɩaa jɩmɩŋ hɛ?
21Ʋ faa nɛ kʋŋkala sɩ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ teeŋ,
ʋ paala faa nɛ diibiisiŋ sɩɩ zaarɛ wɩa-nyuŋ teeŋ.
22Lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ arɩ sʋʋŋ sɩ,
‘La ma nɩɩ ba sɩ nɛ a tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ.’
23Wɩa nɛ jɩŋ ʋ wombiiŋ,
ʋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ jɩŋ lee-la ʋ sɩɩ jʋʋ.
24Ʋʋ beŋ dʋnɩa dɩdɛrɩŋ kala nɛ,
a nɩna kʋŋ na-kala sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ lɛ.
25Ʋ nɛ leŋe peliŋ kɛŋ doluŋ,
aŋ dagɛ ŋɩɩ duonuŋ sɩ maga dɩ ʋ nɩɩ.
26Wɩa nɩɩ dagɛ duonuŋ wombie-la sɩ maga dɩ ʋ to,
aa dagɛ taŋ lɩgɩsɩŋ ma ʋ wɛnɩŋ.
27Ʋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa deemba kala dɛrɛ nɛ, ʋ beŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ, aŋ bɛsɛ ʋ lɛ.
Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ magɩsʋ na, a leŋ ʋ chɩŋ woruŋ.
28Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ nuhuobiine,
‘Dɩ ŋ nɩɩ fá mɩ-na ma Tɩɩna, wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ,
dɩ ŋ nɛ vɩa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ,
ŋ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa nɛ ŋɩɩ.’ ”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Job ha bʋbʋl wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ kɛnɛ:
2“Mɩ tʋɔŋ fa jaŋ tɔrɛ dɩ mɩ nɛ bɩra na chɛnsɩ-la sɩ bala,
tapʋlɩa-la lɛ Wɩa fa sɩɩ beŋ mɩ nyuŋ.
3Ʋ chaanɩŋ fa yie chaanɛ mɩ nyuŋ nɛ,
ʋ pʋlʋmʋŋ laa mɩ sɩpaaŋ birimiŋ tʋɔŋ mɩ vɩvɛŋ.
4Mɩ bapʋɔsʋŋ lɛ,
Wɩa fa ŋaa mɩ nandɔŋ-fɩaŋ nɛ,
a ŋaa wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ pɩ mɩ dɩ mɩ dɩa nɩaa.
5La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna fa ha hɛ mɩ teeŋ nɛ,
mɩ biiriŋ gollimi a chu.
6Bʋa-la lɛ mɩ nɛsɩŋ fa kɛŋ nɛ-yɩlɩŋ nɛ woruŋ,
ba yie tugu mɩ olif nʋʋŋ bʋŋ nyuŋ ʋ pɩpɛllɛ leriŋ kala.
7Mɩ fa yie mʋ la tabalɩŋ boi-baalɩŋ niiŋ,
mɩ dɩ sɩpaalaara-la sɩ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ hɔŋ.
8Bapʋɔsaa yie sʋrɩsɛ nɛ aŋ ka leriŋ pɩmɛ,
nɩhɩasɩŋ sii chɩŋ ba naasɩŋ nyuŋ,
9sɩpaalaaraa leŋ wʋbʋlʋŋ,
aŋ tɔrɛ ba niiŋ,
10nɩbalaa ŋaa fʋɩɩ mɩ sɩpaaŋ,
ba niiŋ jʋʋ kpʋrʋŋ.
11Nʋʋkala nɛ nɩɩ mɩ wɩaa, ʋ yie bʋl wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ a tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ.
Nɩaa nɛ namɛ, ba yie bɛsɛ mɩ lɛ nɛ,
12bɛɛ wɩaa dɩ summoo nɛ bunso a chɩchɛ pɛnɩŋ, mɩ yie laaba ta nɛ,
aa pɛ biisinsiŋ ma sɩ bɩ nɩaa kɛnɛ dɩ ba pɛ ba lɛ.
13Nɩalɩŋ naaŋ sɩɩ lieŋi sʋʋŋ bʋa lɛ yie bɛsɛ mɩ lɛ nɛ.
Mɩ yie leŋ yo-haalaa kɛŋ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ nɛ.
14Tʋɔpʋla nagɛ gɛrɩŋ nɛ mɩ joŋo laalɛ.
Wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ fa ŋaa mɩ gɛrɩŋ arɩ mɩ nyu-bɛlɛ.
15Mɩ nɛ fa ŋaa nyʋlɩmaa sɩaa,
a ŋaa gbɛrɩgɛɛ ma naasɩŋ.
16Mɩ nɛ fa ŋaa nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ nyɩmma,
a bʋla laa nʋhʋɔraa ma tɩta sarɩya dɩ-diiliŋ.
17Mɩ yie chei nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ doluŋ nɛ,
aŋ lorigo laa nɩaa ta ba niiŋ lɛ.
18Mɩ fa bɩɩna mɩ tapʋlaa jaŋ yʋgɛ a nagɛ hagɩlɩ-biee,
dɩ mɩ sʋʋ mɩ tɩtɩa dɩa lɛ.
19Mɩ fa nagɛ tɩa nɛ, mɩ naapoloo tuu tɩgɛ lɩɩŋ lɛ,
nyalɩŋ ma nyala hɩhɛ mɩ naakelee lɛ tɩtaŋ na-kala.
20Mɩ yɩrɩŋ sɩ sii woruŋ,
mɩ doluŋ ma pʋŋa pɩpɛ.
21Nɩaa fa jegilee nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ nɛ woruŋ,
a kpil dɩgɩlaa gbɩgbɛrɛ dɩ ba nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ jaŋ dagɛba.
22Dɩ mɩ nɛ bʋl wɩaa dɛrɛ, nʋʋkala bɩra bɩ niiŋ ka suri.
Mɩ wʋbʋlaa faa jʋʋ ba dɩgɩlaa nɛ woruŋ.
23Ba yie gbɛrɛ dɩ ba nɩɩ mɩ wʋbʋlaa a nagɛ nɩaa sɩɩ gbɛrɛ duonuŋ nɛ,
a nɩɩba woruŋ a nagɛ duoŋ-puso sɩ leŋe tinteeŋ vɔgɛ lɩɩŋ.
24Dɩ ba yɩɛlaa nɛ lɛlɛ wɩɩ lɛ, dɩ mɩ ŋaa sʋsʋrɩ wɩaa ba teeŋ,
ŋɩɩ yie leŋ ba nyuŋ bɩra nyaasɛ nɛ.
25Mɩ-na nɩɩ dagɛba wombii-la sɩ maga dɩ ba to, a nagɛ ba kuoro.
Ba tʋɔŋ mɩ fa nagɛ kuoro sɩ kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo vɩvɛŋ nɛ.
Mɩ fa nagɛ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ nyagɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ yel bɔyɛ nɛ.

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1Ama lɛɛlɛ mɩ ŋaa mɔmɩɩ nɛ,
nɩalɩŋ mɩ ma sɩ hɩa mʋmɔmmɛ,
nɩalɩŋ nyɩmmaba mɩ sɩ paala beŋ dɩ ba bɩ maga
dɩ mɩ jomba hɛ vasɩ-la sɩɩ to mɩ piesee harɩŋ.
2Ba doluŋ fa bɩ bʋbʋa kala kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ,
ba doluŋ kala fa dɛrɛ nɛ.
3Ba fa bɩ kʋŋkala kɛnɛ, losuŋ yie leŋ
ba gɔllɔ bɩbaarɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ tɩtaŋɩŋ a chɩchɛ kɩaa,
leree sɩ bɩ kʋŋkala kɛnɛ.
4Ba yie pʋʋrɛ pɩpaa-haarɩŋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ a chɩchaŋ,
a churi kaala ma a didii.
5Ba fa kiriba ta ba dɔnsʋŋ tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ nɛ,
ba yie kpɩa ba lɛ a nagɛ ba ŋaa gaaraa nɛ.
6Ba fʋgɛba tuu hɛ fuonaa hɩlaa tʋɔŋ,
a jʋjʋʋ bʋ-bʋɔsʋŋ arɩ tinteeŋ bʋɔsʋŋ.
7Ba yie pɩŋ tɩɩ-pugunuŋ bʋbʋɔŋ aa yel a nagɛ kakusuŋ,
a gu dɔŋɔ lɛ chɛ-tiiŋ tʋɔŋ.
8Ba ŋaa nɩtɔɔnɩ nɛ, ba paala bɩ yɩrɩŋ kɛnɛ,
ba kiriba ta tintee-la lɛ nɛ.
9Ama lɛɛlɛ ba biiriŋ nɛ kɛmmɛ hɛ yɩɩlɩŋ a sisieri mɩ lɛ.
Mɩ bɩrɩmɛ kʋtɔɔ a guoli ba tʋɔŋ.
10Ba kɩkɩsɛ dɩ ba kpagɛmɛ,
ba bɩ fá dɩ ba tʋ nantʋɔrʋŋ hɛ mɩ sɩaa lɛ.
11Lɛɛlɛ Wɩa sɩ laa mɩ ba-laala, ka mɩɩ na hɛɛŋ,
ba gennee ŋaa sakɔsʋ wɩaa mɩ sɩpaaŋ.
12Nɩaa deemba sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ-kala kɛnɛ sii chɩŋ mɩ lɛ nɛ.
Ba hɛ bɛrɩsɩŋ nɛ mɩ dɩ-vɛnɩŋ,
a bil wombiee ba sɩ jaŋ to cheimi.
13Ba chei mɩ wombiiŋ nɛ,
a wasa leŋ mɩ wʋjʋʋlaa pʋŋa pɩpɛ,
ka nʋʋ ma tuo dɩ ʋ kiri, dɩ ba sɩ́ ŋɩɩ ŋaa.
14Ba gbu lɩɩ kɔ mɩ lɛ, a nagɛ laalɩyuoroo sɩ bori jebiiŋ jʋʋ nɛ,
a gulimi mɩ nyuŋ.
15Fawʋllʋŋ chaasa jʋʋmɛ nɛ kɩŋkɛŋ,
mɩ yɩrɩŋ kala lɛl a nagɛ peliŋ sɩ joŋ kʋa.
Mɩ dʋa ma kala lɛl a nagɛ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanɩŋ sɩ lɛlɛ.
16Lɛɛlɛ mɩ mɩɩsɩŋ ka mʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ nɛ,
hɛɛŋ tapʋlaa puumi nɛ.
17Tɩtaŋɩŋ, mɩ haŋgbelee yie wʋwɩɩ nɛ,
a bibieri a bɩ dɛrɛ.
18Wɩa kɛŋ ʋ dol-bala-la a kɛŋ mɩ gɛrɩŋ baŋŋaa lɛ nɛ,
a lɛrɛ hɛ mɩ baŋŋaa a kaa mɩlɩmɛ.
19Ʋ jommi yuo hɛ vʋchɔɔŋ lɛ nɛ,
mɩ kala bʋgɛ a nagɛ tʋɔrʋŋ.
20Mɩ Wɩa, mɩ ŋmoo niiŋ pɩŋ nɛ, ama ŋ bɩ wɩɩ bʋla,
Mɩ kʋ chɩŋ ŋ sɩpaaŋ nɛ, ama ŋ bɩ mɩ bee na.
21Ŋ chaasa dɔgɩsɛmɛ arɩ tʋɔhɛɛŋ nɛ,
ŋ kɛŋ ŋ doluŋ kala nɛ a wʋrɩgɛmɛ.
22Ŋ kɛmmɛ chʋʋlɛ nɛ, a leŋ peliŋ jommi,
a leŋ duoŋ-peliŋ kɛmmɛ vivilli.
23Mɩ jɩma ŋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ sʋʋ,
a mʋ lee-la nʋʋkala sɩ jaŋ mʋ.
24Nʋʋkala bɩ puwuol ka ŋmoo,
dɩ ʋ nɛ bunso chɩchɛ dɩ ba pɛ ʋ lɛ.
25Mɩ bɩ yele pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ jʋʋ wɩaa?
Mɩ tʋɔŋ bɩ summoo wɩaa cheyee?
26Ama mɩ sɩ yɩɛla chɩchɛ wʋzɔmʋŋ, wʋbɔmʋŋ nɛ mɩ mɩɩra na.
Mɩ sɩ bee chɩchɛ pʋlʋmʋŋ, birimiŋ nɛ mɩ mɩɩra nɩna.
27Mɩ chʋɩŋ kpʋkpɛrɛ a bɩ leŋ,
hɛɛŋ puumi tapʋlɩɩ kala.
28Mɩ gɔllɔɔ baarɛ birimiŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ, pʋlʋmʋŋ lɛ dee.
Mɩ chɩŋ nɩaa tʋɔŋ nɛ a yele chɩchɛ dɩ ba pɛ mɩ lɛ.
29Jolluŋ nɛ mɩɩra bɩrɩmɛ mɩ naambiiriŋ, hajaaŋkuŋkumba ma bɩrɩmɛ mɩ pɛ-jʋʋraa.
30Mɩ yaraa kala biri, a fɩfɩsɛ,
mɩ yaraa kala lɩŋ a wʋwɩɩ.
31Ba kɛŋ mɩ cheŋ bɩrɩmɛ yo-yelli kʋŋ nɛ lɛɛlɛ,
mɩ ŋmʋlʋŋ ma dɔmɔ nagɛ nɩaa sɩɩ ŋmoo niiŋ.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1Mɩ bil niiŋ nɛ,
arɩ mɩ bɩ jaŋ beŋ hantolibie a hɩɛnʋ.
2Kpaal bɛɛ nɛ nuhuobiine kɛŋ Wɩa sɩ chugili la lɛ teeŋ?
Ʋ time nɛ bɛɛ La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna sɩ hɛ wɩa-nyuŋ teeŋ?
3Ʋ jaŋ chei nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ,
aŋ joŋ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ hɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ.
4Ʋʋ na wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩɩ ŋaa nɛ,
a jɩŋ mɩ naavɛnɛɛ ma kala.
5Dɩ mɩ nɛ fa to wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ harɩŋ,
koo a nyɩnyɩsɛ nɩaa,
6ŋɩɩ-na leŋ dɩ Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ ba kala magɩsɛ na.
Ʋ jaŋ jɩŋ dɩ mɩ bɩ wʋcheeli kala kɛnɛ.
7Dɩ mɩ nɛ yeŋŋe Wɩa wombiiŋ lɛ,
dɩ mɩ nɛ joŋ mɩ tʋɔbɩɩnaa hɛ mɩ sɩaa wʋchooloo lɛ,
koo dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ dɔŋ,
8ŋɩɩ-na a leŋ dɩ nɩaa dii mɩ suoluŋ,
aŋ kɛŋ mɩ kʋpɛrɛɛ churo ta.
9Dɩ mɩ nɛ joŋ mɩ tʋɔbɩɩnaa hɛ mɩ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna haala lɛ,
a faa dɩ-jalɩŋ gbɛrʋ boiŋ niiŋ,
10ŋɩɩ-na a leŋ dɩ mɩ haala mɩɩra bɩrɩmɛ nʋʋ dɔŋ haal,
dɩ baalaa kɛnʋ pɩpɩŋ.
11Dɩ mɩ nɛ fa ŋaa wɩaa deemba, ŋɩɩ fa jaŋ kɛŋ hɩɩsɩŋ,
ʋ fa jaŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba diimi sarɩya.
12Ŋɩɩ fa jaŋ nagɛ nyiniŋ a dii mɩ kɩaa chei,
a dii mɩ kʋpɛrɛɛ kala buru.
13Dɩ mɩ tɩntɩnnaa baalaa arɩ haalaa nɛ kɛŋ wɩɩ tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ a bʋl,
mɩ yie joŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ a to ba lɛ.
14Dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa, dɩ Wɩa nɛ pɩɛsɛmɛ?
Wʋbɛɛ ba nɛ mɩ jaŋ bʋl dɩ ʋ nɩɩ diimi sarɩya?
15Wɩa sɩ ŋaamɛ, ʋ nɛ ŋaa mɩ tɩntɩnna-la ma.
Ʋ nɛ fa ŋaa la kala hɛ la naamba luoruŋ lɛ.
16Mɩ ha bɩ vɩa dɩ mɩ pɛ summoo lɛ dɩ ba na ba kʋchɛɛlɛ,
dɩ yo-haalaa nɛ chaarɛ sɩaa pɛ mɩ lɛ, mɩ yie pɛ ba lɛ nɛ.
17Mɩ dʋndʋŋa bɩ mɩ kɩaa ka dii,
mɩ yie kpaa pɩ biisinsiŋ nɛ.
18Mɩ bapʋɔsʋŋ kala lɛ nɛ mɩ dɩɛsɛba, a nagɛ nyɩmma sɩ yie dɩɛsɛ ʋ bie ŋɩɩ,
ba sɩ lʋlmɛ kala lɛ nɛ mɩ pɛ yo-haalaa lɛ.
19Dɩ mɩ nɛ fa na nʋʋ sɩ bɩ gɛnnɩŋ kɛnɛ,
koo nʋʋ sɩ bɩ ʋ tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ nɛ bɩ gɛrɩŋ kɛnɛ dɩ ʋ kaa tɔ waarɩŋ,
20mɩ yie joŋ gɛrɩŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ mɩ piesee pʋnaa ŋaa a pʋʋ nɛ.
Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yie bɛsɛ mɩ lɛ arɩ ba tʋɔŋ kala.
21Dɩ mɩ nɛ ha lɩɩsɛ mɩ nɩsɩŋ a ŋaa wɩɩ bii-sime lɛ,
a tɩŋ mɩ sɩ jɩma mɩ kɛŋ harɩchɩnnaa sarɩya dɩ-diiliŋ wɩaa,
22ŋɩɩ-na, leŋ dɩ mɩ vaaŋ chɔlɔ tel,
a leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩsaa boro lɩɩ mɩ nasusugusuŋ lɛ.
23Mɩ bɩ sɛɩ dɩ mɩ ŋaa wʋdosunuŋ deemba.
Mɩɩ fá Wɩa sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ dɩ ʋ sɩ́ mɩ chei.
24Mɩ bɩ mɩ yɩɛlaa joŋo hɛ sɛlɩmɛ lɛ,
koo a joŋ sɛlɩmɛ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ, ʋ nɛ ŋaa mɩ wɩɩkala.
25Mɩ bɩ jʋɔsa a tɩŋ mɩ dʋa sɩ faasa yʋgɛ wɩaa,
koo a tɩŋ mɩ nɩsɩŋ sɩ kɛnɛ wɩaa.
26Mɩ ha bɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ tʋla bene,
koo a beŋ chɛnɛ sɩ zɔmɔ a vɩvɛŋ a dɛnnɛba.
27Mɩ tʋɔbɩɩnaa ha bɩ mɩ yige hɛ mɩ lʋara zilba kʋŋ,
mɩ ha bɩ ba kʋŋ kpirime chʋɔlɛ.
28Dɩ mɩ nɛ fa ŋaa wɩaa deemba, ba ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ a magɛ ba diimi sarɩya.
Ŋɩɩ fa jaŋ dagɛ arɩ mɩ bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ Wɩa sɩ hɛ ʋ jaŋ lɛ teeŋ.
29Mɩ tʋɔŋ ha maachie bɩ tɔrɔ a tɩŋ mɩ dʋndɔmɔ sɩɩ na hɛɛŋ wɩaa,
koo a jʋɔsɛ a tɩŋ wɩaa sɩ jʋʋ-ʋ wɩaa.
30Mɩ ha bɩ mɩ niiŋ suro a bʋl wʋbɔŋ
a kalɩbɛ hɛ mɩ dʋndɔmɔ lɛ a chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ.
31Nɩalɩŋ kala sɩɩ tɩŋ mɩ dɩa lɛ jɩma
arɩ mɩ yie cheme laa nʋhʋɔrʋ kala sɩ kɔ mɩ dɩa nɛ.
32Mɩ yie kɛŋ nʋhʋɔraa kʋ jʋʋ mɩ dɩa nɛ, mɩ bɩ leŋe ba pɩpɩŋ wombiiŋ lɛ.
Mɩ dɩa suro nɛ a pɩ wɛŋ-vɛnnɛɛ kala.
33Mɩ bɩ mɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ kaa fɩfaa a nagɛ nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ sɩɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.
Mɩ ha bɩ mɩ wʋcheeli kaa faa.
34Mɩ yie bɩ wɩalɩŋ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ bʋl a mʋ tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ ka fá,
koo a tɩŋ ŋɩɩ wɩaa a tɔrɛ mɩ niiŋ aŋ gʋrɛ dɩa lɛ.
35Mɩ fa jaŋ cho dɩ nʋʋ jegile nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩɩ bʋl.
Mɩ ŋmɩɛsa arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩba nɛ.
Mɩɩ gbɛrɛ nɛ dɩ La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna bʋl wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ kɛnɛ pɩmɛ.
Mɩ fa jaŋ cho dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ joŋ cheeriŋ pɩpɩmɛ ŋmʋnsɛ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ bɩɩna dɩ mɩ cheye a hɛ kʋŋ lɛ bil.
36Mɩ fa jaŋ chaasa lɩɩ chɩŋ a joŋ wɩalɩŋ laalɛ mɩ vaaŋ lɛ,
a jomba chu mɩ nyuŋ lɛ a nagɛ kuoru nyunchuulo.
37Mɩ fa jaŋ dagɛ wɩɩ na-kala mɩ sɩ ŋaa a pʋ.
Mɩ fa jaŋ kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa mʋ ʋ sɩpaaŋ a nagɛ kuoro.
38Dɩ mɩ nɛ gaa pɩpɛrɛ tintee-la lɛ mɩ sɩɩ pɛrʋ,
a gɩrɩma laaʋ ʋ tɩŋŋaa teeŋ,
39dɩ mɩ nɩɩ dii tintee-la kɩaa
ka ʋ tɩŋŋaa pɩŋ losuŋ,
40ŋɩɩ-na, leŋ dɩ sɔsʋŋ nyʋ lee-la, ka dɩ mɛmpɛ vɩa,
leŋ dɩ yaŋ nyʋ, ka dɩ nyonso ma vɩa.”
Job wʋbʋlaa dɩdɛrɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Wɩalɩŋ Elihu ma sɩ bʋla
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ baala-la batori leŋ wɩalɩŋ ba fa sɩ bʋlaa pɩ Job, bɛɛ wɩaa Job fa laa ʋ tɩtɩa dii arɩ ʋ kɛŋ tʋɔpʋla nɛ. 2Ama Barakɛl nanʋala Elihu sɩ lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bus, aŋ ŋaa Ram dɩa nɩaa dɔŋɔ, ʋ faasa na baanɩŋ Job nyuŋ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩɩna arɩ ʋ nɛ kɛŋ tʋɔpʋla a kɩɩ Wɩa. 3Ʋ fa bɩra na baanɩŋ Job nandɔsʋ-la batori ma nyuŋ nɛ bɛɛ wɩaa, ba bɩ wuo dagɛ wɩɩ-la Job sɩ ŋaa chei, aŋ joŋ cheeriŋ pʋ. 4Elihu fa gbɛrɛ nɛ ba kala bʋl wɩaa dɛrɛ, ka ʋ-na bʋl wɩaa pɩ Job, bɛɛ wɩaa ba fa hɩaʋ nɛ.
5Ama Elihu sɩ na dɩ Job nandɔsʋ-la batori bɩra bɩ wɩɩ kɛnɛ dɩ ba bʋl, ʋ baanɩŋ sii ba nyuŋ.
6Ŋɩɩ nɛ Barakɛl nanʋala Elihu sɩ ŋaa Bus tɩɩna bʋl:
“Mɩ ŋaa bii-bie nɛ, ka ma ŋaa nɩhɩasɛ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ fa fɩfá dɩ mɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ jɩma a pɩma.
7Mɩ bɩɩna ma nɛ sɩ ŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ ʋ magɛ dɩ ma nɛ bʋl wɩaa,
ma nɛ sɩ chʋa mʋa, ʋ maga ma dagɛ nɩaa wʋjɩmɩŋ.
8Ama dɩma-la La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna sɩ joŋo hɛ nuhuobiine lɛ,
ʋ nɛ leŋe la jɩjɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa.
9Hɩasɩŋ dee bɩ leŋe nɩaa jɩjɩŋ wɩaa.
Nɩhɩasɩŋ dʋndʋŋa dee bɩ wɩalɩŋ sɩ ŋaa ba bʋa lɛ jɩŋ.
10Ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ sɩ, má jegili mɩ teeŋ.
Mɩ maa chɛ mɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ jɩma nɛ a pɩma.
11Mɩ gbɛrɛ nɛ ka ma kala bʋl wɩaa,
mɩ jegile nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ ma sɩ kaa lɛrɛ,
a loo chɩchɛ wɩaa dɩ ma bʋl.
12Mɩ tɔrɛ mɩ niiŋ nɛ a jegile nɩɩ ma teeŋ woruŋ.
Ama ma kʋŋkala bɩ wuo leŋ Job jɩŋ arɩ ʋ kɩaa bɩ sɩŋ.
Ma kʋŋkala bɩ ʋ kaalɛrɛ-la sɩaa chaara pʋ.
13Má sɩ́ bʋl arɩ ma na wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ,
má leŋ dɩ Wɩa nɛ bʋl arɩ Job kɩaa bɩ sɩŋ, nuhuobiine dee.
14Mɩ teeŋ dee Job fa bʋbʋl wɩalɩŋ,
ŋɩɩ wɩaa, mɩ bɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩaa ʋ teeŋ a nagɛ ŋɩɩ ma sɩ kɛŋ wɩaa lɛrɛ.
15Ma kala niiŋ maa nɛ, ma bɩra bɩ wɩɩ kɛnɛ dɩ ma bʋl,
wɩaa dɛrɛ ma niiŋ lɛ.
16Ʋ saa maga dɩ mɩ bɩra hɔnɔ gbɩgbɛrɛ bɛɛ nɛ,
lɛɛlɛ ba niiŋ sɩ jʋʋ kpʋrʋŋ ŋ-la?
17Mɩ ma jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ kɛnɛ,
mɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la mɩ ma sɩ jɩma.
18Mɩ tʋɔŋ kala nɛ suo arɩ wɩaa.
Dɩma-la sɩ hɛ mɩ lɛ ka fʋgɛmɛ nɛ dɩ mɩ bʋl wɩaa.
19Mɩ kala pʋŋa nɛ arɩ wɩaa a nagɛ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ sɩ su kɔlɩbɔ a lɩɩ tɩta,
a bɩra nagɛ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ puru-falɩŋ a chɩchɛ ʋ pɔsɛ.
20Ʋ maga mɩ bʋl wɩaa nɛ aŋ wiesi,
Ʋ maga mɩ suri mɩ niiŋ nɛ a bʋl wɩaa.
21Mɩ bɩ jaŋ fá nʋʋkala sɩɩŋ,
koo a bʋl nii-sɩŋ wɩaa a mʋ tɩgɛ nʋʋkala lɛ.
22Mɩ bɩ nii-sɩŋ wɩaa bʋlʋŋ jɩŋ,
dɩ mɩ nɛ fa jɩmba, Wɩa sɩ ŋaamɛ fa bɩ jaŋ dieni aŋ kpʋmɛ.

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1Ama lɛɛlɛ Job, jegili mɩ teeŋ,
jegile nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ jaŋ bʋl.
2Mɩ ŋaa siri nɛ dɩ mɩ suri mɩ niiŋ a bʋl wɩaa.
Wɩalɩŋ sugi mɩ niiŋ lɛ nɛ a chɩchɛ dɩ ba lɩɩ.
3Tʋɔpʋla nɛ mɩɩ chɛ mɩ kaa bʋl wɩaa deemba.
Wʋtɩtɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ jɩma nɛ mɩɩ chɛ dɩ mɩ bʋl.
4Wɩa Dɩma nɛ ʋ kaa ŋaamɛ.
La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna nɛ wiese hɛ mɩ lɛ, mɩ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.
5Dɩ ŋ nɛ jaŋ wuo laa wɩɩ bʋl mɩ teeŋ,
kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ dɩ la cheŋ dɔŋɔ.
6Mɩ dɩŋ kala nagɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ Wɩa sɩpaaŋ.
Chʋrʋŋ nɛ ʋ kaa mɛmɩ ma.
7Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ŋ fɩfámɛ,
a leŋ dɩ mɩ wʋbʋlaa yuŋŋie pɩŋ.
8Ama ŋ bʋl wɩaa mɩ nɩɩ nɛ,
wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ bʋla mɩ nɩɩ nɛ ŋ-la, ŋ sɩ:
9‘Mɩ ŋaa nɩpʋla nɛ,
mɩ bɩ wʋbɔŋ kɛnɛ, mɩ bɩ wɩɩ ŋaa chei.
10Arɩ ŋɩɩ kala, ka Wɩa na dɩ mɩ chei wɩɩ nɛ,
ʋ jommi mɩ ŋaa ʋ dʋndɔŋ.
11Ʋ vɔɔ mɩ naasɩŋ nɛ arɩ chɔrʋmɔɔ,
a bibeŋ mɩ naavɛnɛɛ kala.’
12Ama mɩ bʋlaa pɩŋ, wɩaa deemba kala lɛ ŋ kɩaa bɩ sɩŋ.
Wɩa nɛ yʋga a kɩɩ nuhuobiiŋ kala.
13Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ gʋgʋrɩmɛ wɩaa ʋ teeŋ,
arɩ ʋ bɩ nuhuobiine wʋbʋlɩɩ kala jegilee nɩɩ?
14Wɩa yie to wombii dɔŋ a bʋl wɩaa, a bɩra to wombiiŋ dɔŋɔ ma bʋl wɩaa.
Nuhuobiine-na bɩ ŋɩɩ wuo jɩjɩŋ.
15Ʋ yie wuo to duosoo lɛ tɩtaŋɩŋ nɩaa sɩ pɩna,
koo nʋʋ sɩ na wɩaa arɩ duosoo tʋɔŋ
nɩaa sɩ pɩŋ doŋ.
16Ʋ jaŋ bɩra wuo bʋl wɩaa hɛ ba dɩgɩlaa lɛ,
a joŋ fawʋllʋŋ hɛ ba lɛ, a chɩchagɩlɛba.
17Ʋ yie to ŋɩɩ lɛ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ nuhuobiine bɩrɩma lɩɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ lɛ,
a lɩɩsʋ babiibal wɩaa lɛ.
18Ʋ yie ŋaa ŋɩɩ dɩ ʋ lɩɩsʋ sʋʋŋ lɛ nɛ,
dɩ ʋ sɩ́ sʋʋŋ bʋa tuu.
19Ʋ jaŋ wuo chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ nuhuobiine tʋra kɩɩ, a joŋ nyanyalaa hɛ ʋ lɛ ʋ pɩŋ,
ʋ leŋ hɛɛŋ jʋʋ-ʋ woruŋ.
20Ŋɩɩ leŋ ʋ kʋdii-chooloo sʋsʋɔrɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ,
ʋ kʋdii-sɩŋŋaa kɛŋ nyɛsɩŋ ʋ teeŋ.
21Ʋ yaraa kala dɛrɛ aŋ ka,
haŋgbelee ba nyɩɩsɛ nyɩɩsɛ.
22Ʋ naaŋ lilieŋi sʋʋŋ bʋa lɛ,
ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ wɩɩkala nagɛ lɛlɩɩ.
23Ama dɩ Wɩa tɩndaarʋ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ a chɩŋ ʋ harɩŋ,
a ŋaa Wɩa tɩndaaraa bʋɩ fii tʋɔŋ kʋbala a jʋʋ wɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ,
a dagʋ wɩɩ-la sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa,
24a wuo fá ʋ nenige a bʋl, ‘Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ʋ tuu sʋʋŋ bʋa,
mɩ na kʋ-la mɩ sɩ jaŋ kaa time laa nɛ,’
25ŋɩɩ-na ʋ yaraa jaŋ mɩɩra zɔŋ a nagɛ bii-bie,
a bɩra nagɛ ʋ bapʋɔsʋŋ bʋa lɛ.
26Ʋ chʋɔlɛ Wɩa nɛ ŋɩɩ, ʋ laa ʋ sʋla,
ʋ na Wɩa nɛ, a jʋɔsa ŋaa goŋ,
Wɩa leŋ ʋ bɩra chɩŋ ʋ tʋɔpʋla naaŋ lɛ.
27Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ ʋ jaŋ kʋ bʋla pɩ nɩaa,
‘Mɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ a kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ a kaa bɩrɩmɛ.
Ama Wɩa joŋo chɛmɛ nɛ.
28Ʋ laamɛ ta nɛ, mɩ bɩ sʋʋŋ bʋa jʋa.
Mɩ jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ a nɩɩ pʋlʋmʋŋ sɩma.’
29Wɩa yie ŋaa wɩaa deemba kala nuhuobiine lɛ
a mʋ yi naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa koo butori,
30dɩ ʋ lɩɩsʋ sʋʋŋ bʋa lɛ,
dɩ ʋ wuo kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ a nɩɩ sɩma.
31Job, kpil dɩgɩlɩŋ a jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ,
tɔrɛ ŋ niiŋ, ka dɩ mɩ bʋl wɩaa.
32Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ wɩɩ dɩ ŋ bʋl, bʋl dɩ mɩ nɩɩ,
mɩɩ chɛ mɩ na dɩ ŋ kɩaa sɩma nɛ.
33Ama dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩ wɩɩ kɛnɛ, ŋɩɩ-na jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ.
Tɔrɛ ŋ niiŋ ka dɩ mɩ dagɩŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Elihu bʋl:
2“Má nɩɩ mɩ ma wʋbʋlaa, ma-na wʋjɩnna,
ma jegili mɩ teeŋ, ma nɩalɩŋ sɩ gʋnnɛ wɩaa yʋgɛ.
3Nandelimiŋ sɩ jɩŋ kʋsɩmɩŋ ŋɩɩ woruŋ,
dɩgɩlɩŋ maa nɩɩ wʋsɩŋŋaa ŋɩɩ nɛ.
4Má leŋ dɩ la vʋʋrɛ a joŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ,
má leŋ dɩ la hɛ dɔŋɔ a gʋnnɛ wɩɩ-la sɩ zɔmɔ.
5Job bʋla, ‘Mɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye,
ama Wɩa kɛŋ mɩ kʋsɩŋŋaa laa nɛ,
6arɩ mɩ kɩaa sɩ sɩma ma kala,
ʋ ha jommi arɩ mɩ ŋaa wʋnyɩɛrʋ nɛ.
Mɩ ha chaasaa na hɛɛŋ nɛ arɩ mɩ sɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye ma kala.’
7Nuhuobiiŋ bɛɛ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ a nagɛ Job,
nɩa sɩ joŋ hɩɩsɩŋ chɔmɔ nyʋa a nagɛ lɩɩŋ?
8Ʋ dɩ wʋbɔŋ ŋaaraa nɛ pɛ wɩaa,
ʋ dɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ nɩɩ vɛŋ.
9Ʋ sɩ, ‘Nuhuobiine bɩ jaŋ na nyʋʋrɩ kala,
dɩ ʋ nɩɩ nɛrɩgɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩaa a tɔrɛ Wɩa tʋɔŋ.’
10Ŋɩɩ wɩaa ma nɩalɩŋ sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa, má jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ.
Nʋʋkala jɩma Wɩa bɩ wʋbɔŋ kala ka ŋaa,
La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna bɩ wʋlɔrʋ kala ka ŋaa.
11Ʋ yie joŋ nuhuobiine wʋŋaalaa chɩmɩŋ timu nɛ,
a timu a magɛ ŋɩɩ ʋ mɛlɛ sɩ naga.
12Wɩa bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ kala,
La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna bɩ jaŋ gbaa tɔ wʋtɩtɩɩ lɛ.
13Kʋbɛɛ nɛ lɩɩsʋ dɩ ʋ bibeŋ tinteeŋ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ hɛʋ dɩ ʋ bibeŋ dʋnɩa kala?
14Dɩ Wɩa nɛ fa bɩɩna dɩ ʋ kɛŋ wiese-la,
ʋ sɩ joŋo hɛ la lɛ kaa lɩɩsɛ,
15nuhuobiinee kala fa jaŋ sʋʋ,
a bɩra bɩrɩmɛ hagɩla.
16Dɩ ŋ nɛ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa, nɩɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ,
jegile nɩɩ wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩɩ bʋl:
17Nʋʋ sɩ bɛrɛ wʋtɩtɩɩ, ʋ jaŋ wuo beŋ nɩaa?
Ŋ jaŋ wuo chei La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna sɩ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ yɩrɩŋ?
18Ʋ nɛ yie bʋla pɩ kuoroo, ‘Ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,’
aŋ bʋla pɩ nɩbalaa ma, ‘Ma ŋaa nɩbɔmɔ nɛ.’
19Wɩa nɛ ŋaa la kala, ʋ bɩ sɩpaalaaraa kaa pɔrɔ bil ba dʋndʋŋ,
ʋ bɩ kɩaa tɩŋŋaa ma nɛ cho a kɩɩ summoo.
20Ba kala yie guu sʋʋ nɛ,
nɩaa yie vɛsɛ naasɩŋ a sʋʋ tɩta-siesee,
babiibalaa yie sʋʋ dɩ nʋʋ bɩ ba kpʋa.
21Wɩa sɩaa hɛ nuhuobiinee wombiee lɛ nɛ,
ʋ yie na naakiel kala ba sɩ joŋo nɛ.
22Ʋ teeŋ biriŋ kala tuo, biriŋ-lim kala tuo
lee-la wʋbɔŋ ŋaaraa sɩ jaŋ wuo faa.
23Wɩa bɩra bɩ maga dɩ ʋ hɛ tapʋlɩɩ,
a kɛŋ nuhuobiine kɔ ʋ sɩpaaŋ a dii ʋ sarɩya.
24Ʋ bɩ nʋʋ pɩɛsa aŋ lɩɩsɛ sɩpaalaarɩ-duoruŋ tɩta,
aŋ joŋ nɩaa hɩhɛ ba leree.
25Ʋ jɩŋ ba wʋŋaalaa nɛ,
ʋ yie kiriba ba dɩchɩnaa, a cheiba tɩtaŋɩŋ.
26Ʋ yie tɩŋ ba wʋbɔmɔ-la wɩaa a dɔgɩsɛba,
lee-la nʋʋkala sɩ bɩ jaŋ naba,
27bɛɛ wɩaa ba vɩa dɩ ba tou nɛ,
a bɩ ʋ wombiee kʋŋkala kaa tɩtɩŋ.
28Ba wʋŋaalaa leŋe summoo ŋmoo niiŋ Wɩa sɩpaaŋ nɛ,
ʋ nɩɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ nii-ŋmobo.
29Ama dɩ Wɩa nɛ tɔrɛ ʋ niiŋ, kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo joŋ cheeriŋ pʋ?
Dɩ ʋ nɛ kɛŋ ʋ sɩaa faa, kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo naʋ?
Ʋ nɩɩ beŋ nuhuobiinee arɩ tinteyee kala,
30a pɔ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ Wɩa ka fá sɩ́ kuoruŋ dii,
a dʋdɔgɩsɛ ba nɩaa.
31Dɩ nuhuobiiŋ nɛ bʋl ŋ-la a pɩ Wɩa:
‘Mɩ cheye nɛ, mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩ chei.
32Dagɛmɛ wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ bɩ na,
dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ, mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ ŋaa.’
33Ŋ sɩ vɩa wɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ ŋaa,
ɛɛ nɛ ŋ-na saa chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ chɛ a pɩŋ?
Ŋ nɛ maga ŋŋ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la pɩ ŋ tɩtɩa, mɩ-na dee.
Bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ jɩma pɩmɛ.
34Nɩalɩŋ sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa bʋla,
wʋjɩnna-la sɩ nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ bʋla pɩmɛ:
35‘Job bɩ wɩaa sɩaa jɩŋ aŋ bʋbʋl,
wʋjɩmɩŋ tuo ʋ wʋbʋlaa lɛ.
36Mɩ fa cho dɩ ba magɩsɛ Job nɛ a mʋ yi dɩdɛrɩŋ,
bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ wʋbʋlaa nagɛ nɩbɔŋ nɛ.
37Ʋ vɩa Wɩa nɛ, a pɛ wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa lɛ.
Ʋ sieri la lɛ nɛ,
a bʋl wɩaa yʋgɛ la tʋɔŋ a chei Wɩa yɩrɩŋ.’ ”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Elihu bɩra bʋl:
2“Ŋ bɩɩna wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋ sɩ bʋla ŋaa ʋ bʋa lɛ nɛ koo?
Ŋ sɩ sɩ, ‘Wɩa sɩpaaŋ, mɩ bɩ wɩɩkala cheye.’
3Ama ŋ pɩɛsa, ‘Dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa wɩaa tɔrɛ Wɩa tʋɔŋ,
bɛɛ kʋŋ nyʋʋrɩ nɛ mɩ jaŋ na?
Dɩ mɩ nɛ bɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaa, bɛɛ kʋŋ nyʋʋrɩ nɛ mɩ jaŋ na?’
4Mɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩaa dagɛ ŋ dɩ
ŋ nandɔsʋ-la kala sɩ hɛ ŋ teeŋ.
5Beŋ wɩa-nyuŋ na,
beŋ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa sɩ hɛ wɩa-nyuŋ dɩ-bolii.
6Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ, ŋɩɩ jaŋ ŋaa Wɩa bɛɛ?
Dɩ ŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ yʋga, ŋɩɩ jaŋ ŋaaʋ bɛɛ?
7Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna, wʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ, ŋ ŋaa pʋpʋʋ?
Bɛɛ nɛ ʋ lɩlaa ŋ teeŋ?
8Ŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ka chei ŋ nuhuobiiŋ dɔŋɔ dʋndʋŋa nɛ,
ŋ tʋɔpʋla ma pɩpɛ ŋ nuhuobiiŋ dɔŋɔ dʋndʋŋa lɛ.
9Nɩaa yie ŋmuŋmoo niiŋ a tɩŋ nɩaa sɩ nyagɛba a bil wɩaa nɛ,
ba yie sʋl dɩ ba laaba ta nɩduoruŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.
10Ama nʋʋkala bɩ pɩɛsɛ, ‘Nɩɩ nɛ Wɩa, mɩ ŋɩŋaara hɛ,
nɩɩ-la sɩ yie pɩla yɩɩlaa la yɩɩ dɩ leriŋ nɛ bire tɔla,
11nɩɩ-la sɩ dagɛla wɩaa,
la jɩŋ wɩaa kɩɩ baga kɩaa.’
12Nɩaa yie yɩrʋ, ka ʋ tɔrɛ ʋ niiŋ,
a tɩŋ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ sɩɩ-duoŋ wɩaa.
13Wʋtɩtɩɩ, Wɩa bɩ ba yɩrɩ pɛɩ-la ba sɩ yie yɩrʋ ka nɩɩ,
La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna bɩ ba yɩrɩ pɛɩ-la ka jegili.
14Ɛɛ nɛ saa ʋ jaŋ paala jegili ŋ teeŋ,
ŋ sɩ sɩ ŋ bɩ ʋ ka na,
dɩ ŋ wɩaa kala hɛ ʋ sɩpaaŋ nɛ,
dɩ ŋ jaŋ gbɛrʋ?
15Ŋ bɩra bʋla arɩ ʋ bɩ baanɩŋ na a dʋdɔgɩsɛ nɩaa,
ʋ sɩpaaŋ tuo wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ.
16Job wʋbʋlɩa-la kala ŋaa wʋpɛɩba nɛ,
ʋ wʋbʋl daŋ-la kala bɩ wʋjɩmɩɩ kɛnɛ.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1Elihu ha bɩra bʋla:
2“Dii kenyiri mʋa a pɩmɛ, ka dɩ mɩ bʋl wɩɩ dagɩŋ.
Mɩ ha kɛŋ wɩɩ nɛ aa chɛ mɩ chɩŋ Wɩa naasɩŋ lɛ a bʋl.
3Mɩ jɩŋ wʋdaŋ daŋ nɛ,
mɩ jaŋ dagɛ ŋɩɩ mɩ ŋɩŋaara sɩ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ.
4Wʋtɩtɩɩ, wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩɩ bʋl bɩ wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ ŋaa,
nʋʋ sɩ chaasa jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa nɛ hɛ ŋ teeŋ.
5Wɩa kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ woruŋ, ama ʋ bɩ nuhuobiine kaa ŋmuŋmoo gbɛɛŋ,
ʋ doluŋ yʋga, wɩɩkala tuo ʋ bɩ ʋ sɩaa jɩŋ.
6Ʋ bɩ leŋe nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ hɩhɛ ba mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ,
ama ʋ yie leŋ summoo nɩna wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba na nɛ.
7Ʋ bɩ ʋ sɩaa ka lɩɩsɛ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa lɛ,
ʋ yie leŋ ba hɔŋ kuoru kpasɩnɩŋ lɛ nɛ a nagɛ kuoroo,
ʋ leŋ ba kɛŋ doluŋ nɩaa zizilba a kaa mʋ wuu.
8Ama dɩ ba nɛ vɔɔ nɩaa arɩ chɔrʋmɔɔ,
dɩ ba nɩna hɛɛŋ a tɩŋ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa wɩaa,
9Wɩa yie dagɛ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa a pɩba nɛ,
a leŋ ba jɩŋ arɩ ba dagɛ ba tɩtɩa nɛ a ŋaa wʋbɔŋ.
10Ʋ yie leŋ ba jegili wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa a kɛmba tʋraa kɩɩ nɛ,
aŋ bʋla pɩba dɩ ba bɩrɩma lɩɩ ba wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ.
11Dɩ ba nɛ sɛɩ ʋ niiŋ a tou,
tapʋl-kaana-la ba sɩ jaŋ hɛ ba mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, ba jaŋ dʋa woruŋ,
ba jaŋ kɛŋ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ jɩ-kaana-la ba sɩ jaŋ hɛ ba mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ.
12Ama dɩ ba nɛ bɩ jegile nɩɩ,
ba jaŋ kpʋba laalɩŋ lɛ, dɩ ba sʋʋ nɩyaarɛ sʋʋ.
13Nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ Wɩa ka fá bɩ leŋe ba baanɩŋ fɩfɩɛlɛ.
Wɩa nɛ paala vɔɔba bil ma, ba bɩ yele sʋsʋlʋ dɩ ʋ pɛ ba lɛ.
14Ba yie sʋʋ dɩ ba ha pʋɔsa,
hɩɩsɛ wɩaa nɛ yie leŋ ba mɩɩsɩŋ dɛrɛ.
15Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ na hɛɛŋ, ʋ yie laaba ta ba hɛɛŋ lɛ nɛ,
ba wʋjʋʋlaa lɛ nɛ ʋ yie suri ba sɩaa.
16Wɩa ka lɩɩsɛ ŋ ma wʋjʋʋlaa lɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ,
dɩ ʋ joŋuŋ ta pʋlʋŋ-jaala lɛ, ŋ gʋgɔllɛ ŋ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ,
dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ kʋdii sɩŋŋaa gbaarɩŋ.
17Ama lɛɛlɛ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ sarɩya nɛ ba joŋo didii ŋ lɛ,
sarɩya arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ-la ba sɩ jaŋ joŋo to ba lɛ nɛ kɔ ŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ.
18Fɩɛlɛ ŋ sɩaa dɩ nʋʋ sɩ́ kɩaa kaa nyɩsɩŋ,
sɩ́ leŋe dɩ kpalaa kɛnɩŋ mɩɩrɛ wʋtɩtɩɩ harɩŋ.
19Ŋ dʋa arɩ wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ hɛ ŋ doluŋ kala
a ŋɩŋaa bɩ jaŋ wuo lɩɩsɩŋ hɛɛŋ lɛ.
20Sɩ́ chɩchɛ dɩ taŋ biri dɩ ŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ,
bʋa-la lɛ nɛ ba jaŋ chei nɩaa.
21Fɩɛlɛ ŋ sɩaa a sɩ́ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ harɩŋ to,
ba wɩaa nɛ tɩɩ Wɩa joŋ hɛɛŋ hɛ ŋ lɛ.
22Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ kʋŋkala lɛ,
kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo dagɛ wɩaa a nagʋ?
23Kʋbɛɛ nɛ wuo dagʋ wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa,
koo a bʋla pʋ, ‘Ŋ bɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ woruŋ ŋaa?’
24Ŋ ma liisi wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa a lɔllʋ,
wɩalɩŋ wɩaa nɛ nɩaa yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a dɛnnʋ.
25Nuhuobiinee kala nɛ naba,
ba chɩŋ dɩ-bolii nɛ aŋ bibemba.
26Wʋtɩtɩɩ, Wɩa kɛŋ doluŋ, nuhuobiinee bɩ ʋ magɩsɩŋ jɩŋ.
Nʋʋkala bɩ ʋ jɩsɩŋ niiŋ wuo dagɛ.
27Wɩa nɛ yie leŋ lɩɩŋ lɩɩ tinteeŋ a jɩl wɩa-nyuŋ,
a mɩɩra bɩrɩmɛ duonuŋ a kʋ tuu.
28Lɩɩ-la nɛ yie lɩɩ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa lɛ a kʋ tuu ŋɩɩ,
a leŋ nɩaa kala chuoli.
29Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ ŋaa a leŋ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa jɛrɛ tɔ leriŋ,
koo ŋɩɩ duonuŋ sɩ yie kpɩa a lɩɩ wɩa-nyuŋ?
30Ʋ yie leŋ taŋ lɩgɩsɛ a pʋllɛ wɩa-nyuŋ kala nɛ,
aŋ ka mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tʋɔŋ ha biri.
31Wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa bibeŋ nuhuobiinee nɛ ŋɩɩ,
a chɛ kʋdiilee yʋgɛ a pɩpɩba.
32Ʋ yie kɛŋ taŋ lɩgɩsɩna-la kala hɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ,
a leŋ ʋ mʋ yagɛ lee-la ʋ sɩɩ chɛ.
33Duonuŋ nɛ yie kpɩa a leŋ nɩaa jɩŋ duoŋ-peliŋ ka kɔ nɛ.
Nɛsɩŋ ma yie paala jɩŋ arɩ ʋʋ kɔ nɛ.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1Ŋ-la yie leŋ mɩ bɔyɛ joŋ,
a yɩyagɛ.
2Má jegile nɩɩ, má jegile nɩɩ Wɩa yikoro,
arɩ goŋ-la sɩɩ lɩɩ ʋ niiŋ lɛ.
3Ʋ yie leŋ taŋ lɩgɩsɛ a cheŋ wɩa-nyuŋ kala,
a mʋ yagɛ dʋnɩa sɛmɛ na-kala.
4Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ ʋ yikoro ma yie dɔŋ,
ʋ kpɩa goŋ arɩ ʋ yikori-balɩŋ.
Dɩ taŋ nɛ lɩgɩsa,
ʋ yie dɔmɔ to nɛ.
5Dɩ Wɩa nɛ kpɩa goŋ, wʋkpuŋkperisiŋ yie ŋaa nɛ,
ʋ yie ŋaa wʋbalaa la sɩ bɩ ba sɩaa wuo jɩŋ.
6Ʋ yie bʋla pɩ bʋrʋŋ, ‘Tɔ dʋnɩa lɛ,’
a bʋla pɩ duonuŋ ma, ‘Faasa nɩɩ.’
7Ʋ yie ŋaa ŋɩɩ nuhuobiinee kala leŋ ba tɩntɩŋŋaa,
a wuo jɩŋ ŋɩɩ Wɩa sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa.
8Baga kɩaa ma mʋ ba dɩ-pɩnaa,
a pɩŋ ba bugoo lɛ.
9Duoŋ-pel-duoŋ yie tɔɔ lɩɩ ʋ dɩ-lɩɩlɩŋ,
peliŋ lɛrɛ waarɩŋ kɔ.
10Wɩa wiese yie leŋ lɩɩŋ dɛrɩmɛ,
lɩɩŋ sɩ pɩna a yʋgɛ gulimi.
11Ʋ yie leŋ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa kala su arɩ fɩɛlɩŋ,
a leŋ taŋ lɩlɩgɩsɛ ba lɛ.
12Ʋ leŋ ba vivilli
dʋnɩa kala lɛ,
a ŋɩŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ daga.
13Bʋa dɔŋɔ Wɩa yie leŋ duonuŋ nɩɩ, a lɩgɩsɛ, a kpɩa a dɔgɩsɛ nɩaa,
bʋa dɔŋɔ ma ʋ leŋ duonuŋ nɩɩ dɩ ʋ dagɛ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ cho dʋnɩa nɩaa.
14Job, jegile nɩɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ:
Tɔrɛ ŋ niiŋ aŋ kɛŋ wʋkpuŋkperisi-la Wɩa sɩ ŋaa a bɩɩna na.
15Ŋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ Wɩa sɩ kɛŋ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa tɩtɩŋ,
arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ yie leŋ taŋ lɩlɩgɩsɛ nɛɛ?
16Ŋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa sɩ ŋaa vɩvɛŋ wɩa-nyuŋ a bɩ kʋŋkala nyuŋ sagaa?
Wʋkpuŋkperisiŋ deemba Wɩa sɩ ŋaa arɩ ʋ jɩma, ŋ jɩmba nɛɛ?
17Leriŋ yie lɩŋ ŋ susuoli nɛ,
dɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ peliŋ nɛ kɔ a leŋ leriŋ kala ŋaa siuu.
18Ŋ jaŋ wuo pɛ ʋ lɛ a ŋaa wɩa-nyuŋ a leŋ ʋ jɛrɛ,
a kɛŋ doluŋ a nagɛ hɔɔŋ sɩɩ tʋl?
19Dagɛla wɩɩ-la la sɩ jaŋ bʋla pʋ,
la tʋɔbɩɩnaa lɛlɛ nɛ, la-na bɩ wɩɩ kɛnɛ dɩ la bʋla pʋ.
20Mɩ bɩ jaŋ chɩchɛ mɩ dɩ Wɩa bʋl wɩaa.
Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ jaŋ pʋ wombiiŋ dɩ ʋ cheimi?
21Nʋʋkala bɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ wuo beŋ,
ʋ sɩ yie faasa chaanɛ ŋɩɩ wɩa-nyuŋ,
dɩ peliŋ nɛ paa duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa kala aŋ kaʋ.
22Wɩa lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ nɛ a kʋkɔ, a tʋtʋl a nagɛ sɛlɩmɛ.
Ʋ sɩɩ kɔ ŋɩɩ ʋ tʋla-la leŋ fawʋllʋŋ kɛnla.
23La Tɩɩna doluŋ kala Tɩɩna kɩɩ la sɩ jaŋ kpagʋ nɛ, ʋ doluŋ yʋga.
Ʋ sɩ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ arɩ tʋɔpʋla yʋga ŋɩɩ, ʋ bɩ nʋʋkala nyaga bibil.
24Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ nɩaa zizilu,
nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩɩna ba jɩŋ wɩaa, ʋ yie yʋ ba wɩaa nɛ.”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks
From Out of a Storm
1From out of a storm,
the Lord said to Job:
2Why do you talk so much
when you know so little?
3Now get ready to face me!
Can you answer
the questions I ask?
4How did I lay the foundation
for the earth?
Were you there?
5Doubtless you know who decided
its length and width.
6What supports the foundation?
Who placed the cornerstone,
7 while morning stars sang,
and angels rejoiced?
8 When the ocean was born,
I set its boundaries
9and wrapped it in blankets
of thickest fog.
10Then I built a wall around it,
locked the gates, 11and said,
“Your powerful waves stop here!
They can go no farther.”
Did You Ever Tell the Sun To Rise?
12Did you ever tell the sun to rise?
And did it obey?
13Did it take hold of the earth
and shake out the wicked
like dust from a rug?
14Early dawn outlines the hills
like stitches on clothing
or sketches on clay.
15But its light is too much
for those who are evil,
and their power is broken.
16Job, have you ever walked
on the ocean floor?
17Have you seen the gate
to the world of the dead?
18And how large is the earth?
Tell me, if you know!
19Where is the home of light,
and where does darkness live?
20Can you lead them home?
21I'm certain you must be able to,
since you were already born
when I created everything.
22Have you been to the places
where I keep snow and hail,
23until I use them to punish
and conquer nations?
24From where does lightning leap,
or the east wind blow?
25Who carves out a path
for thunderstorms?
Who sends torrents of rain
26on empty deserts
where no one lives?
27Rain that changes barren land
to meadows green with grass.
28Who is the father of the dew
and of the rain?
29Who gives birth to the sleet
and the frost
30that fall in winter,
when streams and lakes
freeze solid as a rock?
Can You Arrange Stars?
31 Can you arrange stars in groups
such as Orion
and the Pleiades?
32Do you control the stars
or set in place the Big Dipper
and the Little Dipper?
33Do you know the laws
that govern the heavens,
and can you make them rule
the earth?
34Can you order the clouds
to send a downpour,
35or will lightning flash
at your command?
36Did you teach birds to know
that rain or floods
are on their way?
37Can you count the clouds
or pour out their water
38on the dry, lumpy soil?
39When lions are hungry,
do you help them hunt?
40Do you send an animal
into their den?
41And when starving young ravens
cry out to me for food,
do you satisfy their hunger?
translation_text:
La Tɩɩna bʋl wɩaa a pɩ Job
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA to duoŋ-peliŋ tʋɔŋ a bʋl wɩaa pɩ Job. Ʋ sɩ,
2“Kʋbɛɛ nɛ kaŋ dɩ ŋ pɩɛsɛ wɩaa a mʋ tɩgɛ mɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ lɛ,
aa bʋl wɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ wʋjɩŋ wɩaa ŋaa?
3Kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ a nagɛ baal,
mɩ jaŋ pɩɛsɩŋ wɩaa, dɩ ŋ chaarɛ ba sɩaa pɩmɛ.
4Bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩɩ bil dʋnɩa gentine, nɩɩ nɛ ŋ hɛ?
Dɩ ŋ nɛ jɩma, bʋla pɩmɛ.
5Kʋbɛɛ nɛ daga ŋɩɩ ʋ jalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ʋ magɛ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ tuuri ʋ bʋa a golli?
6Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ chagɛ dʋnɩa kɩɩ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ bil ʋ gʋnaa jebiee,
7ka chɛnwʋlaa yɩɩ yɩɩlaa hɛ dɔŋɔ chɛɛ-la sɩɩpʋʋraa,
mɩ tɩndaaraa ma ŋaa goŋ arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ?
8Kʋbɛɛ nɛ kɛrɛ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ lɩɩŋ bil,
dɩ ʋ sɩ́ gbu lɩɩ?
9Mɩ nɛ leŋe duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa tɔ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ,
a leŋ birimiŋ lim tɔʋ.
10Mɩ nɛ tuuri mʋgʋ-balɩŋ bʋa,
a kɛrʋ kɩɩ a nagɛ ba sɩ kɛŋ doloo arɩ borusuŋ kɛrɛ kʋa.
11Mɩ nɛ bʋla pɩ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ, ‘Ŋ jaŋ wuo kʋ magɛ ŋ-la nɛ, aŋ sɩ́ ŋɩɩ lɛ kielu,
daha nɛ ŋ lɩɩ-peliŋ doluŋ maga dɩ ʋ chɩna magɛ.’
12Job, ŋ ha wuo dagɛ chʋchʋɔŋ, wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa?
Ŋ ha wuo leŋ sɩɩpʋʋraa kɔɔ?
13Ŋ ha maachie wuo bʋla pɩ wɩɩhɛyɛ pʋlʋmʋŋ dɩ ʋ chaana mʋ yi dʋnɩa dɩdɛrɩŋ,
a kɛŋ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ ta ba kʋ lɩɩ ba dɩ-faalaa?
14Wɩɩ-muluŋ sɩ nyagaa lɩɩ pʋlʋmʋŋ yie leŋ dundolluŋ arɩ fuonaasɩŋ lɩɩ chaanɛ nɛ, a ŋminsi,
a nagɛ ba sɩ kɛŋ gɛrɩŋ kpeŋ ʋ kɛŋ higisiŋ.
15Ba vɔŋ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ pʋlʋmʋŋ nɛ,
ba sɩɩ dii dol-la nɩaa lɛ dɛrɛ.
16Ŋ ha tuu mʋgʋ-balɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ a mʋ yi ʋ lɩɩ-bul sɩaa leriŋ?
Ŋ ha vɛŋ tintee-la sɩ hɛ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ?
17Nʋʋ ha kɛŋ sʋʋŋ boi-baalaa dagɩŋ?
Ŋ ha na lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ dɩ-bine-la boi-baalaa?
18Ŋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ dʋnɩa sɩ jalɩa magɛɛ?
Dɩ ŋ nɛ jɩŋ wɩaa deemba kala, bʋla pɩmɛ.
19Ŋ jɩŋ wombii-la pʋlʋmʋŋ sɩ to kʋkɔ nɛɛ?
Nɩɩ nɛ birimiŋ jʋjʋʋ?
20Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛmba mʋ ba leree?
Ŋ jɩŋ wombie-la sɩɩ mʋ ba dɩjʋʋlaa nɛɛ?
21Ŋ jɩŋ wɩaa deemba kala nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa bʋa-la lɛ dɩ ba lʋlʋŋ,
ŋ hɛ nɩmɛ nɛ ka mɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa.
22Ŋ ha jʋʋ dɩɩsɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ joŋ bʋrʋŋ bil,
koo a na dɩɩsɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ joŋ duoŋ-tabɩaa bil?
23Mɩ joŋ kɩaa deemba a bile gbɛrɛ wʋjʋʋlaa tapʋlʋŋ nɛ,
tapʋlɩɩ-la laalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ sii.
24Wombii bɛɛ nɩɩ mʋ lee-la duonuŋ sɩ yie lɩgɩsa lɩɩ a pɩsɛ?
Koo lee-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ peliŋ sɩ lɩɩ pɩsɛ dʋnɩa lɛ?
25Kʋbɛɛ nɛ bil libisiŋ pɩ duonuŋ ʋ to nɩnɩɩ
koo a bil wombiiŋ pɩ duoŋ-peliŋ?
26Kʋbɛɛ nɛ yie leŋ duonuŋ nɩɩ tinteeŋ lee-la nʋʋkala sɩ tuo,
tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ nʋʋ sɩ tuo,
27tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la vɔgɛ lɩɩŋ,
a leŋ yaŋ nyʋ lee-la?
28Duonuŋ kɛŋ nyɩmma nɛɛ?
Nyalɩŋ nyɩmma nɛ kʋbɛɛ?
29Kʋbɛɛ lʋla lɛ nɛ lɩɩ-gulimoo lɩɩ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ lʋl waarɩŋ sɩ lɩɩ wɩa-nyuŋ,
30a yie leŋ lɩɩŋ gulimi a dolie nagɛ tabɩɩŋ,
mʋgʋ-balɩŋ lɩɩŋ nyuŋ ma kala dɛrɩmɛ?
31Ŋ jaŋ wuo vɔɔ chɛnwʋla-la sɩ chige chɩŋ wɩa-nyuŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ
arɩ chɛnwʋla-la sɩ chige chɩŋ wɩa-nyuŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a hɛ dɔŋɔ?
32Ŋ jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ chɛnwʋlaa kʋ lɩɩ bʋa-la lɛ sɩ maga dɩ ba kʋ lɩɩ,
koo a dagɛ chɛnwʋla-la sɩ chige chɩŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ arɩ kɩalɩŋ sɩ chige chɩŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ ŋɩɩ sɩ maga ba ŋaa?
33Ŋ jɩŋ wombie-la ba sɩ bile pɩ wɩa-nyuŋ kɩaa dɩ ba tuto nɛɛ?
Ŋ jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ wombie-la chɩŋ dʋnɩa ma lɛɛ?
34Ŋ jaŋ wuo kpɩa duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa lɛ,
a leŋ dɩ duonuŋ nɩɩ hɛ ŋ lɛ dɩ ŋ kala chuoli?
35Ŋ jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ taŋ lɩgɩsɛ joŋ ʋ wombiiŋ?
Ba yie wuo bʋla pɩŋ, arɩ daha nɛ la hɛɛ?
36Kʋbɛɛ nɛ joŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ hɩhɛ nɩaa nyuŋ lɛ,
a leŋ ba jɩjɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa?
37Kʋbɛɛ nɛ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a jaŋ wuo dɩɩsɛ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanaa?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ lɛ lɩɩŋ sɩ hɛ
chɩŋ wɩa-nyuŋ kpil dɩ duonuŋ nɩɩ,
38dɩ tinteeŋ nɛ faasa hɩl
a kala kpal?
39Ŋ nɛ chɛ kʋdiilee pɩ naachigi nɩɩŋ,
naachigi biiriŋ dii vɔgɛ,
40dɩ ba hɛ ba dɩ-pɩnaa,
koo a faa tɩɩ-lugunuŋ tʋɔŋ ba bugoo lɛɛ?
41Kʋbɛɛ nɛ yie chɛ kʋdiilee pɩ gɩlɩŋgaamba,
dɩ losuŋ nɛ kɛmba baa baarɛ,
koo dɩ ba biiriŋ nɛ yelee chɛ kʋdiilee mɩ-na Wɩa teeŋ?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
When Do Mountain Goats Give Birth?
1When do mountain goats
and deer give birth?
Have you been there
when their young are born?
* 2How long are they pregnant
3before they deliver?
4Soon their young grow strong
and then leave
to be on their own.
5Who set wild donkeys free?
6I alone help them survive
in salty desert sand.
7They stay far from crowded cities
and refuse to be tamed.
8Instead, they roam the hills,
searching for pastureland.
9Would a wild ox agree
to live in your barn
and labor for you?
10Could you force him to plow
or to drag a heavy log
to smooth out the soil?
11Can you depend on him
to use his great strength
and do your heavy work?
12Can you trust him
to harvest your grain
or take it to your barn
from the threshing place?
An Ostrich Proudly Flaps Her Wings
13An ostrich proudly
flaps her wings,
but not because
she loves her young.
14She abandons her eggs
and lets the dusty ground
keep them warm.
15And she doesn't seem to worry
that the feet of an animal
could crush them all.
16She treats her eggs as though
they were not her own,
unconcerned that her work
might be for nothing.
17I myself made her foolish
and without common sense.
18But once she starts running,
she laughs at a rider
on the fastest horse.
Did You Give Horses Their Strength?
19Did you give horses their strength
and the flowing hair
along their necks?
20Did you make them able
to jump like grasshoppers
or to frighten people
with their snorting?
21Before horses are ridden
into battle,
they paw at the ground,
proud of their strength.
22Laughing at fear, they rush
toward the fighting,
23while the weapons of their riders
rattle and flash in the sun.
24Unable to stand still,
they gallop eagerly into battle
when trumpets blast.
25Stirred by the distant smells
and sounds of war, they snort
in reply to the trumpet.
26Did you teach hawks to fly south
for the winter?
* 27Did you train eagles to build
28their nests on rocky cliffs,
29where they can look down
to spot their next meal?
30 Then their young gather to feast
wherever the victim lies.
translation_text:
1Ŋ jɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ bʋŋ-nyuŋ gbuŋgbogoba sɩɩ lʋl nɛɛ?
Ŋ ha na aamɩŋ sɩɩ lʋl?
2Ŋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ yie kɛŋ luoruŋ a diene magɛ nɛɛ?
Ŋ jɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ yie lʋl nɛɛ?
3Ba yie kpirimi nɛ a lʋl ba biiriŋ,
a wiesi ba lʋlʋŋ hɛɛŋ lɛl.
4Ba biiri-la yie waa gɩrɩ-la tʋɔŋ a kɛŋ doluŋ,
a lɩɩ mʋ hɛ lee dɔŋ, ba bɩra bɩ mɩɩraa kɔ.
5Kʋbɛɛ nɛ puri komo ta?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ puru ʋ ŋmɛsɩŋ lɛ?
6Mɩ-na nɛ joŋu hɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa ʋ dɩjʋʋlʋŋ,
a leŋ kpesiŋ ŋaa ba dɩ-diiliŋ.
7Komo yie mʋmɔŋ goŋ-la ba sɩɩ ŋaa tabalɩŋ tʋɔŋ,
ʋ bɩ nʋʋkala kpɩa-la ka nɩɩ.
8Ʋ yie gɔllɔɔ baarɛ dundolluŋ nyuŋ a chɩchɛ ʋ kʋdiilee,
a gɔllɛ nɩmɛ a chɩchɛ pɩpaa-laarɩŋ dɩ ʋ dii.
9Baga nɛŋ jaŋ sɛɩ a tɩma pɩŋ?
Ʋ jaŋ sɛɩ a chʋa ŋ ja-yaŋ dɩ-biliŋ?
10Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ŋmɛnɩŋ vɔbʋ a leŋ dɩ ʋ pɛrɛɛ?
Koo a joŋ doluŋ sɩ yuŋŋie a vɔɔ ʋ lɛ dɩ ʋ lɛrɛ tinteeŋ dɩ ʋ magɛ dɔŋɔ?
11Ŋ jaŋ wuo joŋ ŋ yɩɛlaa hɛ ʋ doluŋ lɛ,
a leŋ dɩ ʋ tɩŋ ŋ tɩntɩŋ-duoruŋ?
12Ŋ jaŋ wuo joŋ ŋ yɩɛlaa hɛ ʋ lɛɛ,
dɩ ʋ kɛŋ ŋ baga kɩaa kʋ jʋʋ ŋ taha tʋɔŋ a pɩŋ?
13Nyaŋkɩɩbʋʋna yie ŋmoo ʋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ,
ama ʋ bɩ ʋ pʋnaa wuo kaa magɩsɛ diibelimbine pʋnaa.
14Ʋ yie lo ʋ halaa a bil tinteeŋ nɛ,
a leŋ tinteeŋ lɩmɩŋ kɩkɛmba.
15Ʋ yie bɩ bɩɩnɛ arɩ nʋʋ jaŋ wuo nʋɔsɛba yɛrɛ,
koo baga kʋŋ jaŋ nʋɔsɛba.
16Ʋ yie bɩ ʋ biiriŋ woruŋ kɛŋ a nagɛ ʋ dee bɩ ba tɩɩ,
a bɩ ʋ lɔlʋŋ wɩaa chɩla.
17Mɩ-na Wɩa bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ joŋo pʋ,
mɩ bɩ leŋe ʋ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa.
18Ama dɩ ʋ nɛ kɛŋ ʋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ yɛrɛ dɩ ʋ fá,
ʋ yie mʋmɔŋ janɩŋ arɩ ja-jɩllaa lɛ nɛ.
19Ŋ nɛ pɩ jaaba doluŋ
koo ŋ nɛ pʋ gbɛsɛ-la sɩ hɛ ʋ baŋŋaa lɛ a bibiegi?
20Ŋ nɛ leŋe ʋ fɩfɩl a nagɛ hɔbɔ,
a ŋmoo mɩɩsɩŋ a joŋ fawʋllʋŋ hɩhɛ nɩaa lɛɛ?
21Ʋ yie lɔgɛ tinteeŋ yuyuo, aŋ jʋjʋɔsɛ ʋ sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ,
a fá jʋʋ laalɩŋ tʋɔŋ.
22Ʋ bɩ fawʋllʋŋ ka fá, ʋ bɩ kʋŋkala ka fá.
Ʋ bɩ bayuoru kʋŋ na a mɩmɩɩrɛ harɩŋ.
23To-huoŋ yie dʋdɔŋ nɛ ʋ sɛmɛ,
a pɛ timiŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ sɩ leŋe ʋ lɩlɩgɩsɛ lɛ.
24Ʋ yaraa yie nyaasɛ nɛ ʋ chichel, a faasa fá.
Dɩ ba nɛ ŋmʋʋ banyile, ʋ bɩ dɩ-bala wuo chɩŋ.
25Dɩ ba nɛ ŋmʋʋ banyile, ʋ yie ŋmoo mɩɩsɩŋ.
Ʋ yie hɛ dɩ-bolii nɛ aŋ nɩɩ laalɩŋ sʋɔra,
a nɩɩ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ ma sɩɩ ŋaa laalɩyuori goŋ.
26Ŋ nɛ pɩ kɩla wʋjɩmɩŋ ʋ kaa fifil,
a jɛrɛ ʋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ a chaasa wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ?
27Ŋ nɛ yie dagɛ kachuuŋ ʋ file jɩl wɩa-nyuŋ,
aŋ sɩsaa ʋ dɛlɛ tɩa nyuŋ dɩ-leŋii?
28Ʋ yie saa ʋ dɛlɛ bʋsʋŋ sɩ leŋie nyuŋ nɛ,
a faa nɩmɛ, wɩɩ bɩ ʋ ka walɩmɛ.
29Nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ yie hɛ aŋ bee chɩchɛ ʋ kʋdiilee,
ʋ yie naba dɩ-bolii.
30Ʋ biiriŋ ka dii chalɩŋ nɛ.
Nammɩa sɩ hɛ lee-la, nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ ma yie hɛ.”

english_text:
The Lord Continues
I Am the Lord All-Powerful
* 1I am the Lord All-Powerful,
2but you have argued
that I am wrong.
Now you must answer me.
3Job said to the Lord:
4Who am I to answer you?
5I did speak once or twice,
but never again.
6Then out of the storm
the Lord said to Job:
7Face me and answer
the questions I ask!
8Are you trying to prove
that you are innocent
by accusing me of injustice?
9Do you have a powerful arm
and a thundering voice
that compare with mine?
10If so, then surround yourself
with glory and majesty.
* 11Show your furious anger!
Throw down and crush
12all who are proud and evil.
13Wrap them in grave clothes
and bury them together
in the dusty soil.
14Do this, and I will agree
that you have won
this argument.
I Created You
15I created both you
and the hippopotamus.
It eats only grass like an ox,
16but look at the mighty muscles
in its body 17and legs.
Its tail is like a cedar tree,
and its thighs are thick.
18The bones in its legs
are like bronze or iron.
19I made it more powerful
than any other creature,
yet I am stronger still.
20Undisturbed, it eats grass
while the other animals
play nearby.
* 21It rests in the shade of trees
along the riverbank
22or hides among reeds
in the swamp.
23It remains calm and unafraid
with the Jordan River rushing
and splashing in its face.
24There is no way to capture
a hippopotamus—
not even by hooking its nose
or blinding its eyes.
translation_text:
1La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋla pɩ Job:
2“Mɩ nɛ Wɩa, doluŋ kala Tɩɩna, ama ŋ kɛŋ wɩaa lɛrɛ nɛ mɩ teeŋ arɩ mɩ kɩaa bɩ sɩŋ.
Lɛɛlɛ bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ.”
3Ŋɩɩ nɛ Job bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA:
4“Mɩ bɩ kʋŋkala ŋaa, wʋbɛɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ wuo laa bʋl ŋ niiŋ lɛ?
Mɩ tɔ mɩ niiŋ nɛ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩɩkala.
5Mɩ paala bʋl wɩaa a kieli nɛ,
mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩɩkala.”
6Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA to duoŋ-peliŋ tʋɔŋ a bʋl wɩaa pɩ Job:
7“Kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ a nagɛ baala,
mɩ jaŋ pɩɛsɩŋ wɩaa dɩ ŋ chaarɛ ba sɩaa pɩmɛ.
8Ŋŋ chɛ ŋ dagɛ arɩ mɩ-na bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ,
ŋ-na nɛ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ koo?
9Ŋ kɛŋ doluŋ a nagɛ mɩ-na Wɩa nɛɛ?
Ŋ jaŋ wuo kpɩa goŋ arɩ mɩ sɩɩ kpɩa ŋɩɩ?
10Dɩ ŋ nɛ jaŋ wuo ŋaa ŋɩɩ, kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa ŋaa nɩbal dɩ ŋ yɩrɩŋ sisii yee.
Leŋ dɩ nɩaa ziziliŋ dɩ ŋ gigenni dɩ mɩ na.
11Bee na nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ dagɛ ba tɩtɩa,
na baanɩŋ a kɛmba muuri.
12Bemba woruŋ aŋ kɛmba muuri,
chei nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ lee-la kala ba sɩ hɛ.
13Hugi ba kala tinteeŋ,
tɔ ba hɛ lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ lɛ.
14Dɩ ŋ nɛ wuo ŋaa ŋɩɩ, mɩ jaŋ jɩŋ
arɩ ŋ tɩtɩa doluŋ jaŋ wuo laaŋ ta.
15Bee na lɩɩ-nɛŋ,
mɩ nɛ ŋaaʋ, a nagɛ ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ ŋaaŋ.
Ʋ didii yaŋ a nagɛ nɛŋ.
16Bee na doluŋ sɩ hɛ ʋ kparaa lɛ ŋɩɩ,
ʋ luoruŋ nammɩa sɩ yʋga magɛ ŋɩɩ.
17Ʋ bʋbʋɔ-doho sii pɛ a nagɛ kuolo,
nampɩl-bʋɔlaa yʋgɛ ʋ huiyee lɛ.
18Ʋ haŋgbelee kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ woruŋ a nagɛ kɔlɩɩŋ.
Ʋ naasɩŋ nagɛ hɔ-doloo.
19Kɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ ŋaa tʋɔŋ, ʋ nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ a kɩɩba.
Ama mɩ-na Nɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaaʋ ha jaŋ wuo yuo diiu.
20Peelee nyuŋ nɛ ʋ kʋdiilee yie waa ʋ didii,
lee-la baga kɩaa sɩɩ gbielu.
21Ʋ yie pɩŋ sagɩrɩgalɩaba bʋbʋɔŋ,
a faa saŋgɛɛŋ sɩ hɛ lɩɩŋ niiŋ vʋchɔɔŋ leriŋ.
22Sagɩrɩgalɩaba-la bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ ʋ yie pɩŋ,
tɩɩsɩ-la sɩ chɩŋ fuoŋ niiŋ gollu chu a tɔʋ.
23Dɩ fuoŋ nɛ suo a gbu lɩɩ ma, ʋ bɔyɛ bɩ joŋ,
ʋ yie ta jɩa a pɩŋ nɛ dɩ Jɔdaŋ fuoŋ lɩɩŋ nɛ paala pɛllɛ jʋjʋʋ ʋ sɩaa.
24Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo tɔ lɩɩ-nɛŋ sɩaa aŋ kɛnʋ,
koo a bɛrɛ kɛnʋ a joŋ kʋa luro hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
Can You Catch a Sea Monster?
1 Can you catch a sea monster
by using a fishhook?
Can you tie its mouth shut
with a rope?
2Can it be led around
by a ring in its nose
or a hook in its jaw?
3Will it beg for mercy?
4Will it surrender
as a slave for life?
5Can it be tied by the leg
like a pet bird
for little girls?
6Is it ever chopped up
and its pieces bargained for
in the fish-market?
7Can it be killed
with harpoons or spears?
8Wrestle it just once—
that will be the end.
9Merely a glimpse of this monster
makes all courage melt.
10And if it is too fierce
for anyone to attack,
who would dare oppose me?
11I am in command of the world
and in debt to no one.
12What powerful legs,
what a stout body
this monster possesses!
13Who could strip off its armor
or bring it under control
with a harness?
14Who would try to open its jaws,
full of fearsome teeth?
* 15Its back is covered
with shield after shield,
16firmly bound and closer together
17than breath to breath.
When This Monster Sneezes
18When this monster sneezes,
lightning flashes, and its eyes
glow like the dawn.
19Sparks and fiery flames
explode from its mouth.
20And smoke spews from its nose
like steam
from a boiling pot,
21while its blazing breath
scorches everything in sight.
22Its neck is so tremendous
that everyone trembles,
23the weakest parts of its body
are harder than iron,
24and its heart is stone.
25When this noisy monster appears,
even the most powerful
turn and run in fear.
26No sword or spear can harm it,
27and weapons of bronze or iron
are as useless as straw
or rotten wood.
28Rocks thrown from a sling
cause it no more harm
than husks of grain.
This monster fears no arrows,
29it simply smiles at spears,
and striking it with a stick
is like slapping it with straw.
30As it crawls through the mud,
its sharp and spiny hide
tears the ground apart.
31And when it swims down deep,
the sea starts churning
like boiling oil,
32and it leaves behind a trail
of shining white foam.
33No other creature on earth
is so fearless.
34It is king of all proud creatures,
and it looks upon the others
as nothing.
translation_text:
1Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ gbɩaŋ a kɛŋ peribanyeŋŋu,
koo a kɛŋ ŋmɛnɩŋ vɔɔ ʋ nandelimiŋ a bil?
2Ŋ jaŋ wuo joŋ ŋmɛnɩŋ luro hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ,
koo ŋ joŋ gbɩaŋ tɔɔ gɩrɩgɛ ʋ tapaŋaa lɛɛ?
3Ʋ jaŋ sʋlʋŋ dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ ʋ mʋ,
koo a sʋlʋŋ dɩ ŋ fá ʋ nenige?
4Ʋ jaŋ sɛɩ dɩ ŋ dɩ ʋ pɛ niiŋ,
dɩ ʋ ŋaa ŋ yomo ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛɛ?
5Ŋ jaŋ wuo vɔbʋ a nagɛ diibie,
a joŋu pɩ ŋ hantolibiisiŋ dɩ ba kaa gbigbielii?
6Bayalaa jaŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ba yɔbʋʋ?
Ba jaŋ kɛnʋ kpaa pɛ ba bayal kɩaa lɛ a yallɛɛ?
7Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ timiŋ tɔɔ ʋ teniŋ lurii?
Koo a kɛŋ to-hɛmɩŋ tɔɔ ʋ nyuŋ lurii?
8Dɩ ŋ nɛ digu, ŋ jaŋ na ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ jaŋ kɛnɩŋ vɩgɩlɛ,
ŋ maachie kala bɩra bɩ jaŋ yʋ aŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.
9Dɩ ŋ nɩɩ nɛrɩgɛ dɩ ŋ kɛnʋ, ŋ nyɩsɛ ŋ tɩtɩa nɛ,
dɩ ŋ sɩɩŋ nɛ paala naʋ, ŋ nandaasɩŋ yie yʋɔrɛ nɛ.
10Nɩtɛrɛ kala tuo sɩ jaŋ wuo kosu dɩ ʋ sii ŋaa wɩaa.
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ saa jaŋ wuo sii chɩŋ mɩ lɛ?
11Kʋbɛɛ nɛ kɛŋ kʋŋ mɩ teeŋ, a magɛ dɩ mɩ timuu?
Kʋŋkala sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ lɛ ŋaa mɩ kʋŋ nɛ.
12Mɩ jaŋ dagɛ ŋɩɩ lɩɩŋ tʋɔŋ kʋbɔŋ-la naasɩŋ sɩ naga,
ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ, arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ yaraa sɩ mɛ woruŋ.
13Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo puri ʋ teniŋ?
Koo a joŋ koŋ hɛ ʋ niiŋ lɛ?
14Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ʋ niiŋ suri,
ʋ nyɩlaa sɩ kɛŋ fawʋllʋŋ ŋɩɩ?
15Ʋ yaraa puruŋ kpalɩba nɛ,
a chaasa jʋʋ dɔŋɔ woruŋ.
16Ba faasa kpagɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ woruŋ,
peliŋ bɩ ba pɛgɛ wuo too jʋʋ.
17Ba faasa mɛrɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ nɛ,
a nyʋa kɛŋ dɔŋɔ, ŋ bɩ ba wuo kaa lɛrɛ.
18Dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋmoo mɩɩsɩŋ, nyiniŋ yie lɩgɩsɛ nɛ.
Ʋ sɩaa yie nagɛ taŋ sɩ pʋlaa kɔ pʋlʋmʋŋ nɛ.
19Nyiŋ-geliŋ yie lɩlɩɩ ʋ niiŋ lɛ nɛ,
nyiŋ-kɛntɛrɩsɩŋ ma to dɔŋɔ a lɩlɩɩ.
20Nyʋɔsʋŋ yie lɩlɩɩ ʋ mɩɩ-boyee lɛ nɛ,
a nagɛ ba sɩ joŋ kɩaa arɩ pupoiŋ a chɔ nyiniŋ lɛ.
21Ʋ wiese peliŋ yie leŋ hɔlɔɔ chol nyiniŋ,
nyiŋgeliŋ lɩlɩɩ ʋ niiŋ lɛ.
22Ʋ baŋŋaa chaasa kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ woruŋ,
dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ chemu, fawʋllʋŋ yie kɛnʋ nɛ.
23Ʋ yaraa sɩ kuriso kuriso ŋɩɩ chaasa jʋʋ dɔŋɔ lɛ nɛ,
a ŋaa kpɩm a bɩ jigisi.
24Ʋ bɔyɛ dolie a nagɛ bʋŋ nɛ.
Ʋ dolie a nagɛ nɔmʋŋ.
25Dɩ ʋ nɛ sie, fawʋllʋŋ yie kɛŋ nɩduoruŋ nɛ,
ba mɩɩra fá.
26Tokobii kala bɩ ʋ lɛ ka dii,
Timiŋ koo to-hɛmɩŋ ma bɩ ʋ lɛ ka dii.
27Hɔɔŋ nagɛ sekeliŋ nɛ ʋ teeŋ,
kɔlɩɩŋ ma nagɛ daa-pʋɔŋ ʋ teeŋ.
28To-hɛŋŋɛɛ bɩ jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ ʋ fá,
kpalɩŋ tabɩaa bɩ ʋ wʋŋaalɩɩ kala kɛnɛ.
29Toŋguluŋ paala nagɛ sekeliŋ nɛ ʋ teeŋ.
Dɩ nɩaa nɛ yuou arɩ timiŋ, ʋ yie paala mʋmɔmba nɛ.
30Ʋ luoruŋ teniŋ paala kɛŋ niiŋ a nagɛ kenchele nɛ,
dɩ ʋ nɩɩ vɛŋ vʋchɔɔŋ tʋɔŋ, ʋ yie kpɛrɛ tinteeŋ ŋɩɩ nɛ a mʋ.
31Ʋ yie kɛŋ lɩɩŋ vuugi a nagɛ ba sɩ chɔ lɩɩŋ ʋ kpɩkpɛrɛ,
a leŋ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ vuvuugi a nagɛ nʋʋŋ ba sɩ joŋo hɛ pupoiŋ tʋɔŋ a chɔ nyiniŋ lɛ.
32Dɩ ʋ nɩɩ vɛŋ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tʋɔŋ, ʋ libe yie pɩŋ nɛ a tʋtʋl,
ka lɩɩ-la kala tɔ arɩ fʋnfʋgɩ-pʋla.
33Kʋŋkala tuo dʋnɩa lɛ a magʋ.
Ʋ bɩ kʋŋkala ka fá.
34Ʋ yie bee gʋʋnɛ baga kɩalɩŋ kala sɩ bɩɩna ba ŋaa wajɩaba nɛ.
Ʋ nɛ ŋaa baga kɩaa kala kuoro.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to the Lord
No One Can Oppose You
1Job said:
2No one can oppose you,
because you have the power
to do what you want.
3 You asked why I talk so much
when I know so little.
I have talked about things
that are far beyond
my understanding.
4 You told me to listen
and answer your questions.
5I heard about you from others;
now I have seen you
with my own eyes.
6That's why I hate myself
and sit here in dust and ashes
to show my sorrow.
The Lord Corrects Job's Friends
7The Lord said to Eliphaz:
What my servant Job has said about me is true, but I am angry with you and your two friends for not telling the truth. 8So I want you to go over to Job and offer seven bulls and seven goats on an altar as a sacrifice to please me. After this, Job will pray, and I will agree not to punish you for your foolishness.
9Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar obeyed the Lord, and he answered Job's prayer.
A Happy Ending
10 After Job had prayed for his three friends, the Lord made Job twice as rich as he had been before. 11Then Job gave a feast for his brothers and sisters and for his old friends. They expressed their sorrow for the suffering the Lord had brought on him, and they each gave Job some silver and a gold ring.
12The Lord now blessed Job more than ever; he gave him 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pair of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys.
13In addition to seven sons, Job had three daughters, 14whose names were Jemimah, Keziah, and Keren Happuch. 15They were the most beautiful women in that part of the world, and Job gave them shares of his property, along with their brothers.
16Job lived for another 140 years—long enough to see his great-grandchildren have children of their own— 17and when he finally died, he was very old.
translation_text:
Wɩalɩŋ Job ma sɩ bʋla pɩ La Tɩɩna
1Ŋɩɩ nɛ Job bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA:
2“Mɩ jɩma ŋ jaŋ wuo ŋaa wɩɩkala,
nʋʋkala bɩ wɩɩ ŋ sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ŋ ŋaa wuo birigi.
3Ŋ pɩɛsa, ‘Kʋbɛɛ nɛ kaŋ dɩ ŋ pɩɛsɛ wɩaa a mʋ tɩgɛ mɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ lɛ, aŋ bɩ wɩɩkala jɩŋ?
Mɩ sɛnɛ bʋl wɩaa mɩ sɩ paala bɩ ba sɩaa jɩŋ nɛ,
wɩalɩŋ kperi a kɩɩ mɩ jɩmɩŋ.’
4Ŋ sɩ, ‘Jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ, ka dɩ mɩ bʋl wɩaa,
mɩ jaŋ pɩɛsɩŋ wɩaa,
dɩ ŋ chaarɛ ba sɩaa pɩmɛ.’
5Mɩ dɩgɩlaa nɛ faa nɩɩ ŋ wɩaa,
ama lɛɛlɛ mɩ sɩɩŋ naŋ nɛ.
6Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, hɩɩsɩŋ kɛmmɛ nɛ a tɩŋ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ bʋla wɩaa.
Mɩ ŋaa tʋɔrʋŋ bʋgɛ a hɔŋ hagɩla lɛ aa dagɛ arɩ mɩ bɩrɩmɛ mɩ niiŋ nɛ.”
7La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋl wɩaa pɩ Job a dɛrɛ nɛ, ʋ bʋla pɩ Ɛlɩfas, Tɛma tɩɩna-la ma, “Mɩ na baanɩŋ nɛ ŋ dɩ ŋ nandɔsʋ-la balɩa nyuŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa wɩalɩŋ ma sɩ bʋla tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ, ma bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ bʋla a nagɛ mɩ tɩntɩnna Job sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ. 8Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, má kɛsɛ nɛ-belliŋ balɩpɛ, pie-belliŋ ma balɩpɛ a kaa mʋ mɩ tɩntɩnna Job teeŋ a kpʋ a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ ma tɩtɩa. Mɩ tɩntɩnna Job jaŋ sʋlmɩ pɩma dɩ mɩ laa ʋ sʋla. Mɩ bɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛma a tɩŋ nɩyaarɛ wɩalɩŋ ma sɩ bʋla wɩaa. Wɩalɩŋ ma sɩ bʋla tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ, ma bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ bʋla a nagɛ mɩ tɩntɩnna Job sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ.” 9Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛlɩfas, Tɛma tɩɩna-la, Bɩlɩdad sɩ ŋaa Sʋa tɩɩna-la arɩ Zɔfa ma sɩ ŋaa Naama tɩɩna ŋaa wɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pɩba. Ŋɩɩ nɛ La Tɩɩna laa Job sʋla.
10Job sɩ chʋɔlɛ Wɩa pɩ ʋ nandɔsʋ-la harɩŋ, La Tɩɩna leŋ ʋ bɩra dʋa woruŋ, a magɛ ŋɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ kɛnɛ naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa. 11Ʋ naambiiriŋ kala arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala fa sɩ jɩmʋ kɔ ʋ teeŋ a dii kɩaa ʋ dɩa lɛ. Ba bʋl wɩaa nyagɛ ʋ bɔyɛ ʋ yaraa pɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ wʋwalɩmɩa-la kala La TƖƖNA sɩ joŋo hɛ ʋ lɛ. Ba kʋŋkala pʋ hɔpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ nenii-pɩrɩŋ.
12Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA pɛ Job lɛ woruŋ ʋ mɩɩ-kaanɩŋ lɛ, a kɩɩ ʋ bumbuŋ-la. Ʋ kɛŋ piesee bʋɩ fii arɩ banɛsɛ, bʋntaŋŋaba ma bʋɩ balɩdʋ, ʋ nɛ-pɛrɛɛ arɩ ʋ kakusuŋ ma ŋaa bʋɩ bʋɩ. 13Ʋ kɛŋ hambolibiisiŋ balɩpɛ nɛ, hantolibiisiŋ ma batori. 14Ʋ toli-hɩaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Jemima, lɩa tɩɩna yɩrɩŋ nɛ Kezia, tori tɩɩna ma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Kɛrɩŋ-Hapu. 15Haal kala fa tuo tintee-la lɛ a zɔmɔ magɛ Job toloo. Ba nyɩmma kpaa ʋ dʋa pɩba a nagɛ ʋ sɩ kpaa ŋɩɩ pɩ ba dɩbaalaa.
16Wɩaa deemba kala harɩŋ, Job hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ zɔlɔ arɩ mahɩŋ balɩa nɛ. Ʋ sɩɩŋ na ʋ biiriŋ arɩ ʋ nihee arɩ ʋ nihi-lɩɛrɛba nɛ a mʋ yi ba gentiŋ-nɛsɛ lɛ. 17Ʋ fa hɩɛsa nɛ woruŋ aŋ-na sʋʋ.

english_text:
BOOK I
(Psalms 1–41)
The Way to Happiness
1God blesses those people
who refuse evil advice
and won't follow sinners
or join in sneering at God.
2Instead, they find happiness
in the Teaching of the Lord,
and they think about it
day and night.
3 They are like trees
growing beside a stream,
trees that produce
fruit in season
and always have leaves.
Those people succeed
in everything they do.
4That isn't true of those
who are evil—
they are like straw
blown by the wind.
5Sinners won't have an excuse
on the day of judgment,
and they won't have a place
with the people of God.
6The Lord protects everyone
who follows him,
but the wicked follow a road
that leads to ruin.
translation_text:
Tʋɔtɔrʋŋ wombiiŋ
1Wɩa jaŋ pɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ
nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ niiŋ ka to lɛ,
a bɩ wʋbɔŋ ŋaaraa harɩŋ ka to,
a bɩ nɩalɩŋ ma sɩɩ sieri Wɩa lɛ tʋɔŋ ka guoli.
2Ba-na tʋɔtɔrʋŋ nɛ dɩ ba to La Tɩɩna wombiiŋ,
a kɛŋ wombii-la wɩaa chʋchɔgɩsɛ ba tʋɔŋ lɛ wɩɩhɛyɛ arɩ tɩtaŋɩŋ kala.
3Ba nagɛ tɩɩsɩŋ ba sɩ chɔnsɔ fuoŋ niiŋ nɛ,
ba nɩnɛŋ ba bʋa lɛ,
ba pɩpaarɩŋ bɩ yuori.
Wɩɩ na-kala nɛ dɩ nɩaa deemba ŋaa, ʋ yie vɛŋ woruŋ nɛ a pɩba.
4Nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ-na bɩ ŋɩɩ naga.
Ba nagɛ mɩɩ-jɔrʋŋ nɛ peliŋ yie paa viiri.
5Wɩa jaŋ chei nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ sarɩya chɛ-diiliŋ,
ba bɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ wuo guoli.
6Wɩa jɩŋ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa wombiiŋ wɩaa nɛ aa pɔba,
ama nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ-na wombiiŋ jaŋ cheiba.

english_text:
The Lord's Chosen King
1 Why do the nations plot,
and why do their people
make useless plans?
2The kings of this earth
have all joined together
to turn against the Lord
and his chosen king.
3They say, “Let's cut the ropes
and set ourselves free!”
4In heaven the Lord laughs
as he sits on his throne,
making fun of the nations.
5The Lord becomes furious
and threatens them.
His anger terrifies them
as he says,
6“I've put my king on Zion,
my sacred hill.”
7 I will tell the promise
