9Nɩyaarɩŋ sɩ magɛ namaga,
ʋ nagɛ sɩ-nyʋara sɩɩ chɛ ʋ lɩɩsɛ sɔɔŋ sɩ tɔɔ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.
10Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ joŋ nɩyaarɩŋ koo nʋʋ na-kala sɩ kʋʋ bal dɩ ʋ tɩŋ ka ʋ timu,
ʋ nagɛ to-yuoro sɩ gɔllɔ pɩrɛ nɩaa tɩta nɛ.
11A nagɛ vaha sɩ yie tʋɔsɛ aŋ gʋra paa dii ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ nɩyaarɩŋ ma yie ŋaa nɩyaarɩ wɩɩŋ aŋ bɩra ŋaa wɩɩ-la tɩtɩa.
12Dɩ ŋ nɛ na nʋʋ sɩ bɩɩna ʋ jɩŋ wɩɩkala nɛ aŋ bɩ wɩɩ jɩŋ,
nɩyaarɩŋ nɛ kpɩaʋ.
13Yarɩwɩɩ tɩɩna yie bʋl, “Naachigiŋ nɛ hɛ wombiiŋ lɛ,
kpeye yaraa sɩ hoso nɩɩ gɔllɛ jeeŋ harɩŋ.”
14Ba sɩ yie suri boro ʋ chɩna viviisi ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ yarɩwɩɩ tɩɩna ma yie pɩna bibilimi ʋ kʋpɩnaa nyuŋ.
15Yarɩwɩɩ tɩɩna yie joŋ nɩsɩŋ a nʋrɛ kʋdiilee lɛ nɛ,
ama yarɩwɩɩŋ bɩ sɛɩ dɩ ʋ kaa jɩl niiŋ.
16Yarɩwɩɩ tɩɩna bɩɩna ʋ nɛ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ
a kɩɩ nɩaa balɩpɛ sɩ jaŋ wuo lɩɩsɛ wɩaa sɩaa woruŋ.
17Nɩaa sɩ kɛŋ yuosuŋ ŋ wɩɩ tuo nɩmɛ, ka ŋ joŋ ŋ niiŋ hɛ,
ʋ nagɛ vaha sɩ kʋʋ bal, ŋ kɛŋ ʋ dɩgɩlaa lɛ lɛrɛ nɛ.
18A nagɛ nyɩnyɛ tɩɩna sɩɩ yuo to-hɛŋŋɛɛ
sɩɩ chol nyiniŋ koo hɛ-sʋʋlaa,
19ʋ nagɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ yie nyɩsɛ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna aŋ bʋl,
“Mɩ ta kaa gbieli nɛ.”
20Dɩ daasɩŋ nɛ tuo, nyiniŋ dɩsɛ nɛ,
dɩ zɛmbɛ ma nɛ tuo, yuosuŋ jaŋ fɩɛlɛ.
21Hɔlɔɔ sɩ yie ŋaa nyiŋ-muluŋ ŋɩɩ ka daasɩŋ ma nɛ ŋaa nyiniŋ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ yuo-hɛɛrɛ ma yie leŋ yuosuŋ pupusi.
22Zɛmbɛ tɩɩna wʋbʋlʋŋ sɩma a nagɛ kʋdii-sɩŋŋaa nɛ,
baa tuu tʋɔŋ nɛ woruŋ.
23Niiŋ sɩɩ bʋl wʋsɩŋŋaa aŋ kɛŋ tʋɔbɔmʋŋ,
ʋ nagɛ ba sɩ kɛŋ chʋrʋŋ mɛ pupoiŋ aŋ joŋ hɔpʋla bɩnɩŋ taara nɛ.
24Nɩa yie bɛrɩŋ aŋ fugoo bʋl wʋsɩŋŋaa ŋ teeŋ,
aŋ ka ʋ tʋɔŋ biri.
25Ʋ wʋbʋla yie sɩŋ nɛ, ama sɩ́ ʋ laa dii,
bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ tʋɔŋ kala nɛ suo arɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ.
26Ʋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ʋ tʋɔ-bɔŋ-la faa a nyɩsɩŋ,
ama ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ jaŋ lɩɩ nɩaa tʋɔŋ.
27Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ lu buotuoŋ bil ʋ dɔŋɔ lɛ, ʋ jaŋ gʋra tuu bʋa-la.
Dɩ nʋʋ nɩɩ bilimi tabɩɩŋ dɩ ʋ nyagɛ ʋ dɔŋɔ, tabɩɩ-la jaŋ mɩɩra kʋ nyagʋ.
28Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa bɛrɛ nɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa pɩpa nɛ,
nii-sɩma ka chei nɩaa nɛ.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1Sɩ́ chiemiŋ kaa ŋmoo bɔyɛ,
bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ bɩ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ chie sɩ jaŋ nagɛ.
2Sɩ́ ŋ tɩtɩa lɛ bɛsʋ, leŋ dɩ nʋʋ nɛ bɛsɛ ŋ lɛ,
nɩwogo, ŋ tɩtɩa-na dee.
3Tabɩɩŋ yuŋŋie nɛ, ka hagɩla ŋaa chʋga,
ama nɩyaarɩŋ wʋŋaalaa sɩ yie hɛ wɩalɩŋ nɛ yuŋŋie kɩɩ ba kala.
4Baanɩŋ ŋaa kʋbɔŋ nɛ a chichei wɩaa,
ama yarɩ-bieri ma nɛ bɩra bɔmɔ kɩɩʋ.
5Dɩ ŋ nɛ kpɩa nɩa lɛ nɩaa tʋɔŋ,
ʋ nɛ kpɩa ŋ sɩ sɩ ŋ chou nɛ aŋ kaa faa.
6Dɩ ŋ nandɔŋɔ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩ a jʋʋŋ lɛ ŋ ha jaŋ wuo laa ʋ wɩaa dii,
ama dɩ ŋ dʋndɔmɔ-na nɛ guoruŋ ma, ʋ haa nyɩsɩŋ nɛ.
7Dɩ ŋ nɛ vɔgɔ, tʋʋŋ ma yie paalaa sʋɔrɛ nɛ ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ,
ama dɩ losuŋ nɛ kɛnɩŋ, kʋ-la sɩ hɛyɛ bagɛ bagɛ ma paala ŋaa kʋsɩŋ nɛ ŋ teeŋ.
8Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ fá kagɛ ʋ dɩa lɛ,
ʋ nagɛ diibie sɩ yeŋŋi ʋ dɛlɛ leriŋ nɛ.
9Dɩ ŋ nɛ tɩsɛ tʋlaalɩɩ arɩ nʋʋ-sʋara, ŋ tʋɔŋ yie tɔrɛ nɛ.
Ama dɩ ŋ nandɔŋ fɩamɩŋ nɛ chaasa bʋl wɩaa chagɩlɩŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ zɔmɔ kɩɩba.
10Pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ ŋ nandɔŋɔ arɩ ŋ nyɩmma nandɔŋɔ vɩa ta.
Dɩ wɩaa nɛ jʋʋŋ, pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ ŋ naambie teeŋ sii mʋ a chɩchɛ ʋ pɛ ŋ lɛ.
Nɩɩ-la sɩ jʋʋ kpagɩŋ jaŋ wuo pɛ ŋ lɛ a kɩɩ ŋ naambie sɩ hɛ dɩ-bolii.
11Mɩ bii, kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ, dɩ ŋɩɩ leŋ dɩ mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ.
Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ jaŋ wuo na wombiiŋ a bʋl wɩaa nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ba hɩɩsɛmɛ teeŋ.
12Wʋjɩnna yie na wʋbɔmʋŋ dɩ ʋʋ kɔ, ʋ gɛbɛ faa,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ wɩaa jɩŋ woruŋ-na yie vɛnɛ vɛnɛ mʋ jʋʋ-ʋ nɛ, a na hɛɛŋ.
13Laa nɩɩ-la sɩ chɩna pɩ nʋhʋɔra ʋ dii chɩmɩŋ gɛrɩŋ, a bil chɩŋ-la bʋbʋɔŋ lɛ.
Ʋ maga dɩ ba laa gɛrɛ-la nʋhʋɔrʋ-la chɩmɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ lɛ nɛ.
14Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ sii chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla a kpɩa chʋɔlɛ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna,
nɩaa jaŋ joŋu arɩ ʋ kalɩba hɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ.
15Haala sɩ cho yuosuŋ
nagɛ duonuŋ sɩɩ pʋʋsʋ deeŋ deeŋ a bɩ leŋ nɛ.
16Dɩ ŋ nɩɩ walɩmɛ dɩ ʋ leŋ, ʋ nagɛ ŋ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ kɛrɛ peliŋ nɛ,
koo nʋʋ-lɩɩŋ nɛ ŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ŋ gulimi.
17A nagɛ ba sɩ yie kɛŋ hɔɔŋ a kaa taa hɔɔŋ ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ nuhuobiinee ma yie dɩdagɛ dɔŋɔ.
18Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ chɔnsɛ tɩa-la nɛnɛɛ ba sɩɩ dii a beŋ ʋ nyuŋ, ʋ jaŋ dii ʋ nɛnɛɛ.
Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ beŋ ʋ nɩhɩaŋ nyuŋ woruŋ, nɩaa jaŋ zilu.
19Ŋ sɩ yie beŋ lɩɩŋ lɛ a na ŋ tɩtɩa ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ tʋɔbɩɩnaa ma yie leŋ ŋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ ŋ mɛlɛ sɩ naga.
20Sʋʋŋ bʋa arɩ lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ sɩ bɩ vɔgɛ ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ nuhuobiine ma chɩchɛ kɩaa a bɩ vɔgɛ.
21Ba yie joŋ sɛlɩmɛ koo hɔpʋla a hɛ chefuguŋ-bʋa nyiniŋ lɛ nɛ a ŋmɩɛra lɩɩsɛ ʋ disiniŋ.
Ama dɩ nɩaa nɩɩ bɛsɛ nʋʋ lɛ, ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ ŋ jaŋ wuo to a jɩŋ ʋ mɛlɛ.
22Dɩ ŋ nɛ paala kɛŋ nɩyaarɩŋ a hɛ tɔgʋŋ tʋɔŋ a tugi arɩ tendiiŋ,
a joŋo daŋ nɔmʋŋ nyuŋ a nɔŋ a nagɛ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ yie nɔŋ munuŋ,
ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo lɩɩsɛ yaarɩŋ ʋ lɛ.
23Jɩŋ ŋ piesee arɩ ŋ bʋʋnaa yarɩfɩɛlaa wɩaa
a beŋ ba nyuŋ woruŋ,
24bɛɛ wɩaa dʋa bɩ jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ deeŋ deeŋ.
Nʋʋ bɩ jaŋ kuori a kaa mʋ wuu.
25Dɩ ŋ nɛ ku pʋsʋŋ ya-diiliŋ a ku dundolo nyuŋ kɩaa ma pɛ a hiese hɛ dɔŋɔ,
ka dɩ ya-falɩŋ bɩra tɔsɛ,
26piese-la lɛ ŋ jaŋ wuo na gɛnnɩŋ,
aŋ yallɛ bʋʋna-la ma a yɔɔ tinteeŋ.
27Ŋ jaŋ na bʋ-yɩlɩŋ yʋgɛ,
a kaa beŋ ŋ dɩa nɩaa,
dɩ haala-la sɩɩ tɩŋ ŋ dɩa lɛ ma na dii.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Nɩbɔmʋŋ yie fá nɛ dɩ nʋʋ bɩ ʋ kire,
ama tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna-na kɛŋ nyuduoŋ a nagɛ naachigiŋ nɛ.
2Dɩ tinteeŋ nɩaa nɛ bɩ dɔŋɔ ba niiriŋ ka sɛɩ, ba sɩpaalaaraa yie yʋgɛ nɛ,
ama dɩ sɩpaalaarʋ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ a kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa, wɩɩkala yie magɛ dɔŋɔ.
3Dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɩɩ dɔgɩsɛ summoo,
ʋ nagɛ duonuŋ sɩ faasa lɔgɔ jaasɛ a chei kʋdiilee nɛ.
4Nɩalɩŋ sɩ vɩa Wɩa wombiiŋ nɩɩ bɛsɛ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ,
ama ba dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ to wombii-la-na bɩ sugili.
5Nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ paala bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ jɩŋ,
ama nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ chɛ La Tɩɩna, ba-na jɩmʋ nɛ woruŋ.
6Nʋʋ sɩ ŋaa nyaabʋ aŋ bɩ wʋcheeli kala kɛnɛ,
ʋ nɛ kpɩa nʋʋ sɩ kɛŋ kɩaa ka ʋ wʋŋaalaa golibi.
7Bile sɩɩ to Wɩa wombiiŋ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa nɛ.
Ama nɩɩ-la sɩɩ to luobii-tɩŋŋaa harɩŋ hɩɩsɛ ʋ nyɩmma nɛ.
8Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ joŋ kɩaa chɩŋ nɩaa a faasa kɛŋ lɩɩŋ dɩdaŋ a dʋa kɩaa,
ʋ dʋa-la jaŋ ŋaa nʋʋ dɔŋ kɩaa, dɩ ʋ joŋo dii zile summoo lɛ.
9Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ bɩ chɛ ʋ jegili Wɩa wombiiŋ wɩaa,
ʋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ paala sʋɔrɛ nɛ.
10Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ nyɩsɛ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna hɛ wʋbɔmʋŋ lɛ,
ʋ jaŋ gʋra jʋʋ ʋ tɩtɩa bɛrɛ́,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ wʋcheeli kɛnɛ jaŋ na wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ.
11Kɩaa tɩɩna yie bɩɩnɛ arɩ ʋ jɩŋ wɩaa nɛ,
ama summo sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa yie bibenu dɩ ʋ bɩ wɩɩ jɩŋ.
12Dɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna nɛ dii kuoruŋ, nɩaa yie jʋjʋɔsɛ nɛ,
ama dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ die, nɩaa fá fɩfaa.
13Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ joŋ ʋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ faa, ʋ wɩaa bɩ sɩpaaŋ ka mʋ,
ama nɩɩ-la kala sɩ suri ʋ niiŋ a dagɛ ʋ kɩaa aŋ vɩaba, Wɩa jaŋ fá ʋ nisusuŋ.
14Nɩɩ-la kala sɩɩ fá La Tɩɩna bʋa-kala, ʋ tʋɔŋ jaŋ tɔrɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la kala sɩ kɛŋ tʋɔ-doluŋ jaŋ jʋʋ wɩaa.
15A nagɛ naachigiŋ sɩɩ huosu koo lʋgʋmʋŋ yaraa sɩ hoso ʋ kɛŋ fawʋllʋŋ ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ nagɛ summoo lɛ dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɩɩ bemba.
16Sɩpaalaarʋ-la sɩ tɛrɛ bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ kɛnɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ cho dɩ ʋ gɩrɩma dʋa jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩ-duduoŋ.
17Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kpʋ nʋʋ, ʋ jaŋ gɔllɔ baarɛ ŋɩɩ a mʋ sʋʋ.
Nʋʋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ pɛ ʋ lɛ.
18Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ bɩ wʋcheeli kɛnɛ, wɩaa bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ-ʋ,
ama nɩɩ-la wɩaa sɩ golibo jaŋ guu tel.
19Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ faasa tɩŋ ʋ baga lɛ jaŋ na kʋdiilee yʋgɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ kire to wʋpɛɩba harɩŋ jaŋ nyaabɛ woruŋ.
20Wɩa jaŋ chaasa pɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ lɛ woruŋ,
ama ʋ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ chel dɩ ʋ dʋa.
21Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ nɩaa pʋpɔrɛ, ŋɩɩ bɩ zɔŋ,
aŋ ka nɩa yie ŋaa wʋbɔmʋŋ a chɩchɛ kʋdiilee mʋa.
22Tʋɔ-bɔŋ tɩɩna yie chichel nɛ dɩ ʋ dʋa,
aŋ bɩ jɩŋ dɩ nyaaŋ ka gbɛrʋ nɛ.
23Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ nʋʋ tʋra kɩɩ,
ʋ jaŋ choŋ a kɩɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ nii-sɩma.
24Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ gʋrɛ ʋ nyɩmma koo ʋ naaŋ aŋ bʋl,
“Ʋ bɩ wʋbɔŋ ŋaa,”
tɩɩna dii gaara nandɔŋɔ nɛ.
25Tʋɔ-bɔŋ tɩɩna ka hɛ yuosuŋ nɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la kala sɩ joŋ ʋ yɩɛlaa hɛ La Tɩɩna lɛ,
ʋ wɩaa jaŋ vɛŋ woruŋ.
26Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ joŋ ʋ yɩɛlaa kala hɛ ʋ tɩtɩa lɛ ŋaa nɩyaarɩ nɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa, wɩɩkala bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ-ʋ.
27Nɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa kɩaa pɩpɩ summoo bɩ jaŋ chɛ kʋŋ ka,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ ʋ sɩaa tɔ summoo nyuŋ, ba jaŋ ŋmɩɛsa hɛ ʋ lɛ.
28Dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ dii kuoruŋ, nɩaa yie fɩfaa nɛ,
ama nɩbɔmʋŋ kuoruŋ nɛ dɛrɛ, tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa yie pʋŋa pɛ nɛ.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Dɩ ŋ nyuŋ nɛ dolie, dɩ ba tʋrʋŋ tʋrʋŋ lɔl,
ŋ jaŋ kʋʋ jɩŋ dɩ ba guu chei ŋ kala. Wɩɩkala tuo sɩ jaŋ laaŋ ta.
2Dɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna nɛ laa nɩaa sɩpaaŋ, ba yie jʋjʋɔsɛ nɛ,
ama dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ laa ba sɩpaaŋ, ba gʋgʋrɩmɛ wɩaa.
3Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ cho wʋjɩmɩŋ, ŋɩɩ yie leŋ ʋ nyɩmma tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ nɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩɩ to ha-lɩɩ-la harɩŋ, ʋ jaŋ ŋmoo chɩmɩŋ.
4Dɩ kuoro nɛ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ, ʋ jaŋ yie chɩŋ nɛ kpaŋ kpaŋ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ cho kpalaa diiniŋ yie yigi taŋ lo nɛ.
5Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ dii nii-sɩma ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna teeŋ,
bɛrɛ́ nɛ ʋ hɛ bil ʋ lɛ ŋɩɩ.
6Nɩbɔmʋŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ yie gʋra bɛrɛ kɛnʋ,
ama tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna-na jaŋ wuo yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a jʋɔsɛ.
7Tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa chɩl wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba ŋɩŋaa summoo lɛ wɩaa nɛ,
ama nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ-na sɩpaa tuo.
8Babiibalaa yie kɛŋ taŋ hosi nɛ,
ama wʋjɩnnaa-na yie leŋ nɩaa baanɩŋ fɩɛlɛ nɛ.
9Dɩ wʋjɩnna arɩ nɩyaara nɛ mʋ wɩaa dɩ-bʋlʋŋ,
nɩyaarɩ-la yie na baanɩŋ a yigi wɩaa lo nɛ a ŋɩŋaa goŋ. Leriŋ bɩ fɩɛlaa pɩŋ.
10Nɩkpʋʋra bɛrɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ wʋcheeli kɛnɛ nɛ.
Ʋ yie chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ lɩɩsɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ.
11Dɩ nɩyaarɩŋ baanɩŋ nɛ sie, ʋ yie ŋaa wɩaa nɛ nʋʋkala jɩŋ,
ama wʋjɩnna-na yie jɩma kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa nɛ.
12Dɩ kuoro nɛ jegilee nɩɩ wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ,
ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ kala yie bɩrɩmɛ nɩbɔmɔ nɛ.
13Wʋbala nɛ summo arɩ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ dɔgɩsʋ kala kaa magɛ dɔŋɔ:
La Tɩɩna nɛ pɩ ba kala mɩɩsɩŋ.
14Dɩ kuoro nɛ dii sarɩya dɩ summoo ma wuo nɩna ba wʋchɛɛlɛɛ,
ʋ kuoruŋ jaŋ dieni.
15Dɩ ŋ nɛ joŋ chɩba dagɛ bie, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ,
ama dɩ ŋ nɛ leŋ bie ta ʋ dʋndʋŋa, ʋ jaŋ hɩɩsɛ ʋ naaŋ.
16Dɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ laa nɩaa sɩpaaŋ, wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ yie pʋrɩgɛ nɛ.
Ama tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa-na jaŋ na ba dɩ-teliŋ.
17Tʋrɛ ŋ bie, ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ pɩŋ dɩ-bala,
dɩ ŋ kɛŋ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ.
18Dɩ nɩaa nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ a bɩ bee na wɩaa sɩpaaŋ, ba yie berimi nɛ,
ama nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ to wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ bile dɩ baa to, Wɩa jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ.
19Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ niiŋ dʋndʋŋa kɛŋ tɩntɩnna bil wombiiŋ lɛ.
Ʋ yie jɩŋ ba sɩaa ma nɛ aŋ bɩ jaŋ sɛɩ.
20Dɩ ŋ na nʋʋ sɩ pese bʋbʋl wɩaa,
nɩyaarɩŋ nɛ kɛŋ yɩɛlaa a kɩɩʋ.
21Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ ŋ tɩntɩnna pɩɛnɛ ʋ hambiriŋ kala lɛ,
ʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ chei.
22Baaŋ-tɩɩna ka hɛ yuosuŋ nɛ,
nɩɩ-la baanɩŋ sɩɩ sii lɩma lɩma yie ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ yʋgɛ nɛ.
23Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ bigisi ʋ tɩtɩa lɛ yie dii hɩɩsɩŋ nɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa muuri, nɩaa yie zizilu nɛ.
24Nɩɩ-la sɩ pɛ gaara lɛ, bɛrɛ ʋ tɩtɩa mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ.
Ʋ nɛ paala ŋmɩɛsɛ ma, ʋ ha bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ ka bʋl.
25Dɩ nʋʋ nɩɩ fá nuhuobiinee, ŋɩɩ ŋaa bɛrɛ́ nɛ ʋ lɛ,
ama nɩɩ-la sɩ laa La Tɩɩna dii, wɩɩkala bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ ʋ lɛ.
26Nʋʋkala yie chɩchɛ dɩ nɩbalɩŋ cho ʋ wɩaa nɛ,
ama La Tɩɩna teeŋ nɛ nʋʋkala yie na wʋtɩtɩɩ.
27Tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna bɛrɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ nɛ.
Nɩbɔmʋŋ ma bɛrɛ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Wɩalɩŋ Agʋ sɩ bʋla
1Baal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ baa yɩrɛ Agʋ. Ʋ nyɩmma nɛ Jakɛ, a ŋaa Masa tɩɩna.
Wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la:
Ʋ fa bʋla pɩ Ɩtɩɛl arɩ Uka, “Mɩ Wɩa leŋe mɩ kala bɛsɩmɛ nɛ, mɩ bɛsɩmɛ nɛ, a kala pʋgʋmɛ.
2Nɩaa kala tʋɔŋ mɩ nɛ chʋʋla,
nuhuobiinee tʋɔŋ mɩ nɛ bɩ wɩɩ jɩŋ.
3Mɩ bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ gʋnna.
Mɩ bɩ wɩɩkala jɩŋ a mʋ tɩgɛ Wɩa lɛ.
4Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jɩl Wɩa-jaŋ aŋ kʋ tuu?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ wuo kɛŋ peliŋ gulimi ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ wuo kɛŋ ʋ gɛrɩŋ a vɔɔ lɩɩŋ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ bil dʋnɩa dɩdɛrɩŋ lee-la kala ʋ chɩŋ kpaŋ kpaŋ?
Ʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ bɛɛ, ʋ bie yɩrɩŋ nɛ bɛɛ?
Dɩ ma nɛ jɩma, má dagɛmɛ.
5Wɩa niiŋ wʋbʋlaa bɩ cheeri kala kɛnɛ.
Ʋ nagɛ hɔɔ-la laalɩyuoroo sɩ kaa kɛrɛ laa bayuori hɛŋŋɛɛ nɛ aa tɔ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ yuoru.
6Pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ wɩɩ kaa pɛ ʋ niiŋ wɩaa lɛ.
Dɩ ŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ jaŋ kɛnɩŋ tʋra kɩɩ a leŋ dɩ ŋ jɩŋ arɩ ŋ ŋaa wʋnyɩɛrʋ nɛ.”
7“La Tɩɩna, wɩaa balɩa nɛ mɩ sʋlaa chɛ ŋ teeŋ.
Sɩ́ mɩ wɩaa deemba vɔŋ ka dɩ mɩ-na sʋʋ:
8Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ mɩ nyɩnyɩsɛ nɩaa koo aa nyɩɛ wɩaa.
Sɩ́ leŋe mɩ nyaabɛ koo a kɛŋ kɩaa kɩŋkɛŋ.
Ama pɩmɛ mɩ tapʋlɩɩ kala niiŋ kʋdiiliŋ.
9Dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ka dɩ mɩ kɛŋ kɩaa yʋgɛ, mɩ jaŋ wuo vɩaŋ
aŋ pɩɛsɛ, ‘Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa La Tɩɩna?’
Koo mɩ jaŋ ŋaa summu a gaa,
a chei ŋ-na mɩ Wɩa yɩrɩŋ.”
10Pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ tɩntɩnna yɩrɩŋ chei a pɩ ʋ nɩhɩaŋ,
dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ʋ jaŋ ŋmɩɛsa hɛ ŋ lɛ, dɩ ŋ na hɛɛŋ.
11Nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ hɛ nɩmɛ a bʋl wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ pɩpɩ ba nyɩmmaba
a bɩ wʋzɔŋ bʋla pɩpɩ ba naamba ma.
12Dɔnsʋŋ ma hɛ nɩmɛ a bɩɩnɛ dɩ ba tʋɔŋ pʋlla nɛ,
aŋ ka ba bɩ ba disiniŋ fo ta.
13Dɔnsʋŋ hɛ nɩmɛ a kɛŋ sɩɩ-duoŋ,
a bee gʋʋnɛ nɩaa.
14Dɔnsʋŋ ma hɛ nɩmɛ, ba niiŋ nagɛ tokobiee,
ba nyɩlaa ma nagɛ sɩɩsɩŋ.
Ba kɛŋ summoo
arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ liliŋ.
15Dimbaliere kɛŋ toloo balɩa nɛ.
Ba yie ŋmoo niiŋ, “Joŋo pɩmɛ, joŋo pɩmɛ.”
Kɩaa batori koo banɛsɛ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ, ba-na bɩ kɔ dɩ ba vɔgɔ.
Ba-na bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ba sɩ, “Ʋ maga.”
16Ba nɛ ŋ-la: lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ, hapɩrɩŋ,
tinteeŋ sɩ bɩ lɩɩŋ ka vɔgɛ arɩ nyiniŋ.
Ba-na bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ba sɩ, “Ʋ maga.”
17Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ aa mɔŋ ʋ nyɩmma,
a kɛŋ ʋ naaŋ ŋmuŋmoo gbɛɛŋ a bɩ ba niiŋ ka to,
gɩlɩŋgaamba jaŋ chaarɛ ʋ sɩaa,
dɩ duunuŋ ma dii ʋ kala.
18Kɩaa batori koo banɛsɛ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ ba wɩaa kperimi,
mɩ bɩ ba wɩaa sɩaa jɩŋ:
19Ba nɛ ŋ-la: ŋɩɩ duunuŋ sɩɩ fil wɩa-nyuŋ,
ŋɩɩ dɩmɩŋ sɩɩ vɛŋ bʋŋ nyuŋ,
ŋɩɩ lɩɩŋ daboro sɩɩ vɛŋ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ nyuŋ,
a pɛ baala arɩ hatolo pɛgɛ wɩaa lɛ.
20Haal-la sɩ gɔllɔɔ chɛ nɩaa balaba wɩɩŋ kala nɛ ŋ-la:
Ʋ yie dii nɛ aŋ tɩɩgɛ niiŋ ta,
aŋ bʋl, “Mɩ bɩ wʋbɔŋ kala ŋaa.”
21Wɩaa batori koo banɛsɛ nɛ kɛŋ tinteeŋ viviisi,
ba ŋaa wʋfakagɩa nɛ:
22Ba nɛ ŋ-la: Yomo sɩ kʋ dii kuoruŋ,
nɩyaarɩŋ sɩ tagɩlɛ kʋdiilee tʋɔŋ,
23haala sɩ ŋaa nɩaa bɛrʋ, ka ʋ na bala jaa,
arɩ ketiiŋ sɩ yigi ʋ dɩa naaŋ ta aŋ laa leriŋ.
24Kɩaa banɛsɛ nɛ hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ a muuri,
aŋ chaasa kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ woruŋ.
25Chunchusumuŋ doluŋ bɩ wɩɩ maga,
aŋ ka tafaaŋ ba yie tʋɔlɛ kʋdiilee.
26Bʋŋ-nyuŋ gbuŋgbogusuŋ ma doluŋ bɩ wɩɩ maga,
aŋ yie kɔrɩgɛ bʋbʋɔŋ jʋjʋʋ.
27Hɔbɔ ma bɩ kuoro kɛnɛ,
aŋ yie hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a vɩvɛŋ.
28Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ habalɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩsɩŋ,
aŋ ka ʋ yie wuo hɛ kuoro dɩa lɛ.
29Kɩaa batori koo banɛsɛ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ,
dɩ ba nɩɩ vɛŋ sɩma kɛnɩŋ, ba bɩ wɩɩ ka fá.
30Ba nɛ ŋ-la: Naachigiŋ, ʋ nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ baga kɩaa kala tʋɔŋ.
Dɩ ʋ nɩɩ vɛŋ, ʋ bɩ kʋŋkala ka fá,
31ji-bele sɩ gise jiŋŋee tʋɔŋ, gbuŋgbogo sɩɩ vɛŋ arɩ kuoro sɩɩ vɛŋ,
ka ʋ laalɩyuoroo gugollu.
32Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa nɩyaarɩ aŋ bigisi ŋ tɩtɩa lɛ,
koo dɩ ŋ nɩɩ bɩɩnɛ dɩ ŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ, ŋ leŋ.
33Dɩ ba ŋmoo nɛ-yɩlɩŋ, lɩɩŋ jaŋ lɩɩ aŋ ka nʋʋŋ,
dɩ ba ŋmoo nʋʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ chalɩŋ jaŋ lɩɩ,
dɩ ba nɛ dii nʋʋ baanɩŋ lɛ, yuosuŋ jaŋ sii.

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Wɩalɩŋ kuoro Lɛmʋɛl sɩ bʋla
1Lɛmʋɛl nɛ fa ŋaa Masa kuoro. Wɩalɩŋ ʋ naaŋ sɩ dagʋ nɛ ŋ-la:
2Mɩ bii-kpɩana, mɩ nɛ lʋlʋŋ.
Mɩ sʋl Wɩa nɛ ʋ joŋuŋ pɩmɛ.
3Sɩ́ ŋ doluŋ joŋo hɛ haalaa chɛnɩŋ lɛ.
Ba chei kuoroo yʋgɛ nɛ.
4Mɩ bii Lɛmʋɛl, jegile nɩɩ.
Kuoroo bɩ maga dɩ ba nyʋa sɩnɩŋ bubugi.
Ba paala bɩ maga dɩ ba hɩhɩɛnɛ sɩnɩŋ.
5Dɩ ba nɛ nyʋa sɩnɩŋ bugi, ba jaŋ yʋ wombiee-la ba sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto,
aŋ nyagɛ summoo bil.
6Leŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ lɛl nɛ nyʋnyʋa sɩnɩŋ,
leŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ tʋɔŋ sɩ faasa chei nɛ nyʋnyʋa.
7Dɩ ŋɩɩ wuo leŋ dɩ ba yʋ ba sunnuŋ lɛ,
a bɩra sɩ́ hɛɛ-la ba sɩɩ na wɩaa liisu.
8Bʋla laa nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa wuo bʋlaa laa ta,
aŋ pɔ laa nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ bɩ lee kɛnɛ dɩ ba wuo na wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba na.
9Dii sarɩya arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ,
a bʋla laa summoo arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ ta.
Haala sɩ kɛŋ mɛlɛ
10Dɩ ŋ nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ na haal-la mɛlɛ sɩ zɔmɔ,
ʋ hɛyɛ, ʋ nɛ yuŋŋie a kɩɩ yaraa kpɩɛrɩ kala yalɩŋ sɩ hɛyɛ.
11Ʋ bala yɩɛlaa kala daŋ ʋ lɛ nɛ,
ʋ bɩ kʋ-yuŋii kala chɛɛ ka.
12Ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ ʋ yie ŋaa wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ ʋ bala lɛ,
ʋ bɩ wʋbɔŋ ŋaa.
13Ʋ yie kɛŋ pie-pʋnaa arɩ tɩɩ-pugubie-la nɛnɛɛ ba sɩ kaa ŋaa gɛnnɩŋ a ŋɩŋaa gɛnnɩŋ nɛ,
bʋa kala.
14Ʋ nagɛ bayalaa sɩ kɛŋ lɩɩŋ-daborusuŋ tɩtɩŋ nɛ,
a yie mʋ dɩ-bolii a chɛ kʋdiilee kʋkɔ.
15Ʋ yie sii dɩ leriŋ ha bire nɛ,
a ŋaa kʋdiilee pɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa,
aŋ dagɛ haala-la sɩɩ tɩŋ ʋ dɩa lɛ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ jaŋ ŋaa.
16Ʋ yie na tinteeŋ a yɔɔ,
a kɛŋ moribie-la ʋ sɩ tɩma na a chɔnsɛ girep tɩɩsɩŋ baga.
17Ʋ kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ woruŋ,
a chaasa tɩtɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa.
18Ʋ yie na dɩ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la ʋ sɩɩ tɩŋ kɛŋ nyʋʋrʋŋ.
Ʋ tɩŋ ŋɩɩ halɩɩ taŋ siesi.
19Ʋ yie kori kuŋkunuŋ arɩ mɔrʋŋ
aŋ kɛŋ neniee ma kɛŋ jendaaŋ.
20Ʋ yie pɩpɛ summoo
arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ lɛ nɛ.
21Dɩ waarɩŋ nɛ kʋ hɛ nɩmɛ, fawʋllʋŋ bɩ ʋ kɛŋ a tɩŋ ʋ dɩa nɩaa wɩaa,
bɛɛ wɩaa ba kala kɛŋ waarɩŋ gɛnnɩŋ nɛ.
22Ʋ yie ŋaa gɛnnɩŋ ʋ sɩ jaŋ kaa jɩjɛrɛ ʋ kʋpɩnaa nyuŋ nɛ,
aŋ kɛŋ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ arɩ gɛrɩpɛ-vachalɩŋ a yɛrɛ gɛnnɩŋ lɩlaalɛ.
23Ʋ bala yie ŋaa nɩ-jɩmɩɩ nɛ a guoli
ba jaŋ nɩ-hɩasɩŋ tʋɔŋ.
24Ʋ yie kɛŋ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ yɛrɛ gɛnnɩŋ aa yallɛ,
aŋ yallɛ dɔnsʋŋ ma pɩpɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ yallɛ kɩaa.
25Ʋ kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ nɩaa zizilu.
Ʋ bɔyɛ bɩ joŋ a mʋʋ tɩgɛ maachie lɛ.
26Ʋ yie bʋbʋl wɩaa arɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ,
a kɛŋ zile a dɩdagɛ nɩaa woruŋ.
27Ʋ yie bibeŋ ʋ dɩa wɩɩkala nyuŋ woruŋ nɛ.
Ʋ bɩ yarɩ-wɩɩ tɩɩna ŋaa.
28Ʋ biiriŋ yie sii a kɛnʋ yɩyɩrɛ tʋɔtɔrɛ tɩɩna nɛ.
Ʋ bala ma yie bɛsɛ ʋ lɛ a bʋl,
29“Haalaa yʋga nɛ a ŋɩŋaa wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ,
ama ŋ nɛ kɩɩ ba kala.”
30Zɔmʋŋ nyɩsɛ nɩaa nɛ, aŋ lɩlɩɩ ma,
ama haal-la sɩɩ fá La Tɩɩna maga dɩ nʋʋkala bɛsɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ.
31Tɩntɩmɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ tɩma, ʋ maga dɩ ma zilu nɛ,
a bɛsɛ ʋ lɛ nɩaa tʋɔŋ.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
Kʋŋkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ
1Wɩalɩŋ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a dɩdagɛ nɩaa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la. Ʋ fa ŋaa Devit nanʋal nɛ a ŋaa kuoro Jerusalɛm lɛ.
2Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a dɩdagɛ nɩaa sɩ,
“Kʋŋkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,
kʋŋkala chaasa bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,
kʋŋkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ.”
3Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ nuhuobiine yie na,
ʋ sɩ yie faasa tɩma suoli ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ?
4Nɩaa yie sʋsʋʋ nɛ, aŋ ka ba bɩra lʋlʋl dɔnsʋŋ,
ama dʋnɩa ha nagɛ ʋ nagɩsɩŋ nɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.
5Wɩɩ-muluŋ yie pɔsɛ, a tuu jʋʋ,
aŋ bɩra guu mʋ lee-la ʋ sɩ chɩna pɔsɛ.
6Peliŋ yie lu a mʋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ,
aŋ ville mʋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ,
ʋ yie golli golli,
aŋ bɩra mɩɩra mʋ ʋ dɩ-suomuŋ.
7Fuonuŋ kala pɛllɛ hɩhɛ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ lɛ nɛ,
arɩ ŋɩɩ kala ʋ bɩ su.
Lee-la kala fuonu-la sɩ lɩɩ kɔ,
ba yie bɩra mɩɩra mʋ nɩmɛ nɛ.
8Kʋŋkala chaasa lʋlɔl nɛ
a kɩɩ ŋɩɩ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ wuo dagɛ.
Sɩɩŋ nɩna wɩaa ʋ bɩ vɔgɛ,
dɩgɩlɩŋ ma nɩnɩɩ wɩaa ʋ bɩ vɔgɛ.
9Kʋŋkala fa sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ ha jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ.
Wɩalɩŋ sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ a ŋaa nɛ jaŋ bɩra ŋaa.
Wɩɩkala bɩ wʋfalɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ.
10Nʋʋ jaŋ wuo bʋl,
“Má bee na, kʋa deeŋ-na ŋaa kʋfalɩɩ nɛ.”
Ama ʋ fa hɛ nɩmɛ faafaa kala nɛ,
ka ba-na lʋlla.
11Ba bɩ faafaa nɩaa wɩaa ka liisi.
Nɩalɩŋ ma ba ha sɩ jaŋ lʋl,
nɩalɩŋ sɩ tɩgɛ ba lɛ,
ma paala bɩ jaŋ liisi ba wɩaa.
Wʋjɩmɩŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ
12Mɩ-na nɩɩ-la sɩ dagɛ nɩaa nɛ fa dii Iziral tinteeŋ kuoruŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ. 13Mɩ fa joŋ mɩ nyuŋ kala nɛ hɛ dɩ mɩ gʋnnɛ a kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a chɛ na wɩɩkala sɩ hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ. Chʋgʋ yuŋii nɛ Wɩa joŋo daŋ nuhuobiine nyuŋ. 14Mɩ na dɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ba nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.
15Ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo tʋrɛ kʋŋ sɩ golibo,
dɩ kʋŋ nɛ tuo, ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo dɩɩsʋ.
16Mɩ bɩɩna mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ, “Bee na, mɩ waa nɛ mɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ lɛ a kɩɩ nʋʋ na-kala sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ mɩ lɛ a dii kuoruŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ. Mɩ gʋnnɛ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ kɩŋkɛŋ a jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa.” 17Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ joŋ mɩ nyuŋ kala hɛ dɩ mɩ jɩŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ arɩ yaarɩŋ pɛgɛ, a jɩŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ arɩ chʋʋlʋŋ pɛgɛ. Ama mɩ na dɩ ŋɩɩ ma nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.
18Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ kɩŋkɛŋ,
wɩaa yie faasa walɩmɩŋ nɛ.
Dɩ ŋ nɛ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa ma kɩŋkɛŋ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ wɩaa ma yie wʋwɩɩŋ.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Tʋɔtɔrʋŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ
1Mɩ bɩɩna mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ, “Mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ ŋaa wɩaa a na sɩma-la sɩ hɛ ʋ lɛ.” Ama mɩ na dɩ ŋɩɩ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ. 2Mɩ sɩ, “Mɔmʋŋ ŋaa nɩyaarɛ wɩɩ nɛ.” Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ kaa kʋkɔ? 3Mɩ bɩɩna mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ arɩ mɩ nɛ nyʋa sɩnɩŋ mɩ yaraa jaŋ nyaasɛ dɩ mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ, ka dɩ mɩ ha kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ. Mɩ faa chɛ dɩ mɩ na wɩɩ-la sɩ zɔmɔ a magɛ dɩ nuhuobiine ŋaa tapʋlɩa-la baŋmɛnɛ, ʋ sɩ hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ dʋnɩa lɛ nɛ.
4Mɩ tɩŋ tɩntɩŋ daŋ nɛ: Mɩ saa dɩɩsɩŋ a bil girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ. 5Mɩ pɛrɛ ŋmaŋkaanɩŋ nɛ a chɔnsɛ tɩɩsɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ fɩɛlɩŋ arɩ tɩɩ-dosunu-la nɛnɛɛ ba sɩɩ dii. 6Mɩ lu vilee a ŋaa ba lɩɩŋ hɩhɛ tɩɩ-daŋ-la. 7Mɩ yɔɔ yosuŋ, baalaa arɩ haalaa a pɛ yosu-la ma ba sɩ lʋla mɩ dɩa lɛ. Mɩ bɩra kɛŋ nɛsɩŋ arɩ piesee a kɩɩ nʋʋ na-kala sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ mɩ lɛ. 8Mɩ dʋa sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla chʋɔrɛ nɛ, aŋ laa dɔnsʋŋ ma kuoroo arɩ leree dɔnsʋŋ nɩaa teeŋ. Mɩ kɛŋ yɩɩlɩ yɩɩraa baalaa arɩ haalaa, mɩ kɛŋ haala-la kala baala sɩ yie cho dɩ ʋ kɛnɛ nɛ. 9Mɩ ŋaa nɩbal nɛ kɩŋkɛŋ, a kɩɩ nʋʋ na-kala sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ mɩ lɛ. Wɩaa deemba kala wʋjɩmɩŋ harɩŋ nɛ mɩ to.
10Mɩ bɩ kʋŋkala mɩ sɩɩŋ sɩ na a cho vɩa,
mɩ bɩ mɩ tʋɔtɔrɛ wɩaa vɩa.
Mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la kala mɩ sɩ tɩma lɛ nɛ.
Wɩɩŋ deeŋ nɛ ŋaa mɩ tɩŋŋaa kala time.
11Mɩ sɩ kɛŋ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ ŋaa bɩɩnɛ
arɩ ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ faasa tɩŋ a na kɩaa,
mɩ na dɩ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ ŋaa bɩ bʋbʋɔŋ kɛnɛ.
Ʋ nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ,
kʋŋkala bɩ nyʋʋrɩ kɛnɛ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ.
Wʋjɩmɩŋ arɩ yaarɩŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ
12Dɩ kuoro nɛ tuo ka dɩ nʋʋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ,
bɛɛ nɛ ʋ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ ŋaa aŋ ka dee?
Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ suomo kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ,
chʋʋlʋŋ arɩ yaarɩŋ wɩaa a bɩbɩɩnɛ.
13Mɩ na dɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ kpɩa yaarɩŋ,
a nagɛ pʋlʋmʋŋ sɩ kpɩa birimiŋ ŋɩɩ.
14Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ na lee-la ʋ sɩɩ mʋ nɛ,
ka nɩyaara-na vɩvɛŋ birimiŋ tʋɔŋ.
Ama mɩ kʋ jɩŋ
dɩ wʋbala nɛ jaŋ ŋaa ba kala lɛ ba dɩdɛrɩŋ.
15Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋl mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ,
“Wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa nɩyaarɩŋ lɛ nɛ, jaŋ ŋaa mɩ ma lɛ.
Bɛɛ kʋŋ nyʋʋrʋŋ nɛ mɩ saa jaŋ na dɩ mɩ nɛ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ?”
Mɩ bɩra bʋl mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ,
“Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔŋ kɛnɛ.”
16Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ arɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ yaara kala,
ba bɩ jaŋ liliisi ba wɩaa deeŋ deeŋ.
Bʋa kʋbala jaŋ yi dɩ ba yʋ ba wɩaa.
Nɩyaarɩŋ sʋʋ nɛ, wʋjɩnna maa sʋʋ.
Ŋ sɩ tɩma lɔl kɩŋkɛŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ
17Ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ mɩɩsɩŋ fɩɩ dʋnɩa wɩaa nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa tɩntɩmɩɩ-la kala la sɩɩ tɩŋ ŋaa hɛɛ nɛ mɩ teeŋ. Ʋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ. 18Kɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ tɩma lɔl a na dʋnɩa lɛ, mɩ bɩra bɩ ba cho, bɛɛ wɩaa mɩ jaŋ lemba pɩ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ, dɩ mɩ nɛ tuo. 19Nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ jɩŋ dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ ŋaa wʋjɩnnʋ koo nɩyaarɩ. Ka ʋ nɛ jaŋ dii kɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ kɛŋ mɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ faasa tɩma na dʋnɩa lɛ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ. 20Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ wɩɩmɛ, mɩ sɩ faasa tɩma lɔl ŋɩɩ dʋnɩa lɛ. 21Nuhuobiine yie kɛŋ ʋ wʋjɩmɩŋ, ʋ wɩaa sɩaa jɩmɩŋ arɩ ʋ jɩma kala a tɩma na kɩaa, aŋ leŋ kɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ na pɩ nʋʋ sɩ bɩ tɩma chɛ kɩalɩŋ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ ŋaa naabɔŋ bal nɛ. 22Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ nuhuobiine na, ʋ sɩ yie walɩmɛ ʋ tɩtɩa a faasa tɩma lɔl dʋnɩa lɛ? 23Tapʋlɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ yie tɩŋ a na hɛɛŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ chei, tɩtaŋɩŋ ma ʋ tʋɔbɩɩnaa bɩ leŋe ʋ wiwiesi. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ.
24Nuhuobiine bɩ jaŋ wuo nɩɩ sɩma kala ʋ tɩntɩŋŋaa lɛ, a pɛ ʋ sɩ na kɩaa dii aŋ nyʋa lɛ. Mɩ na dɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma lɩɩ Wɩa teeŋ nɛ. 25Dɩ Wɩa nɛ tuo, kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo na kɩaa dii koo a nɩɩ sɩma? 26Wɩa yie joŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ, wɩaa sɩaa jɩmɩŋ arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ a pɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa wɩaa a tʋtɔrɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ nɛ. Ama wʋbɔŋ ŋaara-na Wɩa yie leŋ ʋ tɩŋ nɛ a chɛ kɩaa tʋɔla bil, ʋ joŋo pɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa wɩaa a tʋtɔrɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_text:
Bʋa na-kala arɩ ʋ wɩɩ nɛ
1Wɩɩ na-kala kɛŋ ʋ bʋa nɛ,
wɩɩ na-kala sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ kɛŋ bʋa-la sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa nɛ:
2Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ lʋl nɩa arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.
Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ chɔnsɛ kɩaa arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ churi.
3Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ kpʋ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ tɩɩbɛ.
Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ ŋmoo lo arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ saa.
4Bʋa-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ yel arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ mɔŋ.
Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ ŋmoo niiŋ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ gbieli.
5Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ kɛŋ tabɩaa pɩsɛ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ gbaaba hɛ dɔŋɔ.
Bʋa-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ guori dɔŋɔ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ pɔrɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ.
6Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ chɛ kɩaa arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ leŋe ta.
Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ bil kʋa arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ joŋo yuo ta.
7Bʋa-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ kɛŋ kʋa kɩɛsɛ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ yɛrɛ.
Bʋa-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ tɔrɛ ba niiŋ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩaa.
8Bʋa-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ cho dɔŋɔ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ bɛrɛ dɔŋɔ.
Bʋa-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ yuo laalɩŋ arɩ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ hɔŋ arɩ fɩɛlɩŋ.
9Tɩntɩnna sɩ yie tɩma lɔl, bɛɛ nyʋʋrɩ nɛ ʋ yie na? 10Mɩ na dɩ chʋgʋ yuŋŋii nɛ Wɩa joŋo daŋ nuhuobiine nyuŋ. 11Ʋ ŋaa kʋŋkala ʋ bʋa-la lɛ nɛ, a leŋ ʋ zɔŋ. Wɩa nɛ joŋ wɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ wuu tʋɔbɩɩnaa a pɩ nuhuobiine, aŋ bɩ leŋe ba chaasa jɩŋ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa a chɩŋ dɩ-suomuŋ a kaa mʋ dɩ-dɛrɩŋ. 12Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ jɩŋ dɩ nuhuobiine mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ kʋŋkala tuo a kpɩa tʋɔtɔrʋŋ arɩ wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ. 13Nʋʋkala maga dɩ ʋ dii aŋ nyʋa a nɩɩ kɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ tɩma na sɩma, Wɩa nɛ pʋ. 14Mɩ jɩma kʋŋkala Wɩa sɩ ŋaa jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ a kaa mʋ wuu. Nʋʋ bɩ kʋŋ wuo kaa pɛ nʋʋ bɩ kʋŋ wuo kaa lɩɩsa ta ma. Wɩa ŋaa ŋɩɩ dɩ nɩaa fɩfáʋ nɛ.
15Wɩɩ-la kala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ, laa sɩpaaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ nɛ,
wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa maachie, laa sɩpaaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ nɛ.
Wɩa yie leŋ wɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa faafaa kala, bɩra ŋaa nɛ.
16Mɩ na wɩɩ dɔŋ ma nɛ dʋnɩa lɛ:
Sarɩya dɩ-diiliŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ, mɩ na wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ hɛ nɩmɛ.
Lee-la sɩ maga dɩ ba ŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ, mɩ na wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɩmɛ.
17Mɩ bɩɩnɛ mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ,
“Wɩa jaŋ dii tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa
arɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ kala sarɩya,
bɛɛ wɩaa wɩɩkala kɛŋ bʋa nɛ,
wʋŋaalɩɩ ma kala kɛŋ ba bʋa.”
18Mɩ bɩra bɩɩnɛ mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ, “Wɩa ka magɩsɛ nuhuobiinee dɩ ʋ dagɛ arɩ ba ma nagɛ pʋsʋŋ nɛ. 19Nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋŋ kala wɩɩŋ ŋaa kʋbala nɛ, wʋbala nɛ gbɛrɛ ba kala: Dɔŋɔ sɩɩ sʋʋ ŋɩɩ, ŋɩɩ nɛ dɔŋɔ ma sʋsʋʋ. Ba kala ka wiesi nɛ. Nuhuobiine ma bɩ pʋna lɛ kpɩa, kʋŋkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ. 20Ba kalaa mʋ dɩ-bala nɛ, ba kala lɩɩ hagɩla lɛ nɛ, ba kala jaŋ bɩra bɩrɩmɛ hagɩla. 21Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jɩma dɩ nuhuobiine dɩma ka jɩl wɩa-nyuŋ nɛ, aŋ ka pʋna kʋa tutuu tinteeŋ?”
22Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ mɩ na dɩ kʋŋkala tuo a kpɩa nuhuobiine teeŋ, a kɩɩ ʋ sɩ jaŋ kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ tɩma na a nɩɩ sɩma, ʋ kpaalɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ. Nʋʋkala tuo sɩ jaŋ kɛŋ nʋʋ sɩ sʋba mɩɩra kɔ dɩ ʋ na wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋaa ʋ harɩŋ.

english_text:
1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Nɩaa nyagɛ dɔŋɔ bil
1Mɩ bɩra beŋ, a na nɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ nyaga bil dʋnɩa lɛ:
Mɩ na ŋɩɩ nɩalɩŋ ba sɩ nyaga bil sɩɩ yel sɩlɩɩrɩŋ,
ka nʋʋkala tuo dɩ ʋ nyagɛ ba bɔyɛ.
Nɩalɩŋ sɩ nyagɛba bil kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ,
ka nɩalɩŋ ba sɩ nyaga bil bɩ nʋʋ kɛnɛ dɩ ʋ nyagɛ ba bɔyɛ.
2Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋl mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ:
Nɩalɩŋ sɩ sʋba nɛ kɛŋ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ
a kɩɩ nɩalɩŋ ha sɩ weye.
3Ama nɩɩ-la sɩ kpɩa ba kala nɛ,
nɩɩ-la ba ha sɩ bɩ lʋla,
nɩɩ-la ha sɩ bɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la
ba sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ na.
4Mɩ bɩra na dɩ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la kala nɩaa sɩɩ tɩŋ arɩ kɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ yie na lɩɩ ba yaraa sɩɩ bieri ba dɔŋɔ nyuŋ nɛ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.
5Nɩyaarɩŋ nɛ yie paa ʋ vaasɩŋ vɔɔ hɔŋ
aŋ sʋʋ losuŋ.
6Nʋʋ sɩ bɩ faasa lɔl,
aŋ na kɩaa nɩsɩŋ sɩɩŋ nɛ kpɩa nʋʋ sɩ lɔlɔ kɩŋkɛŋ aŋ na kɩaa nɩsɩŋ sɩɩŋ bʋlɩa,
tɩɩna nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.
7Wɩɩ dɔŋ ma nɛ mɩ bɩra na dʋnɩa lɛ sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ:
8Baal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ ʋ dʋndʋŋ,
ʋ bɩ bii kɛnɛ, ʋ bɩ naambii ma kɛnɛ,
aŋ ka ʋ lɔlʋŋ fa bɩ dɛrɛ,
ʋ sɩɩŋ fa bɩ ʋ dʋa ka su.
Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ pɩɛsɛ ʋ tɩtɩa,
“Kʋbɛɛ nɛ mɩ lɔlɔ pɩpa,
bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ bɩ chɛ dɩ nɩɩ kɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ kɛnɛ sɩma?”
Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,
tʋɔ-chei tɩntɩmɩɩ nɛ.
9Nɩaa balɩa nɛ kpɩa nɩbala,
bɛɛ wɩaa dɩ ba nɛ gbaara tɩŋ, ba yie na kɩaa yʋgɛ nɛ.
10Dɩ dɔŋɔ nɛ tele,
dɔŋɔ jaŋ wuo kɛnʋ dɩ ʋ sii.
Ama dɩ nʋʋ nɛ tele
aŋ bɩ nʋʋ kɛnɛ dɩ ʋ pɛ ʋ lɛ dɩ ʋ sii, ŋɩɩ kɛŋ nenige nɛ.
11Dɩ nɩaa balɩa nɛ pɩna ma, baa tɔ dɔŋɔ waarɩŋ nɛ.
Ama dɩ nɩbala nɛ pɩna, waarɩŋ jaŋ kɛnʋ.
12Nʋʋ jaŋ wuo ŋmoo nɩbala,
ama dɩ ba nɛ ŋaa balɩa, ʋ bɩ jaŋ wuoba.
Ŋmɛŋ-biee batori bɩ ŋɩɩ lɩmaa kɛrɛ.
Nyaaŋ arɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ wɩaa
13Bapʋɔsɛ-bie sɩ nyaaba aŋ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ, ʋ nɛ kpɩa kuoro sɩ hɩɛsa aŋ yaarɛ a bɩra bɩ sɛɩ dɩ ba chagɩlʋ. 14Dɩ ba lʋl bapʋɔsɛ-bie-la hɛ sunnuŋ lɛ nɛ koo dɩ ʋ lɩɩ bɩnɩŋ dɩa lɛ nɛ, ʋ jaŋ wuo dii kuoruŋ. 15Mɩ na dɩ nɩaa kala sɩ hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ ka to bapʋɔsɛ-bie kʋbala sɩ dii kuoruŋ harɩŋ. 16Nɩaa fa yʋga a bɩ nii kɛnɛ a tuto ʋ harɩŋ. Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ to harɩŋ kɔ tʋɔŋ bɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ laa kuoru-la nyuŋ tɔrɔ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Fɩfá Wɩa
1Dɩ ŋ nɛ mʋ Wɩa dɩa, kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa woruŋ. Mʋ kpagɛ a jegile nɩɩ wɩaa woruŋ. Ʋ nɛ kpɩa ŋ sɩ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a nagɛ nɩyaaraa sɩɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, aŋ bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ ŋaa ʋ bʋa lɛ dee ŋɩɩ.
2Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ŋ niiŋ lɩŋ,
sɩ́ pese hɛ niiŋ Wɩa teeŋ.
Wɩa hɛ ʋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ,
ka ŋ ma hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ,
ŋɩɩ wɩaa sɩ́ wʋdaŋ bʋl.
3Dɩ wʋwalɩmaa nɛ yʋga ŋ lɛ, ŋ jaŋ duduosi duosi bɔŋŋɔɔ.
Dɩ ŋ nɛ bʋl wɩaa yʋgɛ, ŋ jaŋ bʋl nɩyaarɩ wɩaa.
4Dɩ ŋ nɛ ta niiŋ Wɩa teeŋ, sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ʋ dieni ka dɩ ŋ lɩɩsɛ nii-la. Ʋ tʋɔŋ bɩ nɩyaaraa nyuŋ ka tɔrɛ. Lɩɩsɛ nii-la ŋ sɩ ta. 5Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩ niiŋ ta, ʋ nɛ kpɩa ŋ sɩ ta niiŋ aŋ bɩ lɩɩsa. 6Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ŋ niiŋ wʋbʋlaa kɛnɩŋ hɛ wʋbɔmʋŋ lɛ. Pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ bʋla pɩ Wɩa tɩntɩnna, “Nii-la mɩ sɩ ta, mɩ perige nɛ.” Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ŋ wʋbʋlaa ŋaa dɩ Wɩa na baanɩŋ ŋ nyuŋ a chei ŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa. 7Tʋɔbɩɩnaa kɩŋkɛŋ arɩ wʋbʋl daŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ. Fɩfá Wɩa.
Kɩaa kɛnɩŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ
8Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ʋ ŋaa wʋkpuŋkpere ŋ lɛ, dɩ ŋ nɛ na dɩ ba nyagɛ summoo bil ma tinteeŋ lɛ, aŋ vɩa wʋtɩtɩɩ arɩ wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba joŋo ŋaa ba lɛ ta, bɛɛ wɩaa tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ kala kɛŋ nɩhɩaŋ nɛ ʋ bibenu. Ka ba kala ha kɛŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ ba bibemba. 9Tinteeŋ sɩ kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ ŋaa nʋʋkala kɩaa nɛ, kuoro ma tɩtɩa yie na kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ pɛrɛ nyʋʋrʋŋ nɛ.
10Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ cho moribiee bɩ moribiee ka vɔgɛ.
Nɩɩ-la ma kala sɩ cho dʋa bɩ kɩaa ka vɔgɛ.
Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ.
11Dɩ kɩaa nɛ pʋŋa pɛ,
diiree ma yie pʋŋa pɛ nɛ.
Nɩɩ-la sɩ tɩɩba bɩ nyʋʋrɩ kala kɛnɛ,
ʋ wɩɩŋ nɛ dɩ ʋ tuo bibeŋ.
12Tɩntɩnna doŋ pɩnɩŋ nɛ sɩma,
dɩ ʋ dii kɩaa vɔgɛ koo dɩ ʋ bɩ vɔgɔ.
Ama kɩaa tɩɩna
dʋa bɩ leŋe ʋ pɩpɩŋ doŋ.
13Wʋbɔŋ sɩ chaasa lɔrɛ nɛ mɩ na dʋnɩa lɛ:
Kɩaa tɩɩna joŋ dʋa bil nɛ, ʋ bɩrɩmɛ ʋ nyu-bɔŋ.
14Naabɔmʋŋ jʋʋ dʋa-la nɛ ʋ lɛl,
ʋ bɩ kʋŋkala leŋe bil ʋ biiriŋ lɛ.
15Ba lʋl nuhuobiine arɩ yarɩ-biree nɛ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ ʋ jaŋ bɩra kaa mʋ.
Ʋ bɩ kɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ tɩma na kʋŋkala wuo kaa pɛ mʋmʋ.
16Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma ŋaa wʋbɔŋ sɩ chaasa lɔrɛ nɛ:
Nuhuobiine sɩ kɛŋ ŋɩɩ kɔ dʋnɩa,
ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bɩra kaa mʋ.
Ʋ bɩ nyʋʋrɩ kala na,
ʋ lɔlɔ ta nɛ.
17Ʋ na hɛɛŋ nɛ ʋ tapʋlaa kala lɛ,
a kɛŋ tʋɔ-cheeŋ kɩŋkɛŋ,
wʋwalɩmaa, ʋ baanɩŋ sisii arɩ nyanyalaa.
18Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ jɩŋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ nɛ a magɛ dɩ nuhuobiine dii aŋ nyʋa, a nɩɩ sɩma ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ tapʋlɩa-la baŋmɛnɛ Wɩa sɩ joŋo pʋ ʋ kaa tɩma lɔl dʋnɩa lɛ a na kɩalɩŋ. Ʋ kpaalɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ. 19Dɩ Wɩa nɛ joŋ dʋa pɩ nuhuobiine dɩ ʋ kɛŋ kɩaa, a wuo leŋ ʋ nɩɩ kɩalɩŋ sɩma, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ nɛ ʋ sɩ nɩɩ kɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ tɩma na sɩma. Wɩa nɛ joŋo pʋ. 20Wɩa sɩ folo leŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ, ʋ bɩra bɩ jaŋ liliisi ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ tapʋlaa wɩaa kɩŋkɛŋ.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
1Wʋbɔŋ dɔŋɔ ma nɛ mɩ na dʋnɩa lɛ, ʋ yuŋŋie nɛ woruŋ a daŋ nuhuobiinee nyuŋ: 2Wɩa yie joŋ dʋa a pɩ nʋʋ ʋ kɛŋ kɩaa ba zizilu, dɩ ʋ sɩ́ kʋŋkala ʋ sɩ cho chɛ ka. Ama Wɩa yie bɩ leŋe ʋ nɩnɩɩ ba sɩma, ka nɩwogo mɩɩra nɩnɩɩ ba sɩma. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ sɩ chaasa lɔrɛ nɛ.
3Nʋʋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ biiriŋ zɔlɔ a hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ jɩ-daŋ, ama ʋ sɩ diene ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ a magɛ ŋɩɩ ma kala, dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ wuo dii ʋ dʋa sɩma, ka ba bɩra bɩ ʋ woruŋ ma hugo, mɩ jaŋ bʋl arɩ bii-sʋʋŋ ba sɩ lʋla nɛ kpɩaʋ. 4Bile-na kɔɔnʋŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, ʋ to birimiŋ lɛ nɛ a viiri, ʋ bɩ yɩrɩŋ kɛnɛ. 5Ʋ sɩ bɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ na ma kala, a bɩ wɩɩkala jɩŋ, ʋ nɛ ha na wiese a kɩɩ nɩɩ-la, 6dɩ nɩɩ-la nɛ paala hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ bʋɩ balɩa ma, aŋ bɩ wuo nɩɩ kɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ kɛnɛ sɩma, dɩ-bala nɛ ba kala mʋmʋ.
7Nuhuobiine yie tɩtɩŋ dɩ ʋ na kɩaa nɛ a dii,
ama ʋ ha bɩ vɔgɛ.
8Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ wʋjɩnna kaa
kpɩa nɩyaarɩŋ lɛ?
Bɛɛ kʋŋ nyʋʋrɩ nɛ summo sɩ jɩŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kɛnɩŋ
nɩaa tʋɔŋ yie na?
9Dɩ ŋ sɩɩŋ nɛ su kʋ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ nɛ kpɩa
ŋ sɩɩ hɩɛnɛ kʋŋ ŋ sɩ bɩ kɛnɛ.
Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,
ʋ nagɛ nʋʋ sɩɩ kiri peliŋ nɛ.
10Kʋŋkala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ laa sɩpaaŋ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ,
la kala jɩŋ ŋɩɩ nuhuobiine sɩ naga nɛ.
Ŋ dɩ nʋʋ sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ
a kɩɩŋ bɩ kaalɛrɛ wuo kɛŋ.
11Wʋbʋl kɩŋkɛŋ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,
ŋɩɩ saa bɩ nyʋʋrɩ kɛnɛ nʋʋkala teeŋ.
12Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la sɩ zɔmɔ a pɩ nuhuobiine, ʋ sɩ hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ tapʋlɩa-la baŋmɛnɛ sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, a bɩbal a nagɛ daaliimiŋ? Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo bʋl wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa ʋ lɛ dɩ ʋ nɛ lɩɩ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
Wʋjɩmɩŋ
1Yɩrɩ zɔmʋŋ nɛ kpɩa tʋlaalɩ-zɔmʋŋ.
Tapʋlɩɩ-la nʋʋ sɩ sʋba nɛ kpɩa tapʋlɩɩ-la ba sɩ lʋlʋ.
2Nʋʋ sɩ mʋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yel
nɛ kpɩa nʋʋ sɩ mʋ lee-la ba sɩ dii kɩaa a gbigbieli,
bɛɛ wɩaa sʋʋŋ ŋaa nuhuobiiŋ kala kʋŋ nɛ.
Nʋʋkala sɩ weye maga dɩ ʋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ lɛ.
3Tʋɔ-cheeŋ nɛ kpɩa mɔmʋŋ,
bɛɛ wɩaa tʋɔ-cheeŋ jaŋ wuo leŋ nɩaa gʋnnɛ wʋjɩmɩŋ.
4Wʋjɩnna ka bɩɩnɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yel wɩaa nɛ,
ama nɩyaara-na yie bɩbɩɩnɛ lee-la tʋɔtɔrʋŋ sɩ hɛ wɩaa nɛ.
5Wʋjɩnna sɩ kpɩa ŋ lɛ,
ʋ nɛ kpɩa ŋ nɩyaarɩŋ sɩ bɛsɛ ŋ lɛ.
6A nagɛ ba sɩ joŋ sɔsʋŋ hɛ nyiniŋ lɛ ba pʋpɔsɛ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩyaarɩŋ mɔmʋŋ nagɛ.
Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔŋ kɛnɛ.
7Gɩrɩma dii nɛ yie leŋ wʋjɩnna bɩrɩmɛ nɩyaarɩŋ.
Kpalaa laanɩŋ ka chei nɩaa nɛ.
8Wɩɩŋ dɩdɛrɩŋ nɛ kpɩa ʋ dɩ-suomuŋ,
kenyiri ma nɛ kpɩa babii-ballɩŋ.
9Sɩ́ guu nɩna baanɩŋ,
bɛɛ wɩaa nɩyaarɩŋ nɛ yie guu na baanɩŋ.
10Ʋ bɩ wʋjɩŋ wɩɩ ŋaa dɩ ŋ pɩɛsɛ,
“Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ faafaa kpɩa lɛɛlɛ?”
11Wʋjɩmɩŋ ŋaa kʋzɔŋ nɛ, a nagɛ ŋ sɩ dii dʋa.
Ʋ kɛŋ nyʋʋrʋŋ a pɩ dʋnɩa nɩaa.
12Wʋjɩmɩŋ jaŋ wuo pɔŋ
a nagɛ moribiee sɩ jaŋ wuo pɔŋ ŋɩɩ.
Ama wʋjɩmɩŋ wɩɩŋ nɛ ŋ-la:
Ʋ yie pɔ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛnʋ mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ.
13Kɛŋ wɩalɩŋ Wɩa sɩ ŋaa a bɩɩna na.
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ kʋŋ
ʋ sɩ ŋaa ʋ golibi a tʋrɛ?
14Dɩ wɩaa nɛ vɛŋ woruŋ a pɩŋ, leŋ dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ,
ama dɩ wɩaa nɛ bɩra lɔrɔ ma, kaa bɩɩna na.
Wɩa nɛ ŋaa ba kala.
Ŋɩɩ wɩaa nuhuobiine bɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa wɩɩkala
a mʋ tɩgɛ ʋ chiemiŋ lɛ.
15Mɩ na wɩaa deemba kala nɛ mɩ mɩɩsɩŋ deeŋ sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ lɛ mɩ sɩ hɛ:
Mɩ na dɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna sɩɩ ŋaa tʋɔpʋl wɩaa aŋ buuro sʋʋ,
a bɩra na nɩbɔmʋŋ ma sɩɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ
aŋ ha hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ a dieni.
16Sɩ́ ŋ tɩtɩa joŋ arɩ ŋ faasa ŋaa tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna nɛ,
koo dɩ ŋ ŋaa wʋjɩnnʋ kɩŋkɛŋ tɩɩna.
Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ŋ chei ŋ tɩtɩa?
17Sɩ́ faasa ŋaa nɩbɔŋ
a bɩra sɩ́ nɩyaarɩ ma ŋaa.
Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ chɛ dɩ ŋ sʋʋ,
dɩ ŋ sʋʋŋ bɩ yie?
18Ʋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ nɛ dɩ ŋ hɛ wɩaa deemba balɩa pɛgɛ.
Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ fá Wɩa nɛ jaŋ wuo lɩɩ ba kala lɛ.
19Wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ yie leŋ wʋjɩnna kɛŋ doluŋ
a kɩɩ nɩduoruŋ fii sɩɩ beŋ tabalɩŋ.
20Tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna kala tuo dʋnɩa lɛ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ,
a ha bɩ wʋbɔŋ kala ŋaa.
21Sɩ́ wɩɩkala nɩaa sɩɩ bʋl jegilu,
ŋɩɩ dee ŋ jaŋ nɩɩ dɩ ŋ tɩntɩnna bʋl wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a tɩgɛ ŋ lɛ.
22Ŋ tɩtɩa jɩma ŋ tʋɔŋ lɛ dɩ ŋ bʋl
wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ yʋgɛ nɛ a tɩgɛ nɩaa lɛ.
23Mɩ kɛŋ mɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ a kaa magɩsɛ wɩaa deemba kala na a bʋl:
Mɩ faa chɛ dɩ mɩ ŋaa wʋjɩnnʋ nɛ,
ama wɩɩŋ deeŋ kɩɩmɛ nɛ.
24Wʋjɩmɩŋ bolie, a luŋ ma.
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo jɩŋ ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ?
25Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ joŋ mɩ nyuŋ hɛ dɩ mɩ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa,
a gbille chɛ wʋjɩmɩŋ dɩ mɩ na ŋɩɩ wɩaa sɩɩ vɛŋ,
a bɩra chɩchɛ dɩ mɩ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ bɔnsʋŋ sɩ naga
arɩ ŋɩɩ chʋʋlʋŋ sɩ naga.
26Mɩ na dɩ ha-bɔmʋŋ nɛ bɔmɔ kɩɩ sʋʋŋ,
Ʋ nagɛ bɛrɛ nɛ. Ʋ nɩsɩŋ nagɛ chɔrʋmɔɔ nɛ.
Nɩɩ-la wʋŋaalaa sɩ tɔrɛ Wɩa tʋɔŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ jaŋ fori ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.
Ama wʋbɔŋ ŋaara-na ʋ jaŋ bɛrɛ kɛnʋ.
27Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a dɩdagɛ nɩaa sɩ,
“Má bee na, wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ chɛ na nɛ ŋ-la:
Mɩ joŋ wɩɩ nɛ a pɛ wɩɩ-la lɛ dɩ mɩ na wɩaa sɩɩ vɛŋ ŋɩɩ,
28mɩ haa gbillu nɛ,
ama mɩ ha bɩ ba sɩaa na.
Mɩ na dɩ nɩaa bʋɩ tʋɔŋ ba-bala dʋndʋŋ nɩɩ ŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ.
Ama ha-bala ma tuo ba kala tʋɔŋ.
29Wʋbala-la mɩ sɩ na nɛ ŋ la:
Wɩa ŋaa nuhuobiine ʋ tʋʋlɛ nɛ.
Ama ʋ mɩɩra kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa a kperi nɛ.”

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Kʋbɛɛ nɛ nagɛ wʋjɩnnʋ?
Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo chaarɛ wɩaa sɩaa woruŋ?
Wʋjɩmɩŋ yie leŋ nɩa sɩaa chaanɛ nɛ,
a kɛŋ tɩɩna sɩɩ-nyalaa bɩrɩmɛ.
To kuoro niiŋ
2To kuoro wʋdagaa, a tɩŋ nii-la ŋ sɩ ta Wɩa sɩpaaŋ wɩaa. 3Sɩ́ pipesu dɩ ŋ sii kuoro sɩpaaŋ. Sɩ́ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ʋ harɩŋ chɩna lɛ pɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ jaŋ wuo ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ cho. 4Kuoro nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa. Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ ŋ ŋɩŋaa ŋɩɩ?”
5Nɩɩ-la kala sɩɩ to ʋ wʋdagaa bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ wɩɩ.
Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ jɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩɩŋ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaaʋ nɛ.
6Wɩɩkala kɛŋ bʋa-la lɛ sɩ maga dɩ ba ŋaaʋ arɩ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ jaŋ ŋaaʋ nɛ.
Ama wʋjʋʋlaa nyagɛ nuhuobiine kɩŋkɛŋ nɛ.
7Nʋʋkala bɩ maachie jɩŋ,
kʋbɛɛ nɛ saa jaŋ wuo bʋl wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ kɔ?
8Nʋʋkala bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ dɩ ʋ wuo kɛŋ peliŋ bil.
Nʋʋkala bɩ tapʋlɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ doluŋ kɛnɛ.
Laalɩŋ tapʋlʋŋ nʋʋkala bɩ fori,
wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ma bɩ jaŋ laa nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋaaba ta.
9Mɩ sɩ na wɩaa deemba kala, mɩ kɛŋ wɩalɩŋ kala sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ kaa chɔ na. Bʋa dɔŋɔ nʋʋ yie kɛŋ doluŋ nɩaa nyuŋ a bibemba, a leŋ ba nɩna hɛɛŋ. 10Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bɩra na dɩ ba paa nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ lɩɩ lee-la sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ lɛ a kaa mʋ sʋʋnʋŋ dɩ-huguŋ a hugi. Nɩaa bɩbɛsɛ ba lɛ tabal-la lɛ tɩtɩa ba sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ. 11Dɩ ba nɛ bɩ nʋʋ sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ dɔgʋsɔ lɩma, nɩaa yie bɩbɩɩnɛ ba ŋɩŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ.
12Dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ jaŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ zɔlɔ aŋ ha hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ a dieni, mɩ jɩma nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ fá Wɩa a zizilu, ba-na wɩaa jaŋ vɛŋ woruŋ pɩba. 13Ama wɩaa bɩ jaŋ vɛŋ woruŋ a pɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ-na. Ba mɩɩsɩŋ bɩ jaŋ duomi, a nagɛ daaliimiŋ sɩ yie duomo pɩpɛ ŋɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba bɩ Wɩa ka fá.
14Wɩɩ dɔŋ ma nɛ bɩra ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ a bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ: Ba yie joŋ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ time a tiŋ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa lɛ, aŋ joŋ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa time a tiŋ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ. Mɩ sɩ, wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ. 15Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bɩɩnɛ arɩ nuhuobiine mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ ʋ maga ʋ dii aŋ nyʋa nɛ a nɩɩ sɩma dɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa kʋŋkala bɩra tuo dʋnɩa lɛ a kpɩa ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ jaŋ hɛ ʋ teeŋ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala ʋ sɩɩ tɩŋ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ tapʋlɩa-la Wɩa sɩ joŋo pʋ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ.
16Mɩ sɩ joŋ mɩ nyuŋ hɛ dɩ mɩ gbilli wʋjɩmɩŋ, aŋ-na tɩŋ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la kala nɩaa sɩɩ tɩŋ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ, mɩ bɩ doŋ wuo pɩŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ arɩ tɩtaŋɩŋ kala. 17Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ na dɩ wɩalɩŋ kala Wɩa sɩ ŋaa, nʋʋkala tuo sɩ jɩŋ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ sɩaa. Dɩ nʋʋ nɩɩ walɩmɛ dɩ ʋ jɩŋ ma, ʋ bɩ jaŋ wuo jɩŋ ba bʋbʋɔŋ. Dɩ wʋjɩnnʋ kala nɛ paala bʋl dɩ ʋ jɩma ma, ʋ bɩ wuo chaasaa jɩŋ.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
Sʋʋŋ nɛ la kala dɩdɛrɩŋ
1Mɩ sɩ kɛŋ wɩaa deemba kala a bɩɩnɛ, ʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ mɩ na dɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa arɩ wʋjɩnnaa arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩɩ ŋaa hɛ Wɩa nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ. Ama nʋʋkala bɩ jɩŋ dɩ chonuŋ nɛ koo dɩ bɛrɩŋ nɛ ba kaa gbɛrʋ. 2Sʋʋŋ nɛ la kala dɩdɛrɩŋ, tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ, wʋzɔŋ ŋaaraa arɩ wʋbɔŋ ŋaaraa, nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ, nɩalɩŋ sɩ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a sʋsʋl Wɩa arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ŋɩɩ ŋaa.
Ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ naga wʋzɔŋ ŋaara lɛ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ nagɛ wʋbɔŋ ŋaara ma lɛ.
Ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ naga nɩalɩŋ sɩ ta niiŋ Wɩa teeŋ,
ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ nagɛ nɩalɩŋ ma sɩɩ fá fawʋllʋŋ a bɩ ta lɛ.
3Wɩalɩŋ kala sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ a kɛŋ tʋɔ-cheeŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Wʋbala nɛ sɩ jaŋ kɛŋ la kala mʋ. Nuhuobiinee tʋɔŋ lɔrɔ kɩŋkɛŋ ba bɩbɩɩnɛ nyɩnyɛ wɩaa ba mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ ba sʋʋ. 4Nɩalɩŋ sɩ weye kɛŋ yɩɛlaa, a nagɛ va-weiŋ sɩ kpɩa naachigi-sʋʋŋ ŋɩɩ nɛ.
5Nɩalɩŋ sɩ weye jɩma dɩ ba jaŋ sʋʋ,
ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ sʋba-na bɩ wɩɩ jɩŋ.
Ba bɩra bɩ time kɛnɛ baa yɩɛlɛ,
nɩaa paala yʋ ba wɩaa nɛ.
6Ŋɩɩ ba sɩ cho nɩaa, ŋɩɩ ba sɩ bɛrɛ nɩaa
arɩ ba yarɩ-bieriŋ kala lɛlɛ nɛ.
Ba-na bɩra bɩ jaŋ pɛ
wɩɩ na-kala sɩɩ ŋaa dʋnɩa lɛ.
7Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, dii kɩaa arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ, a nyʋa kɩaa a nɩɩ sɩma, bɛɛ wɩaa Wɩa sɩ cho dɩ ŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la nɛ ŋɩɩ lɛɛlɛ. 8Ŋɩŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ tɔrɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ bʋa-kala lɛ. 9Leŋ ŋ dɩ ŋ haala sɩ cho nɩɩ sɩma ma mɩɩsɩŋ deeŋ sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ lɛ, tapʋlɩa-la kala Wɩa sɩ joŋo pɩ ma dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ. Má nɩɩ sɩma tapʋlɩa-la kala sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ toruŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ tɩma lɔl a na dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ. 10Tɩntɩmɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ, fɩɛsɛ sɩɩŋ a faasa tɩmʋ. Ʋ bɩ jaŋ dieni ka ŋ mʋ lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ, lee-la nɩaa sɩ bɩ tɩŋ, a bɩ wɩaa ka bɩɩnɛ, a bɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ kɛnɛ, a bɩ wɩaa sɩaa ma jɩŋ.
11Wɩɩ dɔŋ ma nɛ mɩ bɩra na dʋnɩa lɛ:
Naachɛ-lɩmɩŋ tɩɩna dee bɩ fá didii,
nɩduoŋ ma dee bɩ laalɩŋ yuo didii.
Wʋjɩnna dee bɩ kʋdiilee na didii bʋa-kala,
nɩɩ-la sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa sɩaa ma dee bɩ dʋa ka kɛŋ.
Nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ jɩma yie bɩ lere-la sɩ maga dɩ ba jomba hɛ ka na,
ama nyu-sɩmɩŋ ka puu nʋʋkala nɛ.
12Nʋʋkala bɩ ʋ sʋʋŋ tapʋlʋŋ jɩŋ.
Ʋ nagɛ jóŋ sɩ yie kɛŋ chenfiliŋ nɛ,
koo ba sɩ bɛrɛ kɛŋ diibie.
Ŋɩɩ nɛ wʋbɔmʋŋ bʋa ma nagɛ nuhuobiine lɛ,
ʋ yie guu jʋʋba dɩ ba bɩ yɩɛla.
Wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ kpɩa yaarɩŋ
13Wɩɩ dɔŋ ma nɛ mɩ bɩra na dʋnɩa lɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ wʋjɩmɩŋ lɛ ʋ sɩma pɩmɛ kɩŋkɛŋ. 14Tabie kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ, ʋ nɩaa bɩ yʋgɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoru-duo kʋbala sii kɔ dɩ ʋ yuou, a leŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo gollu chu a saa laalɩyuori vaŋkumba dɩ ba jʋʋ. 15Dɩ baal kʋbala ma hɛ taŋ-la lɛ a nyaabɛ aŋ jɩŋ wɩaa. Ʋ kɛŋ ʋ wʋjɩmɩɩ-la laa taŋ-la ta. Ama nʋʋkala bɩ nyaabʋ-la wɩaa liise. 16Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋl, “Wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ kpɩa doluŋ.” Ama nʋʋkala bɩ nyaabɩ-la wʋjɩmɩɩ-la joŋo dɩ ʋ ŋaa kʋŋ, ba bɩ wɩalɩŋ ma ʋ sɩ bʋla jegile nɩɩ.
17Dɩ ŋ nɛ jegile nɩɩ wʋjɩnna sɩ fɩɛla bʋl wɩɩŋ,
ʋ nɛ kpɩa nɩyaaraa kuoro sɩɩ kpɩa goŋ.
18Wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ kpɩa laalɩyuori kɩaa,
ama wʋbɔŋ ŋaarɩ bala yie chei wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ yʋgɛ nɛ.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Nanchʋɔsʋŋ sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ hɛ tʋlaalɩ lɛ dɩ ʋ sʋɔra lɔrɛ ŋɩɩ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ yaarɩŋ mʋa jaŋ wuo chei wʋjɩmɩŋ arɩ zile.
2Wʋjɩnna tʋɔbɩɩnaa yie kɛnʋ tʋʋlɛ nɛ ʋ ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ.
Ama nɩyaarɩŋ-na tʋɔbɩɩnaa kala nɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wʋlɔrʋŋ.
3Dɩ ʋ nɛ paala vɛŋ wombiiŋ lɛ,
ʋ yie ŋaa nɩyaarɩ wɩaa nɛ
a dagɛ nʋʋkala arɩ ʋ yaara nɛ.
4Dɩ ma kuoro nɛ na baanɩŋ ŋ nyuŋ,
sɩ́ ŋ dɩchɩnɩŋ vɩa.
Dɩ ŋ nɛ tɔrɛ ŋ niiŋ, ŋɩɩ jaŋ wuo leŋ dɩ wɩɩ-la fɩɛlɛ.
5Wʋbɔŋ nɛ mɩ na dʋnɩa lɛ,
kuoro sɩ ŋaa wɩaa piperigi:
6Ba sɩ joŋ nɩyaaraa hɛ dɩ-balaa
aŋ joŋ kɩaa tɩŋŋaa hɛ dɩ-biisiŋ.
7Mɩ na yosuŋ dɩ ba jɩl janɩŋ,
ka kuori biiriŋ vɩvɛŋ naasɩŋ lɛ a nagɛ yosi.
8Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ lu buotuoŋ jaŋ foro tuu,
nɩɩ-la ma kala sɩ yigi jeeŋ lo, dɩmɩŋ jaŋ dɩmʋ.
9Nɩɩ-la kala sɩɩ yɛrɛ tabɩaa, ba jaŋ wuo pɩrʋ.
Nɩɩ-kala sɩɩ yɛrɛ daasɩŋ, ba nɛ jaŋ wuo pɩrʋ.
10Dɩ ŋ saaŋ nɛ gbule
ka ŋ bɩ taa,
see dɩ ŋ faasa hɛ doluŋ ka dɩ ʋ-na wuo keri kʋa.
Ama wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ jaŋ wori wɩɩŋ.
11Dɩ dɩmɩŋ nɛ dɩmɩŋ, ka dɩ ŋ-na ŋaa dɩ ʋ bugumi,
nɩɩ-la sɩ bugumu bɩ nyʋʋrɩ kala na.
12Wʋjɩnna wʋbʋlaa yie leŋ ba zilu nɛ,
ama nɩyaarɩŋ-na wʋbʋlaa yie chei ʋ tɩtɩa nɛ.
13Nɩyaarɩŋ yie suomo bʋl wɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ nɛ,
ʋ dɩdɛrɩŋ ʋ bʋl wʋyaayasɩŋ.
14Nɩyaarɩŋ nɛ yie bʋbʋl wɩaa kɩŋkɛŋ.
Nʋʋkala bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa chie,
nʋʋkala bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa ʋ sʋʋŋ harɩŋ.
15Nɩyaarɩŋ yie tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa a bɛsɩmɛ nɛ,
ʋ paala bɩ dɩa wombiiŋ jɩŋ.
16Wɩɩŋ puu tintee-la nɩaa kuoro sɩ nagɛ ŋaa bii-bie,
ba sɩpaalaaraa ma ŋaa nɩaa sɩ yie sii chʋchʋɔ fɩɛla kala
dɩ ba niiŋ chɔgɩlɛ kʋdiile lɛ.
17Tintee-la nɩaa tʋɔŋ sɩ jaŋ tɔrɛ nɛ,
kuoru-bie sɩ dii ba kuoruŋ,
ba sɩpaalaaraa ma ŋaa nɩa sɩɩ dii kɩaa
bʋa-la sɩ maga dɩ ba dii lɛ a kɛŋ doluŋ,
a jɩma kɛŋ ba tɩtɩa a bɩ bugi.
18Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ yarɩwɩɩŋ a bɩ ʋ dɩa nyuŋ ka beŋ,
ʋ jaŋ chuori a tel.
19Kʋdiilee nɛ yie leŋ nɩa tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ,
kʋnyʋalaa ma leŋ nɩaa mʋmɔŋ,
ama moribiee nɛ kɛmba kala kʋkɔ.
20Pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ wʋbɔŋ bʋl a tɩgɛ kuoro lɛ,
koo a bʋl wʋbɔŋ a tɩgɛ kɩaa tɩɩna lɛ ŋ dɩpɩnɩŋ,
bɛɛ wɩaa diibie jaŋ wuo kɛŋ wɩalɩŋ mʋ bʋl.
Fillu dɔŋ ma jaŋ wuo mʋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ bʋla.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Nuhuobiine wʋjɩmɩŋ magɩsɩŋ
1Ŋaa ŋ kɩaa a kpaa,
tapʋlaa baŋmɛnɛ pɛgɛ ŋ jaŋ bɩra naba.
2Ŋaa kpaa nɩaa balɩpɛ, koo chori,
bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ bɩ jɩŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la wʋlɔrʋŋ sɩ jaŋ jʋʋ tinteeŋ.
3Dɩ duonuŋ nɛ tɩna dɛrɛ,
ʋ yie nɩɩ nɛ.
Sɛmɛ na-kala tɩa sɩ tele, nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ yie pɩŋ,
dɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ nɛ koo dɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa nɛ.
4Nʋʋ na-kala sɩ beŋ ŋɩɩ leriŋ sɩ naga
bɩ jaŋ wuo duu kʋŋ koo a kʋŋ kɩaa.
5Ŋ sɩ bɩ peliŋ wombiiŋ jɩŋ ŋɩɩ
koo ŋɩɩ ba sɩ mɛ nuhuobiine ʋ naaŋ luoruŋ tʋɔŋ,
ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo jɩŋ Wɩa wʋŋaalaa.
Wɩa nɛ ŋaa kʋŋkala.
6Duu ŋ kɩaa chʋchʋɔŋ,
dɩdaanɩŋ ma sɩ́ pɛɩ hɔŋ.
Ŋ bɩ jɩŋ ba kʋ-la sɩ jaŋ wasɛ,
dɩ dɔŋɔ nɛ jaŋ wasɛ a kɩɩ dɔŋɔ koo,
dɩ ba kala nɛ jaŋ wasɛ magɛ dɔŋɔ.
Liisi La Tɩɩna wɩaa ŋ hambiriŋ lɛ
7Ʋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ nɛ dɩ la na pʋlʋmʋŋ,
ʋ ŋaa tʋɔtɔrɛ wɩɩ nɛ dɩ la hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ.
8Jɩsɩŋ magɛ ŋɩɩ na-kala nuhuobiine sɩ hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ,
ʋ maga dɩ ʋ nɩɩ ba kala sɩma nɛ.
Ama ʋ maga dɩ ʋ liise yi ʋ sʋʋŋ tapʋlaa lɛ nɛ,
ba nɛ jaŋ dieni a kɩɩ ʋ sɩ weye.
Wɩɩkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ.
9Bapʋɔsɛ bie, leŋ dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ ŋ bapʋɔsʋŋ lɛ,
nɩɩ sɩma ŋ hambiriŋ lɛ.
Ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩɩ chɛ arɩ wɩɩ na-kala ŋ sɩ na,
ama jɩŋ dɩ wɩaa deemba kala ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa lɛ
Wɩa jaŋ diiŋ sarɩya.
10Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ wɩɩkala walɩmɩŋ,
wɩɩ-la kala sɩɩ wɩɩŋ, joŋo ta,
bɛɛ wɩaa hambiriŋ arɩ bapʋɔsɛ doluŋ bɩ dieni.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Ŋ bapʋɔsʋŋ lɛ,
liise yi Wɩa sɩ ŋaaŋ lɛ,
ka dɩ tapʋlɩɩ-la wɩaa sɩ jaŋ jʋʋŋ-na yi,
ka dɩ jɩsɩ-la sɩ jaŋ yi dɩ ŋ bʋl,
“Mɩ bɩ sɩma kala nɩa.”
2Liisi ʋ wɩaa ka dɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ pʋlʋmʋŋ, chɛnɛ
arɩ chɛnwʋlaa-na biri ŋ sɩaa lɛ,
dɩ duonuŋ nɩɩ aŋ ha nagɛ ʋ tɩna ŋ sɩaa lɛ.
3Ka dɩ ŋ nɩsaa sɩɩ pɔŋ-na chichel,
dɩ ŋ naasɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ daagɛ,
dɩ ŋ nyɩlaa ŋ sɩ kaa chaŋ kɩaa churi,
aŋ ka mʋa ŋ bɩra bɩ kɩaa wuo chaŋ,
dɩ ŋ sɩaa gʋɔlɛ a bɩra bɩ na woruŋ,
4dɩ ŋ dɩgɩlaa tɔ a bɩra bɩ goŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa wombiiŋ lɛ ka nɩɩ,
a bɩ ba sɩɩ nɔŋ kɩaa dɔmʋŋ ma ka nɩɩ,
kɩaa chɩɩrɩŋ jaŋ chɩsɩŋ doŋ lɛ
ama ŋ bɩ diibiisiŋ yele ka nɩɩ.
5Ŋ jaŋ fɩfá dundolluŋ jɩlɩŋ, dɩ ŋ vɛnɩŋ ŋaa wʋduo,
ŋ nyuŋ jaŋ pʋllɛ,
dɩ ŋ bɩra bɩ ŋ tɩtɩa wuo lɛrɛɛ vɛŋ,
dɩ ŋ kʋchooloo kala lɛl.
Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ nuhuobiine jaŋ mʋ ʋ dɩ-wiesiŋ,
dɩ nɩaa yiyel wombiee lɛ.
6Liisi Wɩa wɩaa ka dɩ ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ sɩ nagɛ hɔpʋla banzɔlɔ-na kɛrɛ,
dɩ ŋ sɛlɩmɛ chaanɩŋ tele yɛrɛ,
dɩ ŋ gʋʋga ŋmɛnɩŋ kɛrɛ,
dɩ ŋ lɩɩŋ pupoiŋ ma tele yɛrɛ muno muno.
7Ŋɩɩ nɛ nuhuobiine jaŋ bɩrɩmɛ hagɩla a gʋra jʋʋ tintee-la ba sɩ lɔgɔ mɛʋ,
ka ʋ wiese mɩɩra mʋ Wɩa teeŋ, nɩɩ-la sɩ joŋu hɛ ʋ lɛ.
8Wɩɩkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ, wɩɩkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ,
nɩɩ-la sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa a dɩdagɛ nɩaa nɛ bʋla:
Wɩɩkala bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ.
9Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ dagɛ nɩaa fa kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ nɛ woruŋ, a joŋ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ jɩma a dagɛ nɩaa. Ʋ chaasa hɔnɔ bɩɩnɛ wɩaa nɛ aŋ magɛ namagaba ba lɩɩ aŋ ka pɩ dɔŋɔ. 10Nɩɩ-la sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa a dɩdagɛ nɩaa hɛ ʋ doluŋ a walɩmɛ nɛ, dɩ ʋ dagɛ nɩaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba nyuŋ nyaasɛ. Wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋmʋnsa chɩŋ ba bʋa-la lɛ nɛ a ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩba.
11Wɩalɩŋ wʋjɩnna sɩ bʋla nagɛ daaŋ niiŋ sɩ ŋaa chʋla chʋla nɛ, kʋdaaraa kori a kaa daa pʋsʋŋ. Namagaba-la ba sɩ kaa hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ ka dienu a nagɛ ba sɩ joŋ hɛŋŋɛɛ ŋmoo hɛ kʋa lɛ ʋ chɩŋ kpaŋkpaŋ nɛ. Wɩa nɛ joŋo pɩla, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ daa la kala. 12Mɩ nanʋala, wɩɩ dɔŋ nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ mɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa arɩ wɩɩ-la:
Teniŋ ŋmʋnsʋŋ bɩ dɩdɛrɩ kɛnɛ, dɩ ŋ nɛ gʋnnɛ wɩaa ma kɩŋkɛŋ ŋɩɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ kɔsɛ.
13Wɩaa deemba kala dɩdɛrɩŋ,
wʋbala nɛ mɩ kɛŋ dɩ mɩ bʋl:
Fɩfá Wɩa a tuto wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ daga,
bɛɛ wɩaa ŋɩɩ wɩaa nɛ Wɩa ta nuhuobiine.
